## 2026-10-01 A running env saved as a start: two replays of its acts make the image and its twin; a curriculum of milestone starts in GRPO (lane/savestart)

Elliot, 2026-10-01: a curriculum "at different checkpoints of different seeds", the demo target a clip that reaches
iron. A start used to come only from a snapshot the Java oracle recorded. Now pool_start_from_env (pipeline.h
pipe_start_from_env, rlbind.h nwrl_start_save) makes one from a running env, so that an env reset to it continues
exactly as the saved env would have: the same rows and the same frames for the same acts.

Why replays: a reset copies a start's image and rebases its pointers, which a load names by loading the start twice
at two addresses (the twin). A running env has no twin, and telling pointers by value is unsafe (two ints packed in a
word whose high one is near 4,096 + 16 x the slot read as an address in the image window). So with
pool_config.save_slots each env keeps an act log since its reset (process memory, per step the ticks it ran, per tick
the act step_act made: an agent act after the act hook with its hold_only, a tape act or a row's text; about 100 bytes
a tick), and a save copies the log and queues two J_SAVE jobs: each resets a new image to the env's start and runs the
log through step_job itself (replay mode: no tick hook, no profiler, no shared generation cache, which would let one
replay take a chunk the other generates and part their heaps), with a view of its own (spare views n + 2k, n + 2k + 1
of save slot k). The two replays are the start's image and twin: start_scan names the image's pointers as for a load,
plus the words naming the view library's copy. The view (play's statics in its playview.so copy) is saved as its
written pages of the copy's writable segments (less RELRO), the words naming the copy or the image rebased; a reset to
a saved start loads a fresh copy without opening it, writes those pages, rebases, and resumes the view (mesh_resync:
the device forgot the env's meshes). Starts are refcounted with saves on (an env holds its start, a save its parent
until made); the save runs on the workers beside the steps, pool_start_ready/wait report it, a reset to it waits.
Words that differ between the two replays and point at neither are values of each run's own, kept from the first
replay and counted: the view's frame timings (raster_live stats), stack bytes in struct padding; three stale
pointers are cleared in both (the session's hook context, the tile pass's cos_table pointing into its caller's frame,
the shared path search's worker stamp).

The gate, make -C native/runtime rl-start-gate (start_gate.c, startgate.mk): per case env A steps S, is saved (X) and
steps M more; B reset to X, C reset to X then saved again halfway (Y, a save of a saved start), D reset to Y, and A
itself reset to Y: every tick's row record (tests/rowrec.h), every step's result and device frame (and with --draw the
C frame), and the end state must equal A's. Cases: configs/speedrun.yaml at 1 tick a step (walk:1@300+120,
sr-speedrun-s1@400+160) and 4 (walk:2@120+60, sr-speedrun-s1@100+40), device meshing and the HUD; recordings at the
default observation with C frames: chest-chain-s1@20+20 (a chest window open), death-drops-s1@29+40 (the game-over
screen, 73 entities, the drops in flight), cat-recipes-s1@42+30 (the crafting table, its grid filled, 49 entities),
cov-tradelist-s1@3+30 (a trade), fight-zombie-s1@60+40, nether-trip-s1@23+30 (through the portal), @100+40 (in the
Nether), @197+20 (back), end-dragon-s1@50+60: 13 of 13 PASS. Then the binding (mcsr-speedrun mcsr/nwrl_save_gate.py
through libnwrl.so): 100 steps of an env reset to a saved start and 50 of one reset to a save of it equal the saving
env's, every RESULT record field and every frame torch reads: PASS. Per start (start_gate's lines): image 47 to 93 MB
(the env's nonzero pages, 5,855 to 38,281 pointers, 9 into the view), the view's pages 0.18 to 0.45 MB, the region
spill file 0 to 1.7 MB; a save took 0.3 s (60 ticks replayed) to 3.5 s (788 ticks, the Nether), about 1.5 to 4.5 ms a
replayed tick, off the trainer's thread.

mcsr-speedrun (new: mcsr/rl/curriculum.py, mcsr/nwrl_save_gate.py; edited, the originals in data/savestart_backup/:
mcsr/runconf.py, scripts/nw_grpo_async.py): policy.curriculum in the run file (starts fresh|pool, seeds "1-17", fresh,
mix uniform|latest|name:weight, keep, max_starts). With seeds, nw_grpo_async makes one SaveEnv a seed (the pool holds
a start to its config's world.seed), dealt over the sim cards. During rollouts an env whose episode first holds a
milestone (reward.MILESTONES) is saved and filed under it, per seed, keep each (the oldest goes); each group's reset
draws its start (its seed's fresh one with probability fresh, else a milestone by mix and one of its made starts), so

(configs/speedrun-curriculum.yaml, bigA's policy, the full objective, 180-second episodes, 17 seeds x 8 worlds on

## 2026-10-01 The semantic camera, a 5.2M teacher trained by PPO on it in 1.5 h, and DAgger into the 181M pixel policy: 24.0 logs and 99.2% wooden pickaxes against the overnight run's 7.0 and 52.3% (lane/semteach)

Elliot, noon: build the fast tier inside v2 and try it on the GPU host. Four parts.

The camera. native/runtime/semcam.[ch]: after each step, per env, a 64x36 grid of rays from the client player's eye
(the renderer's camera: yOffset - 1.62, vertical fov 70, aspect W/H, the axes from MathHelper's sin table) walked cell
by cell through the client world's blocks to 64 blocks; each ray gives block id | meta << 12, the distance in 1/256
blocks, the face entered (or a miss, or the void). Unloaded chunks and missing sections read as air, the eye's own cell
is passed, and with the eye in water or lava the rays see through it. Read only (the chunk lookups fill the world's
near cache, nothing else). Two casts: semcam_cast_ref reads every cell through world_chunk and chunk_get_block,
semcam_cast (the runtime's) keeps the last cell's chunk and band and ends a rising ray once it is above every loaded
section in reach. Run-file keys (C, WorldConf.java, config.yaml): client.camera pixels | semantic | both,
client.semantic 64x36, client.semantic_range 64. semantic makes the pipeline run no view and no renderer (no_view);
both keeps the frames. pool.h gained step_hook (the worker, at a step's end); rlbind's nwrl_semantic exports the
casts as host memory [n][h][w][4] uint16; pipe_bench --semantic (or the config's camera). New configs:
configs/speedrun-semantic.yaml (camera semantic), configs/speedrun-dagger.yaml (both).

Gate: make -C native/runtime semcam-gate (pool_gate --semcam): sr-speedrun-s1, swim-s42, phys-lavaswim-s1,
nether-trip-s1, end-dragon-s1 and cov-villagerep-s42, each run twice, the cast after every tick both ways: 15,830
casts byte-equal, each recording's episodes give one digest, and every row still equals test_snapshots'. Fast cast
0.08 (village) to 0.82 ms (the End: open sky), 0.17 ms on the speedrun start; the reference 0.12 to 1.24 ms.

Throughput (pipe_bench corpus, the GPU host timing cores 0-31, 32 workers, one run each on a loaded machine;
out/perf/semteach.tsv): 1 tick a step, camera on / off: 256 worlds 35,363 / 43,117 env-steps/s, 512 34,193 / 41,330,
1,024 32,463 / 36,601. 4 ticks a step: 70,053 / 76,439 ticks/s, 75,581 / 91,300, 82,866 / 79,060 (the last pair is
noise). The cast is 0.14 to 0.17 ms of a worker's thread against a host step of 0.89 to 0.98 ms at 1 tick. Workers
99 to 100% busy in every run: the CPU tick is the wall. perf at 512 worlds, 1 tick: ticks_chunk_updates 13.2%,
the cast 10.8%, the kernel 6.3%, entity_move_memo 4.5%.

The teacher (mcsr-speedrun mcsr/rl/semteach.py Teacher, 5.2M parameters: a block embedding, the face and the
distance through three convolutions, the inventory's counts of 32 speedrun items, the hotbar, health, food, air and
the previous action beside them; the student's 14 keys and 41-bin camera as heads). scripts/semteach_ppo.py: PPO
from scratch (a calm camera and forward-held starting bias), 512 worlds of configs/speedrun-semantic.yaml, the
overnight run's game (180 s episodes, the full objective, the macros, attack press), the update on a learner thread
beside the loop, card 0 shared with other lanes. Per batch of 512 episodes (data/semteach/ppoA): the untrained start
3.53 logs, 39.1% wooden pickaxe, return 9.08 (the macros and the bias); 7 min 8.75 / 77.5% / 18.9 (past the
overnight run's final row: 7.10 / 54.6% / 11.6 after 6.1 h of iterations and 531M env-steps); 32 min 27.7 / 99.2% /
45.0; 1.5 h (63M env-steps, 9 to 15k env-steps/s) 32.0 / 100% / 51.4. It stopped mining stone (stone pickaxe 14% at
the start, 0% from 30 min): logs pay more under the full objective.

DAgger (scripts/semteach_dagger.py, data/semteach/daggerA): configs/speedrun-dagger.yaml, 256 worlds, the
imitation checkpoint (fast-D-s20000.pt, version edit) acting on its frames, the 1.0 h teacher labelling every step
from the cast of the same step; after each round the student's temporal core and heads learn the teacher's
distributions (soft cross-entropy on both camera axes, BCE on the live keys) over the last 3 rounds, lr 5e-5, the
rollout's block-aligned windows. Sim on card 1, student, teacher and learner on card 2, 7 to 10k env-steps/s, 2.3 to
3 min a round. Round 0 (the imitation policy) 2.79 logs, 9.0%; rounds 1 and 2 collapsed (0.12 and 0.26 logs: the
student took the teacher's walking before its targeted attacks); round 4 9.73 / 69.1%; round 9 24.7 / 99.6%; rounds
9 to 13 flat. 14 rounds, 37 min, 12.9M env-steps.

Closed loop, scripts/nw_eval.py, configs/speedrun.yaml, 128 worlds x 180 s, the same harness for each:
imitation 2.86 logs, 10.2% wooden pickaxe, 0% stone, return 4.51; bigA's final policy.pt 7.04, 52.3%, 1.6%, 11.48;
the DAgger student 24.03, 99.2%, 0%, 39.84 (every episode with a log, no deaths). Teacher and student together took
2.1 h of wall and 76M env-steps against the overnight run's 7.4 h and 531M.

casting every fp32 weight to bf16 in every step, the same at any batch: 900 MB of temporal weights read and written),
decode attention 1.5, conv blocks 1.2, GEMMs 1.0. B 1,024 18.0 ms: attention 6.1 (bound by the K/V bytes: 1.6 TB/s),
conv blocks 4.2 plus GroupNorm and cuDNN 1.9, copies 2.7, GEMMs 2.7. The decode kernel alone on a quiet card, 12 layers:
bf16 0.39 / 1.46 / 5.99 ms at B 62 / 248 / 1,024 (1.53-1.61 TB/s); int8 0.23 / 0.79 / 3.19. A split-K (flash
decoding) form gains nothing at any batch.

The variants (mcsr.polfast): lean, a bf16 shadow of the model made once (shared by a card's steppers, refreshed in
place after each weight sync) and the conv blocks' filters packed once; attn=fused, the new K/V written by the decode
kernel; kv=int8, the cache in int8 with an fp16 scale per slot and head (6.7 MB an env instead of 12.6); enc8, the
conv blocks on kernels/fp8conv's e4m3 kernels with static scales calibrated on recorded frames (enc8=256/512: stages
3 and 4 only); fp8=enc_out, kvstep's FP8 output projection; obs=128x72, the frame downsampled 2x2 on the card, the
encoder's last 3x4 map resized into the projection, its weights distilled from the 256x144 encoder.

phase-profile over 4,033 rows), 41.8k/s on one thread. 48 worlds is the most that fits: 312.5 MB of device memory a
world (148 real 2 MB granules for 62.9 MB of nonzero image; explore-long-s1 337.6 MB, 82.6 MB). 0.4% of S6 runs come

the rows that copy, because NVPTX makes every memcpy and memset of 128 bytes or more a byte loop.

The three structural costs: (1) the hybrid's round trip: 5.27 MB down (1,288 pages) and 0.34 MB up a world-row, and
The dev host's 3090 sits on PCIe 3.0 x8: a batched pinned upload of 32 worlds moved 256 MB in 32.5 ms, 7.9 GB/s, the link's
peak, so a hybrid S6 tops out near 1.5k world-rows/s whatever the batch; (2) device memory: 312 MB a world, 48 to 60

## 2026-10-01 The raster walks each pixel's own triangles, the generic write fills its warps: raster -14%, clipped write -20%, speedrun env-steps/s +5 to +7% on the dev host (lane/clipclimb)

Elliot, 2026-10-01: "hillclimbing gpu kernels further to get runs done quicker". The two render kernels lane/simclimb
named, profiled with Nsight Compute (ncuwrap.sh) on 161 stored sr-speedrun-s1 frames at 256x144 (render_check
--one-trip --bench 32, 32 frames a render; master 1a9323c4 and the lane in one session):
- generic, the clipped units' write: 322 us, 217 registers, 7.2 of 32 lanes active, 1.7 warps a scheduler, 78% of its
  stalls on local memory (clip_triangle's two 9-vertex arrays of whole vertices, copied each plane; 150 MB of DRAM a
  launch). Bound by latency: few warps, each lane a long serial chain through local memory, and most lanes idle
  because 78% of the list's units had no triangle to write.
- raster: 1,277 us, 80 registers (6 blocks an SM), issue-bound at 11.4 of 32 lanes: the warp visited one triangle at a
  time and only the lanes it covered ran the pixel function (6 lanes), and cover_mask (a lane a triangle, its box's
  pixels) ran at 3.5 to 5 lanes.

Kept, every frame bit-exact:
- The generic write gathers the units with a triangle (ballot, a shared queue of 64) and writes them 32 a warp, on a
  grid of 4 blocks an SM (328 on the 3090; swept 1 to 12): the clipped write 322 to 255 us, the sky's and recorded
  units' 81 to 58 us.
- The raster stages up to 8 of a batch's visited triangles in shared memory (cp.async) and each lane walks the ones
  that may cover its own pixel, in order: a pixel's triangles are drawn in the order they were, and every pixel
  function reads and writes its own pixel alone, so no byte moves. 6 blocks an SM hold it at 80 registers. 1,277 to
  1,100 us (480.8 to 379.1 M warp instructions, 13.8 lanes active, DRAM 592 to 537 MB).
- Both clippers read the first plane that cuts from their input instead of copying it into the polygon array: the
  counts 39 to 28 us (sky and recorded) and 105 to 98 us (clipped).

Tried and not kept (out/perf/clipclimb.tsv): polygons as 4-bit vertex ids with each vertex made once (255 registers,
394 us); the write split into a vertex-path and a recorded-path kernel (the vertex path alone needs 226 registers;
with a register cap it spills); cover masks a pixel a lane by ballot (fewer instructions, but a serial head load per
candidate: 1.30 ms, or 1.64 ms with the heads shuffled); no staging, lanes reading their triangles through L1 (1.13
ms); other group sizes, block sizes and COVER_TEST_MAX values.

## 2026-10-01 One process makes 1,024 envs: the image window is 1,088 slots of 64 GB (lane/imgwin)

The big GRPO run on the GPU host failed at 744 worlds: `nwrl_make: pipe_make: env 139: no image (the address window holds
139)` on its second sim card after 372 on the first. image.c's window was 512 slots of 128 GB from 16 TB, and an
image is 38.55 GB of address (image_bytes measured: struct env 29,160,896 bytes, the arena 7,001,902,464, the heap
32 GB), so half of every slot was never used. The window now has IMG_SLOT 64 GB (1 << 36, 1.66x an image) and
IMG_SLOTS 1,088: 16 TB to 84 TB, below the lowest a PIE program loads (0x555555554000, about 85.3 TB; CUDA maps near
8 GB and 1 TB). The pool takes an image per env, two per start and one per generation thread, so 1,024 envs fit with
slots to spare; image_owner is still one compare. IMG_WINDOW, IMG_SLOT and IMG_SLOTS moved from image.c to image.h,
and cuda/tick/host.c's device child unmaps IMG_WINDOW for IMG_SLOT x IMG_SLOTS: its own copy (S6_WINDOW_LEN, 128
slots of 128 GB) had gone stale when the window grew to 512 slots.

Evidence (the dev host): pipe_bench --config configs/speedrun.yaml --ns 1024 --no-view --device-mesh 0 --warm 2 --steps 10
makes and steps all 1,024 envs (rc 0, trajectory digest ebbdffa9, peak RSS 43.8 GB, 43 MB an env; run under
memslot.sh with a 48 GB reservation and oom_score_adj 1000); master on the same command: `FAIL speedrun N 1024: env
512: no image (the address window holds 512)`. 1,024 views do not fit the 3090 (37 MB of device memory an env), hence
--no-view; the window does not depend on the view. At 128 envs with views (100+200 steps) the trajectory digest is
adff53b75d22a783 on the lane and on master. rl-gate's pipe_bench half ff81b5bb / 23cd81c7 (its Python half needs

## 2026-10-01 The inventory at the action level: an action compiler in the binding (move, item, recipe, masks, click interval), three pointer heads 16/16 by DAgger, the recipe head against the macros in GRPO, the screen layer on threads (lane/guiact)

Elliot, 2026-09-30 11 pm: "lets add support, test, and include these in the yaml". native/runtime/rlact.[ch] is an
action compiler beside rlgui.c. A policy's higher-level screen actions ride in nwrl_act.ops beside pool.h's own:

- NWRL_OP_MOVE moves all, half or one of a stack from a slot (or an item kind: item_select) to a slot (or "a stack
  of it with room, else an empty slot on the other side").
- NWRL_OP_CRAFT crafts recipe R n times, from what the open 2x2, table or furnace can make.

They become the clicks a person makes, one op a tick at least click_interval ticks apart, queued across steps. Each
is planned against the client's screen as it is that tick. The player half comes from the client's own stacks:
survival.c refreshes the container's copy only at a click, so pool.c's fill_hud now reads them too (lane/invact's
head saw an empty inventory screen until its first click). The masks (mask_close_grid, mask_noop_clicks) refuse
ops, and nwrl_act_info exports them, with each recipe's craftable count, as the heads' valid-action masks.

The compiler runs in the pool's act hook. Lane/moveact's compiler and this one chain in rlbind.c's hook (moveact's
first, then this one on the act it leaves). With every key at its default the hook leaves the act alone.
sim.actions' click_interval to recipes come from the config (nwrl_make_ex). worldconf_unimplemented now refuses
nothing. mcsr's runconf takes gui_pointer move|item|recipe, gui_decide and ops_per_step (up to 8). nw_grpo.py and
nw_grpo_async.py run the head from a run file (mcsr.rl.guirollout.check_run, GuiRunner, AsyncGuiRunner).

## 2026-10-01 The big GRPO run's SIGSEGV: a pool worker's collision list kept another env's slab block (lane/slabfix)

Elliot's 10-hour RL goal: bigA (496 worlds, 180 s episodes, nw_grpo_async) died of SIGSEGV in iteration 15's rollout
twice (a general protection fault in slab_alloc's memcpy of a free block's chain link: native/src/arena.c), then on seed
2 around iteration 17 inside python3.12 itself. Cause: a pool worker has one scratch for every env it steps
(env.h nw_thread_scratch, runtime/pool.c worker_main), and collide.c's scratch collision list, once a sweep passed its
own 512 boxes, moved to a slab block of the env it was stepping and kept that block "for its next query". Every later
collision query on that worker, any env's, then wrote its AABBs into the first env's image. Once that env was reset,
those bytes were its slab's again (free blocks and their links, live lists): a double as a chain link is a
non-canonical address (the fault), a small one hands out a block twice and the corruption spreads (the Python crash).
test_snapshots runs each env on its own scratch, so no recording could see it; 60-second runs rarely grow a list.
Fix: collide_scratch_end gives a grown block back to the env that grew it and the list starts in its own room again
(nothing in a worker's scratch outlives its call; AGENTS.md's allocation rule says so now).

Evidence. native/tests/scratch_check.c (make -C native scratch-check, in make test and make smoke): two image envs on
one thread scratch, env a's list grown, then env b's queries; before the fix it fails ("env b's collision list writes
into env a's image", "env b's slab chains name a block outside its slab"; the check build aborts with "free of
-137438953408 outside the slab"), after it passes. The trained policy, update 9's weights from the repro checkpoint,
resumed at 128 worlds on card 2 (180 s, seed 1, same rollout seeds as bigA's envs 0 to 127): with a probe library on
the old code, rollout 14 grew one env's list 512 to 4096 boxes, and another env on the same worker then took the list
with its block still in the first env's image (40 times before the probe's cap); with the fixed library the same
growth happens at the same point (iterations 10 to 16 equal to the old run's in every logged field) and no env ever
takes another's block; it ran through iterations 15 and 16 (the old code had not crashed by 16 either at 128 worlds:
the corruption lands in whatever the owner env puts there next). Only 2 of the ~860 recordings ever grow a list (cauldron-slime-s1, pf-dragonwall-g9).

The search: arena.c has a check build now (cc -DSLAB_CHECK: every block a class larger with a header, poisoned while
free, a red zone, the sites that took and gave it; a write after free, a double free, a free with another class's
size or outside the slab stops the program naming the sites). The whole suite under it: clean but the four retired
recordings; pipe_bench speedrun 32 envs x 3700 steps and the trained policy at 64 worlds, iterations 10 to 13: clean
(no list grew in them).

Gates: scratch_check; smoke 254/254; clangcheck ok (and arena.c with -DSLAB_CHECK under clang); in a fresh worktree of
the merged branch, rl-gate PASS (ff81b5bb/23cd81c7), pipe-gate default 29 recordings 23,987 rows and 6,008 frames
bit-exact, pipe-gate CONFIG=configs/speedrun.yaml PRECS=sr-speedrun-s1 MESH=2 129,056 rows, 32,288 frames, device
meshes all equal; make test: only the four retired recordings fail (combat-pig-s1, replay2-*), as on the GPU host's master.
Not done: the repro itself at 496 worlds through iteration 15 (cards 0, 1 and 3 are the big run's; card 2 had room for
128 worlds). The lane's own out/native device objects were stale (rl-gate's pipe_bench frame digest eabf122f, pipe-gate
MESH=2 2,656 of 3,904 meshes equal); a fresh worktree builds them right.

## 2026-10-01 Where a world's memory goes, and a third of the host's and a fifth of the device's gone: 224 to 256 worlds on the 3090, env-steps/s the same (lane/heapprof)

Elliot, 12:30 am: remove the bottleneck "by profiling memory and where its going in the heap". Measured on the dev host
(3090, co-tenants holding about 4 GB of it) with configs/speedrun.yaml (256x144, normal, render distance 4, device
meshing) and pipe_bench at 32, 64, 128 and 256 envs. Tools in out/perf/heapprof: census.patch (a temporary image-heap
census: every block tagged with its call stack, symbolized by sym.py, removed by lane/cport on 2026-10-01 with smaps.py below; their results stay in out/perf/heapprof), cudahook.c (an LD_PRELOAD of cudaMalloc and
cudaHostAlloc by call stack, versioned as libcudart.so.13's), devmem.sh (nvidia-smi's device memory and the RSS of the
process, sampled), smaps.py (RSS by mapping), shmem.sh (the view copies' memory files).

Where it went at 128 envs on master (per env unless said): host 95 MB, of it the env's image 82 MB (heap 51, chunk
bands and nibbles 16, the list slab 10, chunks 2, livings and their AI parts 3) and each view's playview.so copy 4 MB
of shared memory (a memfd: in the cgroup, not in RSS); per process 0.9 GB (the start image, libc's arenas, pinned
staging, the driver). The heap's 51 MB: the start's parsed snapshot that every env image copies (each entity's runtime
JSON trees: 164k blocks, about 15 MB), the view's frames (22: the device mesher's band shadows 6, texture copies 6,
recording arrays), the views' block tables loaded twice (9), the session (7). Device 100 MB an env: the mesh arena
(the meshes, about 22 MB an env, grown by half and copied), the mesher's band pools (7.7), and per stream (4 at 128
envs) a 512 MB texture pool, 328 MB of mesher lane buffers, the triangle arena (grows only with 1 GB to spare) and the
reset burst's per-request arrays.

Cut, one change a commit, each gated (host image per env at 32 envs, t=30 s; device peak at 128 envs):
- rbshare.c: the block renderer's table.bin and atlas one read-only copy a process (as itemtab.c): image 78.7 to 69.9 MB.
- pool starts: snapshot_drop_runtime frees what only the session's open reads (the entities' rt and trk_rt trees, the
  client's entities) on a start that is not a dev one, and image_heap_trim hands back the whole pages under runs of free
  heap blocks so the env copies do not carry them: 69.9 to 55.2 MB (the drop alone 67.8).
- meshfeed: a band slot's shadow is a 64-bit hash a 64-byte granule (1,544 bytes a slot, not 12,320): 55.2 to 50.0 MB;
  the feeds the same bytes.
- render: the texture pool's floor 64 MB a stream (the item atlas's clock and compass versions fill any size): device
  12,722 to 11,050 MB, textures 15.1 to 18.0 KB an env-step.
- render: the mesh arena on reserved device addresses mapped 64 MB at a time (cuMemCreate, cuMemMap): no copy, no
  second arena while it grows: 11,050 to 10,374 MB.
- view: a copy's memfd without the library's debug sections (a hole after the loaded segments): 3.97 to 0.86 MB a copy.
- raster_obs: a new texture copy takes the unused buffer that fits it best (512 KB buffers stayed on entries holding
  8 KB skins): 50.0 to 46.5 MB.
- meshing: the per-request device arrays sized by the requests, not twice them: 10,374 to 10,152 MB.

## 2026-10-01 Moving, mining and looking at the action level: the engine's action compiler (hold_attack, look_target), action repeat, measured closed loop and under GRPO (lane/moveact)

Elliot, 2026-09-30 11 pm: "lets add support, test, and include these in the yaml". The policy acts at 20 Hz with 14 keys
and a 41-bin mu-law camera (mcsr/rl/actmap.py), with lane/rlbind's swim-up and mine-lock macros.

The compiler (native/runtime/moveact.[ch]) runs on the pool's worker before each tick (a new pool.h act_hook, three
lines in pool.c), so a step of several ticks compiles each tick against what that tick sees. hold_attack: an attack
press holds the key until the block it was pressed on changes in the client world, the crosshair leaves it, a screen
opens or a release command comes; a press on an entity or on nothing is one click. look_target: a frame point
(u, v) becomes a turn over look_ticks ticks of whole mouse counts at the sensitivity's step (0.15 degrees at 0.5),
recomputed each tick from where the camera is, the point's direction from the frame's projection (fov option times
the movement multiplier, 60/70 under water, the frame's aspect). Everything it emits is agent-form input (holds,
presses, dlook). The binding's side is native/runtime/rlmove.[ch] (nwrl_move, nwrl_move_state, nwrl_move_stats,
nwrl_move_script; rlbind.c gains four hook lines); nwrl_make takes sim.actions hold_attack, look_target and
look_ticks from the config, and wconf_unimplemented no longer refuses them (worldconf_check holds that). With both
off, or on with no command, the acts run unchanged.

Gate: make -C native/runtime rl-move-gate. moveact_gate drives one env from sr-speedrun-s1 with a seeded stand-in
policy and writes the compiled ticks as a Java script (java/tests/moveact-{hold,look,tps4}-s1.jsonl, moveact.list);

Elliot, 9 pm: "change this to be more like pufferlib with clever overlapping and the barrier between sim step and

mcsr-speedrun's new mcsr/rl/arollout.py: AsyncRunner keeps G groups (2 to 16) in flight; when a group's results
are in, its frames go from the render card's buffer to the policy card by one peer copy on the group's own CUDA
stream, and the whole step (seeded uniforms, the KV-cached core, the record writes, the log-probability, the packed
actions to a pinned buffer) is one CUDA graph followed by an event; the loop harvests a group when its event has
fired, runs the reward while the step is on the card and the macros at harvest. Sampling is a hash of (seed, env,
step, index), so actions do not depend on which group ran first. scripts/nw_async_check.py runs rollout.Runner (the
synchronous loop, uniforms set the same way) and AsyncRunner on the same envs: acts, frame embeddings, camera bins,
keys, log-probabilities, loss mask, rewards and episodes digest-equal (ASYNC-CHECK PASS at 32 envs and 64 envs, 4
groups, 2 sim cards, 1 and 2 policy cards, 300 steps, across a KV-cache shift).

Three things held the loop back, found by measuring it:
- nwrl_poll(n) waits until every env in flight on the card is done, so a card's groups came back together. New
  pipe_poll_some / nwrl_poll_some (min ready, then everything ready); pipe_poll(b) is pipe_poll_some(b, b).
- rlbind's 0.24 GB a world: raster_hand_item_lookup parsed the 11 MB item_table.json into each env's own heap (2.5
  million blocks, ~120 MB an env) the first time its player held an item, again after every reset (a 300-step replay
  of the policy's acts: +113.5 MB an env, heap blocks 166k to 1.09M; attack-only acts reproduce it without torch).
  native/src/itemtab.c keeps one converted table a process (an engine file, so every view copy shares it; built
  under a lock with the env heap off); 291,171 lookups compared with the jval lookup, 0 differ. The same replay: +38.8
  MB an env, blocks flat; 128 worlds with the policy 33.5 to 14.9 GB, 496 worlds 46 GB.
- numpy: concatenating the nested result dtype promoted every field (a third of the loop's time at 256 worlds); a
  group's results now land by index in a preallocated buffer.
New binding calls: nwrl_poll_some, nwrl_stats_ext (the pipeline's latencies), nwrl_env_mem (envmem by owner).

call netherite.oracle or say oracle), 9 comments of ours, 35 lines of our oracle methods written in vanilla's idiom
(RenderGlobal's oracleSyncForCamera and three more, GuiIngame.oracleTickVignette, KeyBinding's accessors), and 18
vanilla lines with an edit in them (a class line without an interface, the Minecraft constructor and its call
without removed parameters, the key and option arrays without the stream keys, ServerConfigurationManager without
the demo branch).

rollout computed it: log-probabilities 0.0014 mean, 0.046 max apart, ratio 1.000. Placement: an update on 128 x

process (a poller thread a pipeline; two pipelines coexist) and a Stepper per group on its policy card.

## 2026-09-30 the GPU host split between the simulator and mcsr's policy: two render cards and two policy cards, 41.7k env-steps/s at 20 Hz; the policy KV-cached, 56k frames/s a card (lane/rlsplit)

The policy's step (out/policy, mcsr-speedrun imported read only; PORT.txt says what to port there): kvstep.py (removed by lane/cport on 2026-10-01; PORT.txt and this entry keep what it measured)
is a KV-cached, batched single step of the adopted fast-D 181M policy. It converts RGB to yuv420p on the card
(bit for bit policy_server's conversion), encodes only the newest frame (the stem as one GEMM over its tubelet
patches), and runs one temporal token per env against that env's cached K and V (12.6 MB an env). The context
is block aligned (T 256, S 128): when a context is full, its oldest 128 frames are dropped and the kept 128
recomputed, so every step equals the full-sequence forward over its window. policy_server's sliding window
cannot be cached exactly. check.py compares every (env, step) with model.encode over the whole episode plus
model.temporal over the window, in bf16 and fp32: 24 envs x 700 steps, 16,800 outputs (6,749 after a shift),
error against fp32 0.159 max / 0.0060 mean against the bf16 full forward's own 0.598 / 0.0079, camera and key

the references hooked by vp_hook.attach; the edit moves the logits 0.22 mean, so the check is not vacuous) and
with FP8 on the encoder's output projection. FP8 on the temporal core's MLP, attention projections or every
linear FAILS (3-4x the mean error, 98.6-99.0% camera agreement). Frames/s on one card, compiled pieces plus CUDA
graphs, steady state: 24.5k / 34.8k / 44.5k / 51.0k / 55.6k at B 64 / 128 / 256 / 512 / 1,024 (eager 14.2k to

## 2026-09-30 Device generation on the full machine: it wins exploring once rendering goes first; a generation server and cross-card layouts measured (lane/gpuspec)

Elliot, 9 am: "gpu gen shouldnt [lose] since we have 4 of them". lane/genlight had device generation
+3.5% at 64 exploring worlds and -37.1% at 128 on four processes. Measured on the GPU host with one process per
card (out/perf/gpuspec/fn.sh, fullnode.sh's shape; corpus mode, trajectory digests equal to the host
path's in every run), then moved to the dev host at 3:05 pm for the gates.

Why it lost (nsys on one process of four, out/perf/gpuspec/nsys/{r1,m4}-*.sqlite, rounds.py, tlcmp.py):
the round is not on the tick's path. The prediction serves every generation (C generated 0 to 2 of 255k
in a run), steps wait on a round 0.02 to 0.04 times an env-step (3 to 15 ms a wait, about 0.2 ms an
env-step), a round at 64 worlds a process is 4.6 ms of generation thread (median; p90 8.1), 3.3 ms of
device span and 2.5 ms of kernels, 88 us from its start to its first kernel, and 1.3 ms of host copy of
its results (20.5 GB device to host in a 25 s run). The cost is the card: sharing it, the renderer's
kernels ran 25 to 42% longer (mesh_draw 268 to 379 us, raster 123 to 147 us) and the host's render
stages waited longer (read back offsets 223 to 528 us); where the card was also busy with another
project's job, a high-priority generation stream took the render wall from 5.3 to 10.9 ms an env-step
(m4 process 0). The host saves less than the instructions say: 64 to 38 M instructions an env-step but
cycles 39 to 31 M (the noise math it removes was the high-IPC work; what is left is memory-bound). A
round is tiny (5.2 chunks an env-step a process) and the density kernels have a latency floor
(worldgen_bench --seeds: 7.1 ms at 40 chunks, 17.1 at 1024). genlight's -37.1% did not reproduce: on
the two-DIMM machine before 1:29 pm with three cards held by a co-tenant (r1) device generation already
won (host 3,851, same card 5,428).

Built: native/runtime/gensrv.[ch], a generation server (one process's generators take every process's
rounds over a Unix socket, a memfd per client that the client's pool uses as its round buffers, batches
merged across clients; pipe_bench --gen-serve PATH / --gen-client PATH, pipe_gate --gen-serve, GEN=srv);
--gen-prio (stream priority), --gen-nowait (a step never waits for its round), --gen-ahead R (prediction
R rings wider, genahead_set_ahead), --gen-threads T; worldgen_bench --seeds S --per P; configs/explore.yaml
(the exploring world with device generation and meshing on). The pipeline's generation stream is now at
the card's lowest priority by default (pipeline.h gen_high; --gen-prio high for the old).

Full machine, env-steps/s (out/perf/gpuspec.tsv; after the reboot, other lanes' agents running, GPU 0 or
3 sometimes held by a co-tenant; host is the mean of the runs before and after):

| config | worlds | host | same card | low prio | server on GPU 2 | next card |

| explore (m4) | 64 | 6,424 | 7,717 (+20%) | | | |
| explore (m3) | 64 | 5,984 | 7,240 (+21%) | | 6,842 (+14%) | |
| explore (m4) | 128 | 8,774 | 9,031 (+3%) | 10,113 (+15%) | 9,405 (+7%) | |

The server loses to generation on each process's own card: its card is the hot one (74% busy against
53%) and it only moves the same work; merging four processes' rounds does not pay while the prediction
already hides the round. The next card specializes nothing (each card still generates for one process
and renders for another). --gen-nowait with --gen-ahead 1 made C generate what the wider ring missed
(53.5 M instructions against 37.7; +1%). The headline world generates 0.00 chunks an env-step: device
generation has nothing to do there and costs its thread. Defaults: configs/explore.yaml keeps
device_generation on, headline.yaml and config.yaml keep it off; the stream is low priority.

Elliot, 1 pm: look for other bytes every step carries without a reason, after struct living. pahole on
every object, IBS op sampling mapped to struct fields (the GPU host, headline config, 64 worlds a process) and the
per-env resident census (image_census_dump) sorted the big per-world structs into scratch, per-seed tables,
dense mostly-zero arrays and strings. The table is out/perf/coldaudit.tsv; the tools (structs.py,
members.py, ibs.sh, cafields.py, ab.sh, full.sh) are in out/perf/coldaudit (the .py ones removed by lane/cport on 2026-10-01; the table stays).

What a step reads is not where the bytes are. At 64 worlds the DRAM fills an env-step go to the livings
(29%) and their AI parts (9%: lane/villscale's), chunk bands (18%), the tracker (7%), the views (7%) and
chunks (6%); struct world takes 0.6%, struct env 0.8%, the session 2.6%. The big named arrays are mostly
only memory: surv_stats (132 KB of stat counters) is 87 KB resident and in no sampled field's fills,
s0d_ids (64 KB) 4 KB resident, the Nether and End providers (398 KB) are already built on first use.

Changed (rows, frames and trajectory digests the same): struct env_scratch holds what a call fills and
drains (World.lightUpdateBlockList, 128 KB, out of struct world; the light and path memos under their
stamps; the envstack), and a pool worker steps every env on its own copy (nw_thread_scratch), so a worker
stepping 16 worlds walks one hot copy instead of 16 cold ones; world_gen builds the overworld provider at
its first use (world_init built about 200 KB of tables per world); struct client_entity loses its unread

mesher vertex buffer full") failed their live replays (play_check.sh +live) in lane/s6lz and in

three. All three are dev tapes, so play_check runs out/native/play-dev, and the canonical tree's
play-dev was built 2026-09-29 at 9:45 am, before lane/playarena's grave and mesh buffer fixes merged
at 10:06 am: automerge.sh and trainmerge.sh rebuild `make -C native` and `play` after a merge, never
play-dev (nor libframedev.so and the device programs, also from 2026-09-29). `make lane` (02f7b342,
b0e1a055, 2026-09-28) copied out/native into the new lane and touched every copy newer than the
lane's fresh sources, so no lane's make ever rebuilt it: the lane's play (md5 686e4658) matched a
fresh build, its play-dev (cc94f023) did not (fresh ed0fdcba), and rebuilding only that file cleared

The fix, in the root Makefile: make lane still copies the builds with `cp -a` (their own times),
and gives the lane's tracked java/ and native/ files the canonical checkout's times

and rebuilt nothing current, and in a scratch copy of the canonical tree `make play-dev` rebuilt
the stale one to ed0fdcba while `all` and `play` had nothing to do. This lane got the same times
and a rebuilt play-dev. Evidence: the three play checks PASS with 0 mismatches (1001, 3001 and 308
rows) and their live replays reach rows 1018, 3018 and 325; every play check run fresh over all
849 snapshot recordings, 849 of 849 rc 0; the suite with PLAYCHECK=all, no FAIL (3,666 of 3,832

(playfix-staleplaydev, area other, fixed). Follow-up for the merge scripts: build play-dev (and the

## 2026-09-30 The S6 host build keys the region cache by its own build hash (lane/s6lz)

The batch gate on master 922059e9 (4:53 am) failed gpu-tick-check, 731 of 849: all 118 failures
were the C trace by the S6 host build (out/native/cuda/tick/test_snapshots), stopping at once with
"chunk: a packed chunk (X,Z) does not decompress". Not the codec: tests/lzpack_check.c linked
against the S6 build's own host/lzpack.o passes (7,986 round trips), and the same binary with
--region-cache off replays fall-s42 whole. The cause was the key: native/Makefile compiles
regioncache.o with -DREGIONCACHE_BUILD (RC_BUILD, the hash of every source, the flags and the
compiler), but cuda/tick/tick.mk's pattern rule did not, so every S6 build keyed its seed-world
images by the string "unknown" and read whatever an earlier S6 build stored under the same seed
and config. Before lane/spillfast those were the same bytes by luck of an unchanged format; after
it, a zlib-era image's packed chunks went to lzp_decompress, which refused them. A recording
passed only where no older S6 run had stored an image for its world.

The fix, in tick.mk: $(OUT)/cuda/tick/host/regioncache.o has its own rule with
-DREGIONCACHE_BUILD from a stamp (host/regioncache.build, rewritten only when the hash changes),
the hash of src/*.c, src/*.h, cuda/tick/nwpass.cpp, the S6 host flags and the clang version,
prefixed s6- so it never meets the gcc build's. fall-s42 and headline-s1 replay whole on the S6
build (0.7 s), and a fresh worktree's build makes the same hash and replays them. On the 3090:
gpu-tick-check on the 118 failed recordings, 118 of 118 (474,609 device runs, 2,687 redone in
C); lzpack-check PASS; pool-gate OK (40 recordings, 133,280 rows); pipe-gate OK (29 recordings,
23,987 rows, 6,008 frames bit-exact); clangcheck ok. The selected suite fails three play_check
jobs (moon-swamp-s2 and swamp-night-s2 "arena: more than 65536 livings", tnt-cannon-s1 "raster:
mesher vertex buffer full") on master 3a5bb616's own build too, in the canonical tree: not this
lane's, left open. The stale "unknown" images stay in ~/.cache/netherite-regioncache, now
unreachable. Ledger: native/tests/divergences/s6lz.tsv (fall-s42, area cuda, fixed).

accounted for 59% of hits in the first sample, with a 4,224-byte living sampled in 43 of 66 lines

## 2026-09-30 The device mesher's stored count chain 24% shorter, every mesh byte-equal (lane/meshclimb)

On the GPU host's RTX PRO 6000, the same six recordings' stored dumps (10,197 meshes,
360 frames) took 99,531 to 75,205 us summed across mesher kernels, and the
count pass's CUDA events took 57.6 to 43.9 ms. The two main drawing kernels
fell from 36,855 to 24,470 us and 34,091 to 21,218 us. The world, biome and
column-noise cache now filled in mesh_class removes repeated world lookups
from drawing lanes; their record states are contiguous and copied 16 bytes at
a time; the cuts weight cells by measured draw cost. mesh_wcopy's 1,024-thread
launch took 851 to 614 us, mesh_class's 256-thread launch undid part of the
cache fill's cost (2,970 to 2,580 us in the current design), and mesh_cut
shares the next cut through a warp shuffle (636 to 583 us in the weighted
design). The cache and weights deliberately move work into mesh_class and
mesh_cut: against the original base those kernels grew from 1,707 to 2,587
and 487 to 583 us. out/perf/meshclimb.tsv has all 19 mesher kernels before
and after, kept and discarded attempts, and Nsight Compute evidence for
each entry (nine from the baseline report, ten from a bounded final report).

The profiler's drawing launches had 224 and 144 registers a thread, 9% and
14% active-warp occupancy, about five and four threads per instruction, and
low memory throughput. World reads and lane-state stores held them; explicit
ptxas spill loads and stores were zero for these two (their local traffic is
the call stack). mesh_wcopy had 16.9% occupancy, 11.8 load and 15.6 store
sectors a request, and long-scoreboard stalls. The table records registers,
occupancy, stall reasons, sectors per request, branch uniformity, and spills
for all entries. The attempted 192-register draw cap was below the
run-to-run noise. A two-uint64 vector copy and 128-thread copy were slower;
1024-class threads were slower, and 128-class threads were flat against 256.

For the same master 5f4cd0da and village corpus at N 32, the two baseline
runs measured 0.080 and 0.076 device mesh ms per env-step and 4,093 and
5,283 env-steps/s; the lane measured 0.072 and 0.071 ms and 4,334 and
5,492 env-steps/s. All four runs had trajectory digest 876d814b2f108e3a.
Host step time varied from 1.60 to 2.57 ms under other lanes' load, so the
throughput difference is an observation, not a mesher-only speedup. The final
N 128 run measured 10,025 env-steps/s, 0.137 device mesh ms per step and

## 2026-09-30 One config.yaml per world: the oracle, the C side and the pipeline read it; configs/headline.yaml, peaceful at render distance 6 (lane/worldyaml)

Elliot, 2026-09-30 1:40 am: "a unified config.yaml is the ideal setup for a given world". `config.yaml` at
the root replaces world.conf. Sections: `world` (seed, difficulty, render_distance, the game rules
daylight_cycle and keep_inventory, villages and the 17 unsupported switches), `client` (graphics,
particles, observation, ticks_per_step, hud), `engine` (device_mesh, device_generation, device_light) and
`pipeline` (kind, start: the snapshot the pipeline's envs start from, recorded from that file). The
grammar is a strict YAML subset written in the file's header (sections at column 0, entries exactly two
spaces in, plain scalars, # comments; no tabs, quotes, lists, flow or nesting), so a real YAML parser
reads it too and ours need no library: java WorldConf.java (the registry, KEYS) and native/src/worldconf.c
(the same table) parse it line for line; a key left out takes config.yaml's value.

- Java: CONF=path (configs/NAME.yaml), SET="key=value" with section.key or a bare world key (every
  existing SET="seed=... villages=on ..." caller unchanged). world.difficulty and world.render_distance
  feed options.txt (difficulty was a constant 2 even on replay: a replay now takes options.difficulty
  from the header); --rd and --particles stay as overrides; client.graphics and particles are the
  defaults of --option fancy and --particles. A seed start's non-vanilla game rules are set at its
  first server tick (Dev.atServerTick -> WorldConf.atServerTick, no java/src edit).
- What a tape records: the header's `world` stays the seed and the switches, plus a game rule only when
  it is not vanilla's; difficulty and render distance stay options.difficulty and options.rd, where
  every tape has them (1.7.10 applies both from options.txt at server start, a save does not keep
  them; 189 stored recordings run rd 8 through --rd). So every existing header is unchanged, and a
  default-config re-record of fresh-play-s1 has the same rows and the same world and options.
  session.sh's chain passes the tape's difficulty and render distance on with its world keys.
- C: `make -C native worldconf-check` (tests/worldconf_check.c, in make test): config.yaml lists every
  registry key in order at its default; 33 grammar cases refused and 5 read; each config's pipeline.start
  matches it (manifest world, header options) and a start one key off is refused.
- Runtime: pool_config.config (was world_conf) holds every start to the file's world
  (wconf_match_start: seed, switches, rules, difficulty, rd); pipe_config_file sets the observation,
  rd, hud and device switches; pipe_bench and pipe_gate --config FILE (flags override), pool_gate
  --world|--config, make pipe-gate / pool-gate CONFIG=FILE. pipe_bench --config adds the file's kind
  (its pipeline.start) and makes it the default --kinds.
- configs/headline.yaml: seed 1, peaceful, render distance 6 (lane/headline's choice to come), device
  meshing; its start is headline-s1.

The brief's ncu sample (the GPU host, village N 32) flagged ten kernels above 9 global sectors a request. ncuwrap on
The dev host's 3090 gives master the same counts to the decimal (quads<1> 20.3 / 13.8, ebox 28.2 / 31.9, pairs 8.9 / 4.7),
so the counters carry over between the cards; every before and after below is the 3090's (sm_86), master
b930b03d against the branch, medians of 3 on six recordings' stored dumps (render_check --seq, 60 frames each:
out/perf/coalesce/kt.sh) and ncu over the pipeline's own launches (ncup.sh). The attempts, kept and not, are in
out/perf/coalesce.tsv (17 steps; 1 to 11 were run on the GPU host, then the dumps were made again here).

Kept:
- tri's binning fields lead the record (box, mode, sx, sy, then a crack's x, y: 64 bytes), may_cover picks
  by value. The section quads' kernel loads each 128-byte quad as eight 16-byte loads (bytes used a fetched sector
  12% to 50%; quads<0> 3259 to 3025 us, quads<1> 7891 to 6306).
- pairs and trip_pairs: a warp per 32 triangles, their 64-byte heads loaded whole by the warp's 16-byte loads into
  shared memory, one pair a lane (its triangle by a 5-step search over the 33 offsets), keys and values stored
  consecutively. A thread a triangle read fields 240 bytes apart and a triangle over many tiles held its warp.
  Global load sectors in the pipeline's launches 173 M to 8.6 M, bytes used a sector 12.7% to 81%.
- edge_may's double fallback out of line (edge_exact_ge0, __noinline__): inlined, the binning's loops had its
  F2F/DADD/DMUL hoisted and speculated into every row of every triangle, terrain too (FP64 runs at 1/64 here: 62%
  of pairs' stall samples, the FP64 pipe 68% busy). pairs 9398 to 2265 us on the dumps; 325 to 167 us a launch in
  the pipeline. raster has no such code (60 FP64 instructions of 135 M).
- The generic kernel's and the entity clipper's planes that every vertex is inside of are skipped (the copy of a
  polygon in local memory was most of their traffic): generic<0> 3443 to 2921, generic<1> 7747 to 6727.
- equads<1> builds its triangle in registers and stores 15 uint4s (1323 to 662 us; store sectors 10 M to 1.8 M).
- ebox a thread a face (it was a thread a box, 258 word stores from a grid of a few blocks), and ebox and eitem
  build their cquads in shared memory and the warp stores the records' words consecutively (cquad_flush): ebox
  loads 28.2 to 5.6 sectors a request, stores 32.0 to 4.8 (bytes used 12.5% to 84%), 74 to 11 us a launch.
Explained, not fixed: quads' loads stay at 26 sectors a request (a lane's 16-byte loads 128 bytes apart; L1
serves the other half of each sector) and the count reads 12 of each vertex's 32 bytes: that is the mesh's vertex

## 2026-09-29 Unloaded chunks 5.7 to 19 times cheaper to park: an in-tree LZ codec, a park that waits a row, and the spill's writeback without a wait (lane/spillfast)

Where the zlib time went, exactly: temporary counters (perf_event user instructions around every
pack, unpack, spill and take; out/spill/instrumented.diff, never committed), N 8, the difference of a
--steps 1100 and a --steps 100 run (8,000 env-steps). Base: village 1.09 M instructions an env-step in
the path, exploring 4.41 M, Nether 0.69 M. deflate in chunk_pack took 605 to 658 K a call (19.5 a
byte of a 34.6 KB raw chunk), inflate 258 K (7.8 a byte), the spill's compress2 of the chunk struct
and extra bytes (3.5 KB) 128 to 149 K; zlib's init is not the cost (deflateReset measured the same).
The packed blob was never compressed twice (the spill appends it as it is). Most chunks a load takes
back from the store come back within a tick of their park (village 6,095 of 6,785 reloads), each one
a full pack, spill, take and unpack.

Codecs on the captured bytes (1,506 parked chunks, 1,347 spill records, three kinds): zlib 1 10.45x
at 19.5 / 7.8 instructions a byte (compress / decompress), zstd -1 10.9x at 12.7 / 6.4, lz4 5.93x at
3.25 / 2.36; the dev host has no zstd.h or lz4.h (the GPU host no lz4.h), so no new library. native/src/lzpack.c is
an LZ77 in LZ4's block form (a five-byte hash, an immediate second match, fixed-size copies, LZ4's
overlap copy): 6.53x at 4.1 / 2.8 at -O2, portable C, allocating nothing (the table and the
decoder's slack are the caller's). chunk_pack, chunk_unpack_blob and regionspill.c (records and
blobs) use it; zlib is gone from world.c and regionspill.c. A parked chunk now packs one row after
its unload (SR_PARK_WAIT 1, serverreplay_park's park_row stamps; 2, 4 and 20 rows measured no
better); its entity lists still go at the park of its own row. tests/lzpack_check.c (make
lzpack-check, run by make test): 7,986 round trips over every path of the format, 14,598 damaged
streams refused, none decoded past its buffer.

## 2026-09-29 A chunk section's light and metadata arrays held once when they are one value: server chunks 38% smaller (lane/chunkmem)

The server's loaded chunks were the largest owner left in an env after lane/entmem (27.6 MB of a village env,
about 56 KB a chunk): every section a whole 10,304-byte band (ids 4 KB, metadata, sky light and block light 2 KB
each). A census of the loaded bands (a temporary envmem hook, out/perf/chunkmem/census.patch; N 32 capacity
window, t 10 s) over the corpus: in a village env sky light is one value in 69% of bands (0 in 68.7%, 15 in
0.4%), block light 0 in 85%, metadata all 0 in 69%; exploring 67 / 83 / 63%, the Nether kind 65 / 81 / 64%. A
section of one block is 0.07% (not worth a mode); 98% of bands hold 16 distinct (id, meta) or fewer, 99.8% 16
ids or fewer.

Kept: struct chunk_sec is a 32-byte header and the ids (4,160-byte slot); its three nibble arrays are named by
self-relative offsets (nib[k]) into a new arena pool of 2 KB slots (ARENA_NIBS), whose first sixteen slots are
the constant arrays (every nibble v), made with the arena and shared by every band. A read is chunk_sec_nib (the
offset sits in the header line beside ids_hi); a store that changes a constant array takes the band's own slot
first (chunk_sec_nib_set: a pool slot, no allocation); the bulk stores (chunk_cells_in, generate_skylight_map's
fill, lightcap's write-back, the region codec) hold an array that comes out one value as the constant again
(own arrays left uniform afterwards: under 1%). A copy with its arrays inline (struct chunk_sec_flat, offsets
pointing inline) is what the device mesher's band images (meshfeed, MF_BAND_BYTES 12,320) and the light
engine's mirror (lightcap_layout) carry, so every device kernel reads the bytes it read before and the same
accessors read either form; S6 on the device reads the arena image's offsets as the host does. A second
candidate, a 4-bit id palette on top (a 64-byte header, the index array a fourth nibble array, ids as bytes
past 16 distinct), saved 6 to 10 MB an env more but cost 7 to 8% more user instructions per env-step on the
tick's hottest read (world_get_block) and the bulk paths; not kept (out/perf/chunkmem/palette.patch).

## 2026-09-29 Cache locality for the host tick: env to worker pinning and L3 placement measured, nothing wins at N 128 (lane/pincache)

The question (from lane/tickmem): the tick runs at a fraction of its N 16 IPC at N 128 with the same
code; does keeping each env on one worker, and each worker on one core or L3, recover it? The GPU host's
timing cores 0-31 are four L3 domains of 8 cores (32 MB each), siblings 64-95.

Built (native/runtime, every output the same): pool_config.place (enum pool_place: none, cores,
siblings, spread, domain; each worker on one CPU of the mask pool_make ran under, domain: any CPU
of its L3), pin 2 (a queue per L3 domain beside pin 1's queue per worker), steal (an idle pinned
worker takes a job waiting beyond another queue's idle workers, its own L3's first: the corpus tail
when envs divide unevenly); pipe_config.pool_layout (0: the pipeline's layout, 1: cfg.pool's);
pipe_bench --pin P --place NAME --steal. The pipeline's default stays today's (any worker, any CPU).

Measured on the GPU host GPU 2, PERF=1, pipe_bench's corpus (100 + 1000 steps), device meshing, --counters,
perf stat over the measured steps (DRAM demand fills; fills from another L3, near_cache; from the
own L3, local_ccx), every run under tbench.sh -big so no other big run overlapped (the first N 32
batch ran beside another lane's 128-env run and was thrown away). All 228 runs of a kind and size
gave the same trajectory digest, whatever the layout or worker count (and each half of a two-process
split its own digest, the same in every round).
Medians of paired rounds against today's, out/perf/pincache.tsv (raw rows pincache-raw.tsv,
pincache-two.tsv), chart out/perf/pincache.png:

- N 32 (30 workers, 6 rounds of today's and cores): cores (env on worker i mod T, a worker a
  physical core, L3 by L3) cut the tick's cycles an env-step 32 / 30 / 19% (village / Nether /
  exploring), DRAM demand fills 38 / 39 / 16%, fills from another L3 46 / 59 / 66%, IPC 1.67 to
  2.48, 1.66 to 2.45, 2.23 to 2.56. env-steps/s +7, +13, -12%: at N 32 the render stream bounds,
  and 30 workers for 32 envs leave two workers two envs, the corpus's tail. Affinity alone (a worker
  a core, shared queue: lane/pagefault's try) +0 to +3%; both threads of a core (siblings) no
  cycle gain; the L3 queue with stealing +6, +2, +7%.
- N 128 (24 workers, 3 rounds): no layout cut the DRAM fills (-5 to +13%); fills from another
  L3 were already 4 to 8% of the DRAM fills (964 / 1,682 / 1,437 an env-step against 19.7 k /
  22.2 k / 39.3 k). env-steps/s against 7,884 / 8,720 / 3,276: cores -4, -17, -20%; spread (a
  worker a core, the L3s in turn) +9, -12, -13%; L3 queues with stealing +20, -2, -12%; spread
  with L3 queues and stealing +15, -26, -2%; pinned queues with stealing -41, -29% (one round:
  envs bounce). With 32 envs an L3 an env's lines are gone before its next step; the pinned
  layouts lose to envs dividing unevenly (5.33 a worker: workers 84% busy against 98%) and to
  the render streams' threads losing cores. Today's own runs spread 11 to 41% run to run on
  this shared machine.
- Workers (N 128, 16 to 64): at 32 (4 envs a worker, even) every layout is within 8% of today's
  (village 9,067 to 9,323 against 9,114; exploring 3,762 to 4,124 against 4,058). Today's layout
  at 16 / 24 / 28 / 32 / 40 / 48 / 64 workers: village 8,190 / 8,168 / 7,408 / 7,884 / 6,522 /
  8,038 / 8,545, exploring 2,607 / 3,276 / 3,534 / 3,554 / 3,451 / 3,838 / 2,819: 24 to 48
  within the noise, exploring loses a fifth at 16 and 64. Each added worker raises the tick's
  DRAM fills and cycles an env-step (village 4.9 M cycles at 16 workers, 6.2 to 7.3 at 24, 7.4
  to 10.8 at 32 to 64): the tick at N 128 is bound by the machine's memory system, not by where
  its threads run.
- One process of 128 against two of 64 (--env-base 0 and 64, 12 workers each, 3 rounds): two on
  the same cores 7,939 / 6,254 / 2,615 against 8,793 / 7,785 / 2,917 (-10, -20, -10%); each on
  two of the four L3s 8,088 / 6,101 / 2,766 (-8, -22, -5%). Halving the envs an L3 does not buy
  back what the second process's streams and caches cost.

ticks, light results and Random draws in the same order):

- Springs (features_springs.c): func_149808_o's flow-cost search, when every

  first over grid indices: a side's value is the least depth at which a
  non-reversing walk of FC_ON cells stands beside an FC_FALL cell, so each
  side stops at its first layer that finds one and a (cell, incoming side)
  met again is not walked again. With a side to search, the 61 cells within
  5 are classified at once (SP_CLASS by id), and a diamond with no fall
  answers every side 1000. Otherwise the Java-order walk runs as before. A
  throwaway bench found 0 of 133,355 calls differing from the old walk.
  Springs water 975 to 498 K a chunk, lava 229 to 176.

  (chunk, band) its box touches, each band looked up at its first read and
  all dropped after a write or a read through world_get_block.

  written blocks are both on SET_PLAIN (a checked list of ids with empty
  breakBlock and onBlockAdded in blockcb.c, no chest or tile entity) and
  whose chunk is in the near cache runs set_block_step's calls in its order
  without a worklist frame: an ore write 1,146 to 936 instructions. The
  population features' plain writes take it, and the tick's.

  first loop a column's 16 cells of a band are tested for a light source at

## 2026-09-29 The device mesher's table mode: every cell drawn apart, a thread a cell or a face (lane/meshtab)

The device mesher's draw kernels were 53% of the device's time at N 128 village: the C block
renderer run by lanes, each walking a run of cells in rb_mesh_section's chain. Measured first
(temporary clock64 counters, N 32 corpus, out/perf/meshtab.tsv p0-p2): of the lanes' per-cell draw
cycles, hidden cubes 35 / 43 / 42% (village / Nether / exploring; 29-48k cycles each, for a draw
that emits nothing), standard blocks 41 / 38 / 37% (155-225k cycles each, 98% full cubes), liquids
16 / 17 / 9%, crosses, stairs, logs and vines the rest; no lane ever emits a vertex before its own
setters (0 in 76 M); and the pipeline's scenes mesh without smooth lighting (forest-fast, ao 0).

Without smooth lighting a cell's draw depends on the mesher's state only through the words its own
begin sets (the bounds), and leaves the others as it found them, for all but pistons, fence gates
and dragon eggs: a section pass's cells can be drawn independently and laid out in order after.
--mesh-tab (pipe_bench, pipe_gate, the pipeline's cfg.mesh_tab, render_check and gate.sh; make
pipe-gate MESHTAB=1) runs every count pass that way (cuda/meshing/table.h, table.c, table_host.c,
table.mk). The host builds a class table at setup from the C renderer itself: every (id, meta)
drawn on its own in 24 random worlds and held to the checks the device repeats (the end state the
template's but the bounds, no vertex field left at the mark, at most 128 vertices), and how the
device draws it: standard blocks, liquids and doors a face a thread, logs, fences and stairs a box's
face a thread (their draws are render_standard_block over boxes), anything else whole, a thread a
cell (rb_mesh_cell). The face and box paths transcribe the C's float operations in its order; the
host holds each of their (id, meta) against rb_mesh_cell byte for byte and draws whole whatever
differs. Icons that only the (id, meta, face) decide and a door's upper icon (door_upper_uv's
atlas search) are baked in the table. Per launch: a world cache and the cell lists beside each
other, the five classes' kernels on five streams, each request's layout and a wide copy into vbuf.
A request with a drawn cell the table cannot draw, or a whole-cell draw failing its checks, is
counted by mesh_run the exact way; one past the table's buffer goes to the write pass. The lanes'
kernels do not run in the table mode; kernels.c keeps three small hunks (the shared context
header, mesh_run's filter).

## 2026-09-29 An exploring env's memory bounded: unloaded chunks to disk (lane/envmem)

An exploring env grew about 37 KB of resident memory an env-step (N 8, a seed per env: 2.8 MB/s an
env; heap address space 20 MB/s, which would fill the 32 GB heap reservation in about 26 minutes;
the 131,072 chunk slots full in about seven minutes). Measured by owner (pipe_bench --mem-every,
test_snapshots --mem-every, and a temporary allocation-site census of the image heap and the list
slab, out/perf/envmem/census*.py), the growers were, per env at N 8: parked chunks in the region
store 1.66 MB/s (21 KB an env-step), the heap blocks around them (chunk_pack's deflateBound blocks
kept by an in-place realloc), saved-entity records and their NBT about 0.4 MB/s, the entity chunk
tables (a list set per chunk ever holding an entity) 0.19 MB/s, the spawner's append-only records
0.064 MB/s (abort at 131,072), mineshaft pieces about 0.29 MB/s. Loaded chunks, livings, the
client world, the generation cache (1,024 MB, full), the pool's result buffers and the device side
stayed flat or fluctuated with what is loaded; the view's texture copies grow to the set seen.

Fixed, each checked over every stored recording (out/native/recs '*': 839/843, the four retired
ones fail on master too): native/src/regionspill.c keeps a parked chunk (packed, with its tile
entities, saved entities by an iterative NBT codec, saved ticks) in one unlinked file per env and
reads it back byte for byte at its load; an unloaded chunk's empty entity lists go; the overworld
spawner drops the records of mobs gone for good (also proven at a 64-record threshold); loaded
saved-entity records nothing reads again go; a mineshaft's or village's pieces are freed once every
chunk that can reach it has populated, and a far mineshaft's pieces wait in a blob file (also
proven spilling every start every row). The files are written back and dropped from the page cache
every 8 MB. pool-gate (40 recordings), pool-gate GEN=cuda and pipe-gate DRAW=1 bit-exact; the
corpus runs' trajectory digests identical before and after.

Results: explore-long-s1 peak RSS 456 to 254 MB (region store at its end 173.6 to 5.8 MB), 617.1
to 604.2 G user instructions. N 128 exploring with a seed per env: before, 23 GB after the warm-up
and killed at the 40 GB cap 56 s in; after, 10 minutes at a 36.2 GB peak, the growth falling to
about 2 KB an env-step while it still explores (out/perf/envmem/rss.png). Fixed corpus N 128:
village 9,332 / 9,178, Nether 8,450 / 8,296, exploring 3,317 / 3,428 env-steps/s (noise 15%),

## 2026-09-29 The device mesher's illegal address: warps left split by ptxas's spilled barriers (lane/meshcrash)

renderprec-anvil-cumesh reproduced on the dev host's 3090 only with the ptxas -O1
mesher (PERF=0; the ledger rows were -O1 builds, -O3 has been the default
since this morning): `make -C native cuda-mesh-check PERF=0
MESH_ARGS=pix-fluid-s1` died in its 73rd launch, 8 of 12 batches of the
93-recording gate died, pipe_bench explore N 32 died 2 of 2. memcheck on a
line-info cubin (MESH_G=1, new): Invalid __global__ read of size 4 at
rec_state (kernels.c wget) from lane_end, address 0x7ffd00000040. The
kernel kept the local mesher's generic address in uniform register UR5 from
its entry to lane_end, and lane_end's state_changed loads c[0x0][0x118]
into UR4:UR5; cuda-gdb found lane 29 alone in lane_end after the other 31
lanes had run it and exited. That is legal code only for a whole warp:
device printf of __activemask showed the warp whole after the warm draw and
split after the run's draw_cells_cube (477,880 split lanes over the 93
recordings, all in the cube kernel), and the bar.warp.sync(live) after it
compiled to a NOP. The split: the render tree's calls take every
convergence barrier ptxas has (B0..B9, B11 at calls), so a branch around a
call above it gets its barrier spilled (BMOV.32.CLEAR Rn, B0 before the
call, BMOV.32 Bk, Rn + BSYNC after), and the lanes that come back first (a
hidden cube is quick, a drawn block is not) restore the barrier while the
others still use it inside. A 12-deep nvcc test with 15 such spills does
not split, so this is named by what the SASS and the masks show, not
proven a ptxas bug. The run kernels split too (59,008 lanes) but their
block barrier rejoins them; their overflow redraw went straight into
SHFL.UP with no sync (meshcrash-run-overflow-shfl).

Fix (cuda/meshing/kernels.c): draw_cells_as is one loop over the cells
with no branch around a call (render_all_faces is 0 between cells,
MESHING_ERR_STATE if not) and the warm draw is unconditional, which leaves
the cube kernels with no barrier spilled across a call and no splits; a
block barrier follows every draw in the draw kernels (lanes past the
kernel's part meet both barriers) and in run_block (the warm draw, the
overflow redraw). meshing.mk: MESH_G=1, and gpu-meshing-check depends on
render_check by path (render.mk is read after meshing.mk, so
$(RENDER_BIN) was empty and a mesher edit was checked with the old
render_check). New MESHING quick gate: gpu-meshing-check PERF=0 on
pix-fluid-s1; gpu-meshing-stress walks a seed per env.

Gates on the merged tree: gpu-meshing-check 96,003 of 96,003 meshes and
1,694 of 1,694 frames at PERF=1 and PERF=0; pipe-gate MESH=2 DRAW=1 at
GROUP=1 and groups of 8, 80,346 of 80,346 device meshes, 6,008 frames;
pipe-gate OK; explore N 32 --env-seeds 3 of 3 at PERF=0 (master 0 of 2);
memcheck on perfhost's explore repro 0 errors at both builds;
initcheck: only word 6 of a vertex without normals copied unwritten
(vanilla's Tessellator leaves it stale too); clangcheck ok; the four quick
gates in a fresh worktree; make -s -C native test rc 0. Performance
(out/perf/meshcrash.tsv, gpubench, interleaved, same digests): explore N 64
mesher 0.960 to 0.823 device-ms an env-step (-14%), 1,578 to 1,720
env-steps/s (+9%); village unchanged. nsys per launch: mesh_draw_cube 2.97

## 2026-09-29 native/cuda by what each part does, with plain names (lane/cudanames)

Elliot: "we are clearly in a cuda directory, cu___ doesn't make sense".
native/cuda is one folder per part, and inside a folder the names drop the
prefix the folder already says. A rename only: every device output is
byte-identical (the gates below at -O1 and at PERF=1), the host engine is
untouched. Done by out/cudanames/rename.py (`moves`: git mv, the first
commit alone so other lanes' edits follow the renames; `text`: includes,
paths, kernels, host API, targets, output names, mirror keys over native/,
index/, AGENTS.md and SPEC.md, nothing under java/), then by hand: the
worldgen and light sections of native/Makefile moved to
cuda/worldgen/worldgen.mk and cuda/lighting/lighting.mk (cwlight.mk folded
into the latter), every object named out/native/obj/cuda_PART_FILE.o (so
two parts may each have a host.cu; NVJOB's memory key is PART_FILE),
cuda/include serving both clang device builds (the mesher's pthread.h
stub behind -DNW_MESH_DEVICE, the tick's pthreadtypes-arch.h for the
tick only), nwpass.cpp keeping the runtime's kernels out of nw-stub and
nw-dev by their calling convention (PTX_Kernel) as it keeps nwdev_ names
(renaming nwdev_s6 to chunkloop would otherwise have instrumented it; the
build's counts are the same: 347 functions kept, 1945 pointer loads, 593
stores, 6471 writes), the tick scripts' `cd` one level deeper, the
include guards. The mesher's PTX and ptxas report are the old ones but for
the names; the mirror check's mirrored sets are the same size per kernel
(121, 236, 366, 422, 437, 253).

Kernel names are by stage and unique across native/cuda; the folder's word
goes in front where the bare word would clash: `seeds`, `replay`, `tri_env`
and `scatter` are already parameter or function names where the kernel is
launched, the mesher's kernels share one C module with the engine's
render_blocks*.c where run, plan, cut and fix are names (the whole family
is mesh_*), and the tick's scatter and gather would repeat the renderer's.
The plan labels (GPU plan L15, L16, L17 in comments and SPEC) stay: they
name the design plan's items, not mirror keys. out/perf and the ledger's
rows (native/tests/divergences/*.tsv) keep the old names as history.

## 2026-09-29 The tick's memory: the pending ticks as sorted runs, the random ticks fetched ahead, the chunk's hot fields together, the spawner's census as bytes (lane/tickmem)

Profiled on the GPU host at N 128, device meshing, the pipeline's 24 workers
(perf record with ls_dmnd_fills_from_sys.dram_io_all and cycles on a
frame-pointer build, attributed by call chain; IBS needs system-wide
access, so structures are named by the missing loads' functions and
lines). At the episode's start one structure dominated: the pending tick
set, a 40-byte-entry binary heap of a snapshot's 150,000 falling-block
ticks drained 1,000 a tick, where ticks_pop was 19% of the workers'
cycles and 23 to 29% of their DRAM fills (a heap descent a pop). After
it, the misses are spread thin: the random ticks' block reads (18.7% of
the village's steady-state fills), the entity pass (28 to 38%, no line
above 3%), chunk lookups reading a chunk only to compare its key, the
spawner's walk over every record it ever made.

What changed, every output the same:
- ticks.c: the pending set keeps up to 8 sorted runs (rings) beside the
  heap; an entry joins the run whose last it follows most closely, so a
  snapshot's backlog and each delay's schedules (time and entry id both
  rise) pop from a run's head; the membership slot is prefetched 8 pops
  ahead. A pop no longer descends a heap: the heap stays empty in the
  three recordings.
- servertick.c: the random ticks' cells prefetched from the update LCG
  before each chunk's loop (only a hint: the loop still decides), and the
  next active chunk's lines.
- world.h: struct chunk's key, mask and bands 0 to 5 in its first cache
  line (a read below y 96 touches one chunk line, not two), the random
  tick gates and relight cursor in line 2, the light memo in line 3; the
  chunk map keeps each slot's key beside its ref (a lookup or a loaded
  check reads no chunk).
- world.c: a parked chunk's blob leaves out all-zero metadata and light
  arrays (a flag bit each: 79% of them in a Nether run); a band copied
  whole is taken without the pool's 10 KB clear (arena.c pool_take_raw).
- spawning.c: each record's alive, persistent and type as a byte beside
  the records (countEntities walks bytes), set_persistent writes a record
  only when the flag changes, and the id index is sized to the records
  with the ids in its slots.
- native/runtime: the pool's workers count user cycles beside
  instructions; pipe_bench --counters prints the tick's cycles and IPC.

counters; 3 interleaved rounds, medians; out/perf/tm/final.tsv, the
digests equal between base and lane in every start and corpus run):

| corpus | exploring | 3,201 to 3,236 | 6.42 to 6.16 | 19.9, 2.25 to 19.2, 2.30 | 46.2 k to 38.7 k |

## 2026-09-29 Generation on the device in phases, and a batched device backend for the pool (lane/genphase)

Measured first, on master (0b90acac with pipe_bench --env-seeds added),
exploring at N 128 with device meshing, perf record over the measured
steps (instructions:u, a frame-pointer build), shares of the tick: with one
seed for all envs, generation (world_chunk_request) 2.1% and population
(sr_populate) 54.2%: the generation cache served 17,097 chunks from 165
generated. With a seed per env (--env-seeds: env g's worlds of seed S + g,
src/populate.c populate_reseed), generation 25.1% (raw 22.4%: density
12.7, surface 4.9, biomes 1.7, caves 2.6, ravines 0.5; the constructor 1.9
and its sky map 1.4) and population 27.3%; tick 69.5 M user instructions an
env-step against 92.6 with one seed. out/perf/genphase.tsv step 0.

The kernels (cuda/cugen_carve.cuh, byte-exact with the C generator): the
carvers walked every tunnel of the 289 source chunks around each target, a
thread per chunk. Now the batch's sources are deduplicated in a device hash
table, each source's tunnels listed from its Random, each tunnel walked once
(a thread a tunnel) into spheres (a branch's children after the parent's
steps), and a block per target carves a thread per column: the reach, box and
room tests are the target's (one thread per staged sphere computes them: FP64
runs at 1/64 rate on this card), the water (the Nether: lava) shell test is
per column and ORed per stage of 128 spheres (water is never written or
cleared by a carver), and a tunnel whose reach box misses the target is
skipped. The overworld surface pass is a thread per column (LCG jump-ahead
starts; a column draws 258 times plus a sand run's or a rejected draw, the
extras scanned until the starts settle), the Nether's too (each column's
extra draws, 0 to 4, tabled over a window of starts and chained; a rejected
draw or a start outside the window runs the chunk serially), the End's no-op
pass a thread per column. Device ms per batch of 1,024 fresh chunks (gen-bench,
PERF=1): overworld caves 191.6 to 3.0, ravines 156.8 to 1.7, surface 10.1 to
0.6, the whole batch 362.3 to 13.2 (0.013 ms a chunk, C 0.35 on one thread);
Nether caves 328.8 to 2.9, surface 6.6 to 5.1, the batch 254.2 to 7.8 (at
32 chunks 11.4 to 2.1). out/perf/fig/genphase-kernels.png. cuda_chunkgen now
also checks each column's topBlock entry and the provider rand after the
surface pass, cuda_dimgen the Nether's rand (a planted off-by-one fails at
the surface stage). nvcc 13.3's cicc segfaults on cugen_carve.cu if four
doubles are added to struct cv_tun (the reach box lives in struct cv_box).

The pool (runtime/pool.c, pool_config.gen; pipeline.h gen_device;
pipe_bench and pipe_gate --gen-device, pool_gate --gen c|cuda,
make pool-gate or pipe-gate GEN=cuda): at the end of each step (and at the
first step after a reset) an env predicts its next step's generations
(genahead_predict: genahead's square, pathfinder windows, due ticks, portals,
the tape's Dev tp targets, now a dead player's respawn square); a generation
thread takes every waiting env at once, generates the round's unique
requests on its generator (ga_gen_cuda_local_create: cugen and cudim in the
process, on a non-blocking stream of the device's highest priority, waits on
a blocking event, pinned round buffers), two rounds in flight
(ga_gen.another), the last 2,048 results kept for later rounds (one seed:
a chunk is not made again); each result is held by reference
(genahead_fill_raw) and constructed when a tick takes it, population stays on
the host in its order, a generation the prediction missed runs on C in the
tick. The host path stays the default.

Gates, all on the merged tree (60d9efee): L15 quick and full (chunkgen 6,848
and dimgen 3,494 chunks with every negative control, gen-ahead 3/3);
pool-gate host and GEN=cuda, 40 recordings, 133,280 rows equal each (35,154
tick generations served from the device, 1 by C); pipe-gate DRAW=1 host and
GEN=cuda, 29 recordings, 23,987 rows and 6,008 frames bit-exact (3,444
served, 0 by C); pipe-gate GEN=cuda MESH=1 the same; clangcheck ok;

## 2026-09-29 pipe_bench measures what it claims: a fixed corpus, global env ids, a symmetric walk, invalid runs fail, the device's busy union (lane/benchfix)

From GPT-6 Astra's review of the benchmark (each point checked against the
code). pipe_bench's default mode is now a fixed corpus: every env reset to
its kind's start, 100 steps unmeasured and 1000 measured (--warm, --steps),
each env's actions from its own seeded stream, and a trajectory digest
(every result's flags, ticks, row, the player's position, look, dimension,
health and food, env by env) printed to prove the work: the same digest at
-j 4 and 16, 1 and 2 streams, host-only, with and without counters, CUPTI
and the sweep. --seconds is the capacity mode, never an A/B (a faster build
reaches other states in a wall-time window). Each line names its mode, the
policy and the global env ids (--env-base E seeds env i as global env E+i:
two processes of 64 no longer replay the same 64 streams). Policy 2 (the
default) centres the look deltas ((u - 127.5) x scale, (u - 31.5) x 0.05;
policy 1, the walk before, drifted -0.025 degrees of pitch and -0.05 of yaw
a step); pipe_tune's walk too. A run with an error, a missing or lost frame
or a short corpus prints FAIL, no throughput, and exits 1 (it caught
--warm 0 stepping every env once: fixed); ticks are the steps' own. The
per-tick hardware counters (18 read syscalls a step in the views, 2 in the
pool) and the shared atomics are gone from the default path: pool_config
no_counters, per-env sums on their own cache lines summed outside the hot
path, on with --counters or --profile. --profile also records the device's
timeline with CUPTI (native/runtime/devbusy.c: kernels, copies, memsets on
every stream) and prints the union; without it the renders' CUDA events are
printed as overlapping stream sums with the host's staging in them (the
"upload" interval is render.cu's ev[0] to ev[1]: the host building the draw
lists plus the copies it queued). pipe_tune resets every env and reseeds
before each candidate's window and, when the pipeline chose the workers,
gives each candidate its own count (pool_threads_set). pipe_make refuses
--host-only with device meshing (it meshed on the host).

The corpus on master's engine (d5d950ff), the GPU host GPU 1, N 128, device
meshing, 24 workers, --profile, env-steps/s (out/perf/benchfix.tsv):
village 9662, 9495, 8733 (policy 2) and 9857, 9623 (policy 1); Nether 8465,
6215, 8391 and 8467, 7997; exploring 3267, 3062, 3296 and 3275, 3290. The
two policies are within the spread. The device is busy (some kernel or copy
in flight) 98.4 to 99.1% of the wall in village, 85 to 93% Nether, 90 to 92%
exploring, while the same intervals summed over the streams give 460 to 487%
(the old "device 345% of the wall" was that kind of sum); kernels overlap

The Nether kind measures the overworld: its players die in the fortress
within the warm-up (16 of 16 by step 100 at N 16) and respawn at the world
