## 2026-09-29 The device renderer builds in pieces: an -O3 edit to the geometry kernels 20.4 s to 1.8-2.6 s, the count passes lean (lane/renderbuild)

render_kern.cu (one unit: k_generic's count and write templates took 7.3
and 7.7 s of ptxas at -O3, over 4,000 SASS instructions each, because
every sky slot's clip_quad inlined two copies of clip_triangle) is split
by kernel family: render_quads.cu (k_quads), render_equads.cu (k_equads),
render_gen.cu (k_generic with its path for the sky's slots and the
clipped section quads) and render_gen_rec.cu (its path for the recorded
passes: the clipped entity quads, cracks, end portals, lines, depth
clears, called across units), sharing render_geom.cuh. The sky's units
now fill four vertices and a mode (sky_verts, quad_verts) and one loop
clips them (clip_unit), so each pass has one clip_triangle. The count
passes (<0>) clip cvx vertices (clip coordinates and screen position)
through the same templates as the write passes (clip_tri, emit_tri,
e_clip, e_tri over the vertex type), so their counts are the write's
triangles by construction and the shading is never computed.

## 2026-09-29 The renderer's precision: exact and fast, the C renderer and the device alike, stage by stage (lane/renderprec)

A frame's precision is a mask of fast stages (native/src/raster_prec.h):
xform (the terrain vertex's camera offset in float, exact subtracts in
double), edge (the entity and end portal edge tests in float, exact in
double), light (the light coordinates' interpolation and the lightmap's
filter in float16), color (the vertex colour's interpolation in float16),
fog (the fog blend in float16), shade (texel times colour times light,
the entity's material times diffuse and its diffuse's interpolation, the
alpha test's product, in float16) and rcp (the perspective weights by
1 / area and 1 / w once a triangle and one division a pixel, where exact
divides about ten times). exact (0) stays the default and the only mode
judged against Java; fast is every stage. Screen positions, depth and
texture coordinates are float32 in both (they already were); the sky, the
clouds, the crack and the outline draw the same in both. C rounds each
float16 operation's float result to half (rp_h: equal to gcc's _Float16
conversion on all 2^32 floats, and to the correctly rounded half operation
since float's 24 bits are at least 2 x 11 + 2); the device uses its own
__half and __half2 operations (the _rn forms, never contracted), so a
device frame is byte for byte C's in either mode. The setting travels as
raster_obs.prec (the dump format NWOBS7; NWOBS6 dumps read as exact),
raster_live_set_prec, raster_entity_set_prec (the entity rasterizer's
process state, one per playview copy), pv_config.render_prec (PV_API 5),
pool_obs.prec (the observation spec), play --render-prec, pipe_gate and
pipe_bench --render-prec, pipe_play.sh -p, render_gate.sh --prec
(RENDER_PREC), judge_gate.sh --prec (JUDGE_PREC), pipe-gate RPREC. Never
an environment variable.

Device: k_raster is templated on the render's precision (every frame
exact: the fast stages compiled out, the kernel master's to the
instruction; every frame fast: compiled in; mixed: each environment's
mask), chosen per render; rcp's reciprocals and fast frames' colour and
light (as __half2s, what the stages round them to) are written by the
triangle writers (write_sink, k_quads' lean path, e_tri), not in k_raster,
so lane/rasterkern's barrier-free k_raster keeps them. One bug on the way:
envp.prec first sat after fogm, past the part k_quads copies to shared
memory, and 15 cov-zoo-s1 frames drew with an uninitialised mask; it
leads envp now, with the camera.

The cost of each stage, C exact against C with that stage alone fast,
over the render gate's 1694 frames (93 frame judges, 128x128; render_check
--prec-diff, one line each): xform 3.54 px a frame (691 frames differ,
up to 242 a channel: pxdiff calls the worst a texel-selection row, one
pixel row taking the neighbouring texel row), edge 0, light 301.35 px
(1.84%, at most 8 a channel), color 183.83 (1.12%, 2), fog 177.56 (1.08%,
2), shade 234.30 (1.43%, 2), rcp 3.58 (0.02%, 103), fast 606.46 px a frame
(3.70% of the pixels, 1643 of 1694 frames; mean channel error 0.025).
pxdiff's clusters on fast's worst frame: none, even at threshold 1 (every
differing pixel is one step off). The worst frames' pairs and zooms are in
out/perf/renderprec/.

Speed (PERF=1, the GPU host GPU 0, tbench.sh; every attempt in
out/perf/renderprec.tsv): k_raster per 64-frame render (render_check
--bench 64, 16 recordings' 290 frames), re-measured under the CPU
partition and interleaved: master 1.884 to 1.898 ms, exact 1.886 to
1.890, fast 1.681 to 1.690 (-10.6%). The first fast build (every half
operation between float conversions) was 15% slower than exact; the
device's own halves, the templated kernel (inline, the exact path had

What changed, all exact: texanim writes and names only sprites whose bytes
change, with their rectangle; the recorder takes a texture copy back
without a compare unless a write named its source or a free could have put
other bytes at its address (image.h image_free_count_at: the frees of the
block's own class when the texture starts an image heap block, else of its
size tier), and compares only a patch's tiles. The mesh key's band parts
(27 kinds), a section's drawn passes and pot flag are kept per band by pool
slot and generation, since a band a window record holds is never written;
the verify found bands written while no record held them and then taken
back (bed-respawn-s1, chat-deaths-s1, bonemeal-s1), so play names each
band entering a record (dropped hashes) or replacing one with equal bytes
(hashes carried); the hash is four independent xxh64-style lanes. The feed
skips a band whose content serial its slot was last sent, and scans for
pots by memchr. raster_live_frame drops meshes only when the square moves
and reads a per-slot bitmap of sections that may need a key. Atlases only
one owner writes keep the frame each sprite holds. pipe_gate --mesh-check
compares every texture copy, band hash, pass flag and unsent band taken on
trust with the bytes and fails on a difference. Not kept: a memo of a

## 2026-09-29 k_raster 14 times faster: FP32 edge signs, heaviest tiles first, only the triangles that draw a pixel (lane/rasterkern)

Measured on the GPU host's GPU 3 (RTX PRO 6000, sm_120), PERF=1, before = master
25876549 built in a scratch tree, interleaved with the lane under the
1:25 pm CPU partition. render_check --bench 64 over perfrender's 90
pipeline-kind dumps (village, Nether, exploring snapshots): k_raster 5.42
-> 0.39 ms a 64-frame render, the binning 0.155 -> 0.25 ms, the render's
device time without the upload about 7.2 -> 2.1 ms. pipe_bench N 128 with
device meshing (nsys): k_raster a launch 1.05 -> 0.32 ms village, 1.03 ->
0.21 Nether, 1.30 -> 0.24 exploring, its share of all kernel time 18 ->
7%, 15 -> 3%, 28 -> 7%; device ms an env-step -29, -31, -22%;
env-steps/s medians of three rounds 2290 -> 2451, 2975 -> 3198, 2017 ->
2087, inside the rounds' spread (host bound). Every attempt, kept or not,
is a row of out/perf/rasterkern.tsv; out/perf/rasterkern.png the picture.

What limited it, in order (NCU and a per-block clock64 over the tiles):
- A 64-frame launch was 15.8 M cycles with the SMs active 33% of it: two
  tiles of about 4400 entity triangles ran 13.8 M cycles each, on
  edge_exact's doubles (FP64 is 1/64 of FP32 here). edge_sign decides the
  sign in floats when |t1 - t2| > 2^-19 (|t1| + |t2|) (the float and the
  double both within a few ulps of the exact value), the double
  otherwise: 6.71 G adversarial cases on the device, 0 differ; the
  fallback fires 13 times a frame. 5.43 -> 2.58 ms.
- The heavy tiles of the last environments started at the grid's end:
  k_tile_order (one block, a quarter-octave histogram of the tiles' pair
  counts) hands k_raster the keys heaviest first. 2.05 ms.
- 78 to 92% of the triangles whose box met a warp's 8 x 4 pixels drew
  none of them: cover_mask (each lane its batch triangle, the pixel
  functions' own edge predicates on its box's pixels, a superset) and the
  warp visits only triangles that may draw one of its pixels, each pixel
  function only there. 0.93 ms.
- Then the block's two barriers a batch (62% of stall samples): each warp
  walks its tile alone through L1 (0.85), the pixel functions leave the
  box test to the mask (0.81), 80 registers without spills (0.78), the
  next batch's indices and lines fetched ahead (0.73).
- The binning drops a (triangle, tile) pair whose box meets the tile in
  16 pixels or fewer when it draws none of them (the sentinel key, sorted
  last; counts and arena unchanged): the heaviest tile 5993 -> 1414 pairs.
  0.50 ms (the binning +0.09).
- A visited triangle's middle line prefetched (0.455), then each visited
  record copied by cp.async into its warp's shared slot while the one
  before is drawn (0.39).
Tried and dropped: the fallback out of line (FP64 pipe 2% -> 0.03%, no
time), 32/64/128-thread blocks, a power-of-two wrap, 8 x 8 bins, 64
registers again, waves of disjoint visits (host model: 993 k visits in
460 k waves; the grouping cost more than it saved), indices two batches
ahead: the last three under 3% in a row, the stop. NCU after: SM 52%
(the limiting unit), L2 46%, issue active 58%, SM active 90% of the
launch; latency bound on each pixel's dependent chain, not at a roofline.
In the pipeline's 32-frame launches one heavy tile still sets the length
(village SM active avg 237 k against max 897 k cycles): the follow-up.

Gates, the default and PERF=1 builds alike: the 90 dumps 90 of 90, render
quick 276 of 276 and 32 of 32 variants, judge quick 322 of 322, pipe-gate
OK 6008 frames and MESH=2 DRAW=1 OK (80346 of 80346 meshes); the quick
gates again in a fresh worktree; clangcheck ok. No divergences found.

is rb_mesh_cell for hidden cubes and render type 0 (rb_mesh_cell calls it

## 2026-09-29 play's live replay frees dead livings; the mesher's buffer is vanilla's (lane/playarena)

The deferred batch gates (batchgates/2026-09-29-0407) failed the sampled
render gate on three recordings, every device frame bit-exact: play, making
C's reference dumps, aborted on moon-swamp-s2 and swamp-night-s2 ("arena:
more than 65536 livings", rc 134) and exited on tnt-cannon-s1 ("raster:
mesher vertex buffer full", rc 1).

The livings were the server's, not the client's: the abort was the
spawner's living_alloc at row 555. play enabled the grave (grave.h, the
reclaimer of dead livings) only in --check and the judges; its live and
--replay loops never freed a dead or unloaded living, so a swamp's slimes
at full moon (seed 2) took every slot. play now enables it in every mode
(main, after the checks return). The first sweep then faulted: it read a
render thread's stack, whose guard page glibc 2.43 installs with
MADV_GUARD_INSTALL inside the rw-p mapping (test_interleave's grave_forbid
names the same fault). The sweep now reads /proc/self/pagemap beside each
mapping and skips pages with bit 58 (a guard region, Linux 6.15). And
grave_hold keeps sweeps off while the device renderer's plugin opens on a
thread of its own (dlopen and the device's context map and unmap memory
between the sweep's maps read and its scan); the thread ends the hold when
the open returns. tnt-cannon-s1 has a section of 3,739 cauldrons (about
164,000 vertices in the opaque pass); the mesher's buffer was 1<<20 ints,
half of Tessellator.instance's 2097152, which vanilla fills in one draw. It
is RB_TESS_CAP now (a pass past it still fails loudly: vanilla would draw
the full buffer and go on, which the mesher does not do).

Evidence: all 930 recordings the render gate samples (837 snapshots with
two sampled shots each, 93 frame judges' shots), master's play against
this one on the same shots: 928 give the same C frames and the same tapes
byte for byte, and the three that failed now run to the end (the others
of the three on master: rc 134, rc 1). cuda-render-check RENDER_ARGS="
--sample 2 snapshots/moon-swamp-s2 snapshots/swamp-night-s2
snapshots/tnt-cannon-s1": 6 of 6 frames and 24 of 24 variants bit-exact.
The pin: play_check.list's +live (and +live:T) lines run, after play's
--check, the render gate's own command over the whole tape (two render
threads, frames dumped after the last row and after rows T):
moon-swamp-s2 and swamp-night-s2 +live, tnt-cannon-s1 +live:68. master's
play fails all three there, this one passes (2.6, 4.1 and 0.6 s).

of the faults were memmove at the image heap's top: image_free hands a
freed block of more than a page back (MADV_DONTNEED; each call flushes the
TLB of every CPU the process runs on) and the block's next owner, mostly
raster_live_frame's 64 to 256 KB buffers, faults every page in again; the
rest is heap growth (rec_tex takes a new 512 KB copy of a texture patched
between uses in a frame). The step is not bound by that: the same 155 M
user instructions an env-step run at IPC 3.26 at N 16 and 0.73 at N 128
(111 k DRAM demand fills an env-step; frontend 27%, backend 54% of slots).

Tried and measured (every line in out/perf/pagefault.tsv; the patches in
out/perf/pagefault-*.patch): keeping a freed block's pages (cleared by
writes) cut faults 627/660/901 to 169/216/326 an env-step, the kernel's
share by half, TLB flushes 99.5% and L2 DTLB misses 75%, and made the
Nether's host step 7 to 14% slower (RSS +1.6 to 4.4 GB); budgets and
chain-depth limits, and clearing with streaming stores, did not recover
it: the kernel hands a fault a page it freed moments before on that CPU,
still in its caches, where a kept block's own pages have gone cold.
Releasing the step's freed blocks together (one process_madvise with
PIDFD_SELF at the step's end, one TLB flush; a block taken again in the
step cleared by writes) halved the faults and cut TLB flushes 97%, and
env-steps/s went -2.7, -3.5, -0.7% over three interleaved rounds. Sharing
the views' 700 KB of playview.so code between the env copies (each copy's
read-only segments mapped from the first copy's file) measured +0.6 to
+1.7% host, -0.3 to +1.1% device: noise. Per-worker CPU affinity: no
effect. None of these is kept.

What moved it: fewer workers. A sweep at N 128 (48, 56, 64, 72, 96, 128
workers) found 48 to 56 best: 64 cores and 128 hardware threads, and a
worker on a core's second thread made the same env-step cost 1.4 to 2.1
times the CPU for fewer env-steps (the tick is memory bound; the render
streams need cores too). native/runtime/pool.c pool_cores counts the
physical cores in the process's CPU mask (sysfs thread_siblings_list); the
pool's default workers are that many, the pipeline's that many less its
streams' threads (two a stream with the device meshing), at least half the
cores and at most one an env: 48 with host meshing, 56 with device meshing
at N 128 on the GPU host. pipe_bench takes the pipeline's default when -j is not
given. env-steps/s, N 128, PERF=1, tbench.sh 1 -big, two interleaved
rounds against master 96446b0a's default (128 workers), village / Nether /
exploring: host meshing 2100 / 2356 / 1726 to 2288 / 2624 / 1818 (+9.0,
+11.4, +5.3%); device meshing 2574 / 2939 / 2020 to 2793 / 3108 / 2160
(+8.5, +5.8, +6.9%); CPU per env-step 43.7 / 37.7 / 58.2 to 20.7 / 19.0 /
27.2 ms host, 23.3 / 19.1 / 34.5 to 16.6 / 13.6 / 23.7 device. Against

steps of village: cumesh_run 6.67 s of kernel time (87.9%) to 1.34 s
(59.6%). What changed, one step at a time (out/perf/perfmesh.tsv, every
attempt with its numbers, kept or not):

- The baseline drew a section on lane 0 alone (1.9 threads a warp active,
  210 registers, the SMs idle half of each launch). A block of 4 warps now
  meshes a section: the cells are cut into 128 runs and each lane draws its
  run from a guessed start state (the one cell before the run drawn from
  the section's start), then every start is checked, word for word,
  against the lane before's end state (the 112 mesher words a draw writes,
  the Tessellator's translation and normal; the other mesher words are
  checked once against the template, CUMESH_ERR_STATE), and a lane with a
  wrong start draws again from the right one. The Tessellator's texture
  coordinates, colour, brightness and has_* flags only reach a written
  vertex, so the counts never depend on them: each lane runs with them at a
  mark, and the values it starts with are resolved from the nearest lane
  before that set them. Over the gates' recordings 0 to 128 lane redraws.
- One mesh pass instead of two: each lane draws its run once, into a
  512-vertex buffer of a pool (one slot a resident block), and once the
  counts are known copies its vertices into a launch-wide vertex buffer,
  giving each marked field its resolved value; the write pass is a copy.
- Slot pools grow in one allocation per feed, not one per 128 bands.
- Two bugs on the way: clang does not treat plain C functions as
  convergent on nvptx, so it sank a shuffle into a branch (meshdev.c is
  built -fconvergent-functions); and reading struct words through a
  uint32_t pointer broke C's aliasing rule, so fields came back stale
  (memcpy now). And one in the C: rb3_render_cocoa cached its icons in a
  function static, one for every device thread, read half filled: the
  explore crash (the baseline's too). The icons are looked up each time,
  mesh.mk fails a build whose device code keeps a writable global (a

env-step at about 50 us of thread time each). pipe_bench's "upload"
device-ms was the device waiting for that staging between two events, not
PCIe: 1.7 to 2.3 MB cross an env-step (about 3 GB/s at the new rates, 0.07
ms of copies an env-step). Changes:
- cuda/render/render.cu (host side only, no kernel signature changed):
  every region a render uploads is staged in one pinned buffer and goes
  over in one cudaMemcpyAsync into a device staging buffer (d_up) that the
  per-render arrays point into; fresh meshes and pool textures go from it
  to their arenas in one k_scatter launch; the atlas patch and the water
  order run after the copy; the per-group event wait that only fed the
  timing stats is gone (each group's events are read after the render's
  last wait); the host lists keep their capacity across renders.
- runtime/pipeline.c: a stream's render takes every frame queued (B is
  what it waits for, not what it takes). Defaults: host meshing, a stream
  per 8 envs (at most 16) with B 1; device meshing, a stream per 32 envs
  (at most 4) with whole batches. pipe_tune sweeps 1 to 16 streams with B
  1 or all, one unmeasured step after each change (new streams resend
  every mesh).

## 2026-09-29 The device renderer's performance phase, and the entity quads' upload (lane/perfrender)

Measured on the GPU host's GPU 1 (RTX PRO 6000, sm_120) with pipe_bench --kinds
village,nether,explore --ns 128 -j 64 under tbench.sh -big, before and
after at the same host load (about 27): env-steps/s went from 914, 776,
711 (perf-base-mesh; perf-base 936, 810, 732) to 1415, 1131, 946
(+55%, +46%, +33%); the render's device time per frame from 0.268,
0.184, 0.152 ms to 0.090, 0.061, 0.069 ms; the entity quads uploaded per
env-step from 905, 990, 928 KB to 432, 473, 443 KB. nsys over the same
run: every renderer kernel 4628 ms before, 1710 ms after (k_raster 3352
-> 998). Every step, kept or not, is a row of out/perf/perfrender.tsv
with the NCU verdicts; out/perf/perfrender.png the picture.

What limited it, in order:
- The render ran in about 18 groups of about 10 envs each: the
  pipeline's 128 MB arena held that many envs' triangles, and a group is a
  host wait plus a raster launch whose time is its slowest tile's (1.5 ms
  whatever its size). arena_fit grows the triangle and pair buffers a
  quarter over what a render needs while the device has 1 GB to spare;
  one group a render: device time 0.266 -> 0.114 ms an env-step.
- The entity quads: render_batch copied every env's raster_obs_equad
  array (360 bytes a quad, 58 MB a 64-frame village render) into a vector
  grown each render and then into the stage, 37.5 of the stream thread's
  62 ms upload phase. A quad goes up as a cquad (172 bytes: the fields the
  device reads before e_screen writes the rest; colour and alpha in a side
  record only for the states that read them, vertex_color, vertex_alpha,
  blend 6), written straight into the stage over up to 8 threads:
  env-steps/s 980 -> 1431 village. Sending only the quads that changed is
  no use: 0.1% of a slot's quads are byte-identical to its previous
  frame's (1.94 M quads over 60 village renders), the camera and the mobs
  move every step. What is left of the upload phase is the meshes (16.4 of
  about 24 ms a village render; lane/perfoverlap's).
- The kernels: k_raster's warps ballot which of the batch's triangles
  meet their 8 x 4 pixels (instructions 1.6 G -> 0.77 G a render);
  triangles padded to 240 bytes, written and staged as uint4s; the
  clippers swap their polygon buffers instead of copying them back;
  k_key_runs (tile runs from the sorted keys) replaces an atomic count and
  a scan; the clip list's launch walks the device's count with 1024
  blocks instead of 3.3 M mostly idle threads; k_raster held to 64
  registers (__launch_bounds__(TILE_PX, 4)): the split's unit build gave
  it 104, two blocks an SM, 25% slower. Tried and dropped: warps walking
  their tile's list without the block barrier (from global memory 14%
  slower, through per-warp shared memory 6% slower: a block ends with its
  slowest warp), uint4 mesh loads (1%).

NCU verdicts (PERF=1): k_raster (58% of the render's device time) is
latency bound, SM 15%, memory 11%: each pixel walks its tile's triangles
in draw order and the heaviest tile (about 4000 triangles against a mean
of 500) sets the launch's length (one SM 6.8 M cycles, the average 4.4 M);
three attempts in a row gained under 3%. k_quads' write pass (18%): DRAM
48%, latency bound on the mesh reads. The clip lists' two passes (7%, 6%):
L2 58 and 65%. k_quads' count pass (5%): DRAM 85%, at its roofline.

Gates, the default (-Xcicc -O1) and the PERF=1 build alike: render quick

## 2026-09-28 Section meshing on the device, byte for byte the host's (lane/gpumesh)

The observation's section meshes are now made on the 3090. The device
mesher is not a port: native/cuda/mesh/mesh.mk compiles render_blocks.c,
render_blocks2.c, render_blocks3.c, blocks_table.c and noise.c for the
device as they are (clang 21 to nvptx64 bitcode, linked with meshdev.c's
runtime and kernels, internalized, llc with no FMA, ptxas --fmad=false),
so every render type is there and a C fix reaches the device at the next
build. Four hooks in the C: a Tessellator without a buffer counts vertices
(the count pass sizes each section's arena block), libm's cos, sin and
atan2 go through rb_cos, rb_sin and rb_atan2 (the device looks up glibc's
values: the liquids' flow angles over every level sum and the brewing
stands' arms once, a sunflower's head per request), the two Perlin
generators sit behind pointers, and rb_mesh_section is begin, cell kind
and cell (a warp meshes a section: its lanes classify 32 cells at a time,
air, other pass and hidden cubes, and lane 0 draws the rest in order).
The host sends each frame a feed (src/meshfeed.[ch]): the stale sections
as requests, and the chunk bands and headers the device slot lacks, kept
current by the renderer's own stale marks and a compare of height maps,
masks and biomes; a section reads its 3x3 chunks. raster_live_device_mesh
(0 host, 1 device, 2 both) sets where; play --obs-mesh 2 dumps feeds, the
pipeline's views send them (pipe_config.device_mesh), the renderer counts,
allocates, writes and sorts translucent quads on the device, feeds counts
back and resyncs a view whose meshes it lost. Gates: every frame judge's

device section meshes equal to the host's in the fields the Tessellator
wrote, 1,694 of 1,694 frames bit-exact drawn with the device's meshes;

## 2026-09-29 The client world's light on the device, exact (lane/cwlight)

D8 as the design review put it (out/plan/gpu-design-2026-09-28.md part 3
item 3): the tick records the client world's light calls and the device runs
them before the frame. The premise was that nothing in the tick reads that
light but the frame. For the rows it holds: `test_snapshots --light-defer
never` (every client world call and relight check recorded, never run)
replays all 837 recordings with every row equal. For the light itself it
does not: the client's own block writes read it. Chunk.func_150807_a's
propagateSkylightOcclusion test reads the cell's light, a write reads the
band storage a light write may have made, and Chunk.relightBlock's
markBlocksDirtyVertical calls must run before its own height and sky writes
(idx-cwlight-s1 row 19 took 51 more light writes without that). Play reads
it too (entity, particle and HUD brightness, the mesher's bands). So the
calls go to the device and those reads stay on the host, behind a sync:
src/lightdefer.[ch] keeps the pending list, world.c syncs before every
client chunk write, inside relight_block, before the propagate test, at a
light read and at the frame, and the executor runs the list. With C as the
executor, all 837 recordings give every row's client light digest
(tests/cwdigest.h: light, band storage, heights, stamps, write sequences,
the world's epoch) equal to the immediate run's: 1,988,264 rows, 16.0 M
calls and 17.0 M relight checks deferred, 3.29 M syncs (1.97 M at row
ends, 1.30 M before client writes, 24.6 k at light reads). Syncing only at
row ends leaves 90 of 837 right; without the read syncs 834 (cov-blkplace-s1,
cov-glowstone-s1, pickblock-s1 need the propagate test's). The device
executor is L16's kernel in a deferred mode (LC_F_AUTH records: the

## 2026-09-28 The pipeline: the pool's worlds drawn on the device, bit-exact against play's frame (lane/pipeline)

The two halves of the RL product run as one pipeline on the dev host
(native/runtime/pipeline.[ch], the trainer's C API: pipe_make, pipe_reset,
pipe_step for any subset, pipe_poll for the first b done, each result the
pool's HUD numbers, flags and events and the observation's place in one
device buffer uint8 [depth][N][128][128][3]). The observation is play's
world frame: play.c builds as a library (-DPLAY_VIEW, playview.h) and each
env loads a private copy of it with the renderer's files
(out/runtime/playview.so via memfd; their statics are the env's view), run
by pool hooks around each tick, after a reset and at the step's end; the
frame is recorded, not rasterized (raster_rec_set_only), and the device
renderer draws it from meshes kept per section version, per-env atlases and
the recorded entity passes. Groups of envs are resident on S streams (a
host thread, a CUDA stream and a renderer each); a stream's batch goes at B
frames or when all its envs in flight have queued; frames rotate over depth
slots; pipe_tune sweeps S and B at startup. Meshing stays on the host by
measurement: it is the only bit-exact mesher and costs 36 to 622 M
instructions per env-step against a 19 to 84 M tick when the agent moves,
so a device port is the next step. Device: a render makes 3 host round
trips instead of about 20 (each 18 ms on today's shared 3090), the mesh
arena frees and reuses blocks (it restarted 11 times in 40 renders), waits
sleep (the stream threads spun at 100%). Host: the views share one parse of
hud_live's item table (341 MB per env to 149), and the mesher skips buried
opaque cubes (frame recording 137 M to 76 M a step; test_meshes 0 bad, and
every section of the gate's 29 recordings meshed both ways in play,
identical). The gate (native/runtime/pipe_gate.c, pipeline_gate.list):
29 recordings over the three dimensions at N = 16, groups of 4 on 2
streams, 23,987 rows equal to test_snapshots and 6,008 device frames
bit-exact against the C renderer and equal to play's own frames at the
same ticks. It found three divergences in the lane's first run (native/tests/divergences/
pipeline.tsv): play's renderer hook read the stale view dimension at a
respawn tick, drawing the dials' Math.random off the surface (cp-end-s1,
d.cmath) and reading the fog's light in the old dimension's server world,
which generated a chunk there (nether-fight-s1, w.ents); and device meshes
keyed by a per-renderer version met an old mesh after a dimension change
(nether-trip2-s42, fixed by process-wide versions). Measured beside other
lanes (host load 105 to 135, the 3090 at 97 to 100%): 58/114/302 (village),
57/99/393 (Nether), 49/40/291 (exploring) env-steps/s with observations at
N = 16/64/128; the device path bounds at N = 16 and 64, the host's mesher
bounds exploring. The device renderer is under the mirror rule (master's
RENDER entry in native/cuda/mirror.tsv, with this lane's root
raster_live_frame and host-data cuts; mirror.py on 81bf49ff names it). After merging master a fourth cause showed:

rendertick/anim_liquids). Merging lane/gpujudge's render.cu kept its

build at the end (lane/cudasplit adds the switch to every CUDA build and

## 2026-09-28 Builds from caches, links in one step per area (lane/trialcache)

A fresh checkout no longer rebuilds what has not changed. Every C compile
goes through ccache (~/.cache/ccache) and objects no longer name their
checkout (a relative -include, -fdebug-prefix-map=CURDIR=.), so one tree's
compile serves another's: 476 objects (engine, tests, play, fncov, CUDA
host, runtime) built without ccache, through a cold cache and through a warm
one in three checkouts are byte-equal, and fnkey check replays the same
507 of 2,099 jobs on master's old build and this one (FNKEY_GLOBAL keeps
its string; the region cache's hash is unchanged). A full Java build's
classes go to a class store (java/tests/classtore.sh, keyed by the harness
id and every source's path and SHA-1, javac and its flags); a build of
those exact sources unpacks them instead of running javac (a byte moved
across a file boundary keeps the harness id and misses). Found on the way:
make re-ran `command -v` and uname at every compile and link (recursive ?=
variables), every test object recompiled when the library changed, and
make lane's copied builds were always rebuilt (the flags stamp named the
checkout, touch ordered them badly). A fresh worktree's java, native and
play went from 9.2 to 31.9, 26.5 to 43.8 and 5.1 to 6.5 s to 1.2 to 2.0,
5.7 to 13.1 and 0.3 to 0.8 s (load 100 to 140; 0.1, 1.1, 0.1 s at load 42).
lane-share and the trial's links take one ln per area: 24.4 s to 1.3 s
(lane-share, load 70), 48.2 s to 2.1 s (trymerge with two lanes, load 100).

## 2026-09-28 L16 repaired, and the mirror rule: a C change cannot break its device kernel unseen (lane/gpumirror)

L16 (the light engine on the device) had failed on master since 4ab41c3b
(lane/idxclient, 2026-09-27 3:49 pm), which made a client world's 17-block
box test always true (ChunkProviderClient.chunkExists, world.c
chunks_exist_box) without telling the kernel. The capture's call record
now carries the world's is_remote (lc_call.remote, the old pad0); the
kernel's box test is its y test alone on a remote world, and its sky read
of a chunk the client lacks is false (EmptyChunk) instead of an error.
The full light-check over every recording then found three more exact
gaps in the kernel that the recordings of 2026-09-26 never reached: C's
chunk_touch sets the chunk's stamp, write sequence and edge stamps while
the device took the largest (wrong where a chunk's stamps exceed the
world's epoch, as the client world's copies of the server's chunks do:
fight-ghast-s42, nf-blaze-s42, fight-blaze-s42, nf-mobs-s42; the record's
first write of each is now cleared first); a neighbour read clamped at y
255 or 0 is the cell itself, which C has just written (chat-build-s1);
and the entry whose write makes a section reads its neighbours after the
section exists and the chunk's sky is regenerated (explore-long-s1, record
2,423,798). The queue's 32,768 cap was already handled as C handles it and
is now exercised: 1,298 calls hit it on the plan's recordings, all
byte-equal. The capture counts the client world's calls (light_check.sh
prints them), and light_check.sh retries a run the shared 3090 had no
memory for (58 of the first full run's failures were a co-tenant's memory,
"culight: mirror: out of memory").

The mirror rule (GPU design part 6): native/cuda/mirror.tsv names each
device kernel (L16 light, L15 generation; L17's lines are ready, commented,
for lane/gpus6b), the C it mirrors (roots and cuts; the mirrored set is
their closure over direct calls, macros, tables and enum constants: L16 73
items, L15 344), the files whose any change counts (the port, the capture,
the gate scripts), a build, a quick gate and the nightly's full gates.
native/cuda/mirror.py parses native/src at two revisions into top-level
items (comments and whitespace do not count), finds the changed ones and
prints the gates of every kernel they reach; its function ranges agree with
gcc's -fcallgraph-info start lines on all 6,465 functions (--verify-ci).
`make -C native mirror-gates [BASE=] [REV=] [RUN=1] [FULL=1]` and
`mirror-check`. cuda-chunkgen-check and cuda-dimgen-check take DUMPS= and
SPAWNS= for L15's quick gate. On 4ab41c3b^..4ab41c3b the script names L16
(chunks_exist_box, world_check_chunks_exist, generate_skylight_map,
chunk_height_map); 4ab41c3b's own tree fails light-check on all five quick
recordings ("return value: device 0, C 1") and passes all five with the
first repair commit on top. On master's merge of lane/rlfuzz2 (72 changed C
items) it names nothing. The trial and nightly wiring are untracked
(out/flywheel/bin): the trymerge.sh patch runs mirror.py --check and the
reached kernels' build and quick gate beside the suite and refuses the
merge (rc 3) on a failure (proven in a scratch trial tree: a lane that
drops the kernel's remote test is refused); automerge.sh reruns them when
master moved in code under the trial; mirrornightly.sh runs every full gate
of master in a scratch worktree and logs one line a night.

Evidence: light-check over all recordings on the lane (784): 723 OK on
the first run, 58 lost to a co-tenant's device memory and rerun OK, 6
differing and fixed above. After the last fix, on the tree merged with
lane/chunkspeed (which changed world.c's light pass; the rule named L16 and

## 2026-09-28 lane/replaylat: a short replay's fixed cost

Where a short oracle replay's wall time goes, end to end, and the biggest
costs removed; rows, frames and saves unchanged. `--tick-profile` now also
prints ORACLE PROFILE PHASES, the run's timeline from the JVM's start (or a
pool job's arrival): jvm, client, pool, save, spawn (the server's world load
and spawn area), poll, join, loop, end. Found and fixed:

- The harness id was a recursive make variable: every use re-read the 1,400
  sources through cat and sha1sum, 5 or 6 times per `make replay`, 1 to 4 s
  before a member even got the job at load 80 to 120. It is now computed
  once per make and cached in out/java/harness.id against the sources'
  paths, sizes and mtimes (java/tests/harness.sh): 0.05 to 0.2 s.
- WorldServer.getPendingBlockUpdates walks the whole pending-tick set for
  every chunk it saves, and a fresh world unloads (and saves) its 336
  chunks outside 128 blocks of spawn over the first ticks: a third of a
  warm member's server thread in a seed-start replay (JFR, act2-bisect x5:
  655 of 1,970 samples). A one-line hook hands a save's call
  (remove=false, no tick in progress) to netherite.oracle.PendingTicks, an
  index valid while the set's TreeMap modCount holds, returning the same
  list (checked against vanilla's scan on 1,286 calls before the check was
  removed). Server-thread samples for the same five runs: 1,970 to 1,467.
- Minecraft.launchIntegratedServer polled the server's start every 200 ms
  (0.13 to 0.32 s a launch); Oracle.launchWait polls every 5 ms in agent
  mode (nothing is drawn: the loading screen's clock is the tick's).
- A pool member prelaunches the last job's world 300 ms after it; a job for
  another world then waited for the whole spawn area before its own launch
  (1.8 to 3.6 s in the A/B; 1,226 of master's 1,540 prelaunches were never
  taken). The member now reads a job that arrives during a prelaunch at
  once (from the launch poll) and, unless it likely runs the same world
  (same world flags, world.conf text, replay header world fields), gives
  the prelaunch up there (the server stops within a chunk, saves nothing);
  a same-world job waits for it and takes it as before. No prelaunch after
  a --save-at-end replay: the next run starts from its checkpoint.
- Members run -XX:+DisableExplicitGC, so nothing collected the old
  generation until it was full: each job's world was promoted, the heap
  grew into new pages and a member retired at 2,500 MB after 6 to 20 jobs
  (a new one takes 25 to 300 s at load 100 to 160, its callers run fresh
  JVMs meanwhile). Between jobs the member now runs a full collection (the
  DiagnosticCommand heap histogram) once the garbage since the last one is
  a third of the old generation: members lived 40 to 90 jobs in the
  selfcheck. They still grow: they keep some of their jobs' worlds live
  (master's too: 1,250 to 1,875 chunks after 2 to 12 jobs), a follow-up.
- poolauto: a run that finds every live member busy waits up to 15 s for
  one before a fresh JVM (20 to 180 s at load 100 to 160), and up to 3
  members of a key start at once.

Breakdown (medians, s; master b998b211 with only the PHASES stamps, and this
lane, each on its own tree-local member, interleaved, load 80 to 100):
act2-bisect warm 4.74 -> 4.15 (spawn 3.26 -> 2.89, the rest 1.5 -> 1.3),
pf-blazefall-g7 warm 3.37 -> 2.54, gold-g6-s42 warm 6.66 -> 5.32; fresh
10.39 -> 9.15, 8.82 -> 8.61, 12.50 -> 13.34. Sixteen short recordings,
warm, interleaved (load 86 to 118): median 4.79 -> 3.54 s. Not halved: what
is left of a seed-start short replay is its spawn area (625 chunks
generated, populated and lit, the same work a fresh JVM does, 2.5 to 3.5 s
at this load) and its ticks; everything else is 0.1 to 0.3 s.

Selfcheck J=8, each on a private pool home: master 782/782 OK, 16,791
replay-seconds, wall 2,213 s at mean load 96 (88 fresh runs, 6,985 s);
this lane before the poolauto change 782/782, 13,430 s, 1,884 s at load
146 (63 fresh, 2,014 s); with it 782/782, 15,647 s, 2,236 s at load 156
(20 fresh, 3,603 s); the merged tree (harness fd165030be5a) 784/784
OK, 22,910 s, 3,011 s at load 173 (12 fresh). make -C java gate 5/5;
pool-proof on the merged tree: 9 re-records, 7 replays and 3 session-check
saves (saveend mode) through a member equal fresh JVMs in every file and

## 2026-09-28 The env pool: N envs of the C engine in one process, reset by image copy, stepped on worker threads (lane/envpool)

native/runtime/pool.[ch] (rules in native/runtime/pool.mk, the dev host only) is
the host half of the RL product (D1): pool_make(N, world.conf, obs spec),
pool_start_load (a snapshot directory, a checkpoint start's included, loaded
once into an env image), pool_reset (each env becomes a copy of the start's
image), pool_step (n ticks per env, queued to worker threads) and pool_poll
(the first B envs whose step finished; the rest keep running). A start is
loaded twice at two addresses (L12's twin): the words that point into the
image and differ between the two by the image's move are its pointers
(5,400 to 514,000 per start; over 40 starts 0 words name memory outside the
image and 0 other words differ), and a reset copies the start's nonzero page
runs (18 to 153 MB) into the env's own image, rebases those words and gives
back the env's other written pages: 3.5 to 8.5 M user instructions and 20
to 45 ms for one env (a load from disk is 0.4 to 1.4 s). Each env keeps its
own randomness and order, so a step's result does not depend on the thread
count or the envs beside it. Acts are a tape row, a tape-form act, or java
Act.java's agent form (holds, presses, look or dlook, hotbar, ctrl, gui
ops): native/src/act_agent.c resolves it inside the client tick where the
oracle runs Act.applyGui and Act.applyInput (struct act_agent on the act),
and the pool resolves the look and parseAgent's refusals before it;
refusals are flags (PF_REFUSED: no tick; PF_OPS_REFUSED with the count). A
step returns the HUD as numbers (health, food, armour, air, XP level and bar,
the selected slot, the nine hotbar stacks, the screen, its slots and cursor),
the client's stat and achievement increments, PF_DEAD and PF_DIED (the env
keeps running; the respawn op respawns it), privileged state behind a flag,
and the render feed (feed.c; pool.h struct pool_feed, for lane/gpurender:
one block of plain data, the camera at partial tick 1.0, the sections whose
blocks or light changed since the last feed, the chunk loads and unloads of
the render range, the entity draw list).

The gate, native/runtime/pool_gate.c: native/tests/rowrec.h writes every
field test_snapshots compares, one line per row, and the end state
(test_snapshots --row-dump FILE); every env's rows must equal those lines.
Engine fixes it found, in the ledger (native/tests/divergences/envpool.tsv):
collide_env_init set the chest and ladder bounds of the current env, not the
new one, so every env_new env (test_interleave, test_relocate, the pool) had
zero-size chest and ladder boxes (s1chain-S8 row 12, a bat through a
dungeon chest; cov-villagerep-s42 row 225); in the agent form, where a tape's
resolved input no longer hides them, the credits respawn sent an S09 that
vanilla's respawnPlayer does not (end-exit-s1 row 1297), and a closed
container screen skipped setIngameFocus (achieve-s1 row 666). For envs on
several threads: the nbtjson interned keys take a lock on a miss, the grave
sweeps an image env's own memory with thread-local scratch
(grave_enable_images), 512 image slots.

Gates (40 recordings in native/runtime/pool_gate.list: explore-long-s1,
villages, fights, deaths and respawns, Nether trips and the fortress, the
End and the dragon; load average 150 to 260): on the tree merged with master
(c0287b6c), tape rows at N = 64 on 32 threads, 128 episodes, 437,164 rows
equal (explore-long-s1 four times; peak RSS 10.0 GB), and at N = 1 on 1

The render feed (--feed, N = 16, 28 recordings, 31,496 rows): every env's

## 2026-09-28 chunk loading a third cheaper: the light window, one biome run a chunk, lazy limit noise (lane/chunkspeed)

explore-long-s1 (30,100 rows walking into new terrain, the merge trial's
longest job) replays with the same rows, writes and light as before in a
third fewer instructions. Measured on the dev host, master b998b211 against this
lane, both replays run at the same time (load about 130): 1,371.8 G user
instructions to 927.7 G (-32.4%), 698.1 G user cycles to 512.5 G (-26.6%),
143.2 s user to 105.2 s (-26.5%), 299.9 s wall to 212.4 s. The phase
profiler's tick instructions: 1,312.7 G to 868.1 G (-33.9%); ~LIGHT 358.3 G
to 111.3 G, ~GEN 357.3 G to 229.8 G, ~POP 339.3 G to 247.1 G, the client's
C2 214.6 G to 45.5 G, S2 472.8 G to 332.6 G, S6 289.8 G to 200.4 G; the
worst tick (row 719) 7.68 G to 5.31 G; allocations per tick 276 to 177.

The light engine (world.c) reads chunks through a per-world window (struct
world lwin: the refs of the 8x8 chunks around a pass's origin, each looked
up once; map_ver, bumped by every insertion and removal, drops it; kept
across moves) and memoizes the last doChunksNearChunkExist box; lp_pass is
updateLightByType specialized on the type and inlined, reusing
computeLightValue's six reads for the spread. The client's gap relight
floods into chunks it does not have (no_generate: they read 0 and drop
writes; 404 M of 3,000 rows' client reads were such cells): those cells run
a path that reads only their cross-chunk neighbours. Generation: one biome
layer run per chunk (biomes_chunk: the voronoi's 6x6 parent sits inside the
10x10 generation area, and a layer's cell depends only on the cell), the
two 16-octave limit noises computed only where denormalize_clamp reads them
(octaves_3d_need, with the y cell's corner gradients taken at the cell's
first y as NoiseGeneratorImproved does), the surface pass stepping the seed
alone above y 4 (nextInt(5) cannot reach there; its three rejected values
redraw), chunk_construct one pass per band, the sky map by band pointer.
Population: world_get_block and world_get_meta inline on a near-cache hit,
ore rows scanned from their ends (the test is monotone along a row), and
the hot strcmp material and rail tests replaced by indices built before
main. Still the floor: entity AI's getEntitiesWithinAABB (an_collect, 13.5%
of the run's cycles), the replay's digests, the noise and RNG arithmetic
Java defines, and MapGenCaves re-walking every tunnel for each of the 289
chunks around it (follow-ups in the report). genahead with the C generator
serves all 30,087 overworld generations (8,802 made and dropped); its
generator calls take 28 s of a 136 s replay, the part worker threads could
take off the step (not done).

Checks: `make -s -C native test` rc 0 on the merged tree (798 snapshot
replays OK, no FAIL); the chunk stage tests (test_worldgen over the 23
out/java/chunks dumps) PASS; globals, order and stack clean; callgraph
reports one TICK cycle from master's hardeggs commit (zombie jockey eggs,
not touched here); cuda-chunkgen builds; clangcheck ok; index/check.py 0
errors.

## 2026-09-28 pool members run the session checks' Save and Quit and diverge's snapshots (lane/poolsave)

A played session's check (native/play/session.sh: make replay SAVEEND=cp
SAVEPRE=0) always went to a fresh JVM: Main.configurePool and pool.sh's
never() refused --save-at-end by rule (4,978 refusals in the shared
members' logs; lane/chainfuzz3 paid 22.9 s a check for 250-tick
sessions). Nothing in a member stopped it: the replay's saveAtEnd branch
is the Checkpoint.save that a script's {"cmd":"save"} already runs
pooled, and the teardown already handles a server the save stopped. The
one real hazard was the prelaunch: after a job, Pool.cycle parses the
last job's arguments again to launch its world, and resetArgs did not
put saveAtEnd, saveNoPre, snapTicks, snapDir, snapPlain, detailFrom,
untilTick or rerecordClient back, so a plain replay that took the
prelaunched world saved into the last job's checkpoint (negative control
with the old list: "checkpoint already exists", rc 2). Pool.ORACLE_ARGS
now lists them, resetArgs clears the netherite.enbt property that
--detail-from sets mid-run, and members take --save-at-end, --snap-at,
--detail-from and --until (diverge's and the keyframes' replays; 792
--snap-at refusals). session.sh's POOL=0 POOLAUTO=0 retry of the next
start is gone: it came in before lane/poolfix (a member that answered rc
0 without its Snapshot after an OOM), which since makes any thrown job or
OOM a POOL-FAULT that make reruns fresh; the manifest check after it
still fails the session loudly, and none of the 36 session logs on
The dev host had it fire. POOLMAX is now derived from the memory: half the
memslot budget over POOLMAXMB (the dev host 12; poolauto's half-budget rule
stops 2.7 GB members at 11), or a quarter of the RAM without a budget (a
16 GB Mac 1, 32 GB 3). pool-proof.sh gains `saveend MODE ROOT TAPE...`
(the saving replay, then the same tape without SAVEEND a second later,
so it takes the world the member prelaunched from the saving run) and
SNAPAT/RARGS on replay.

game-s1-1, 2346 ticks; pf-g29-2901-s1-1 in the End; chainfuzz3's

## 2026-09-28 The merge trial's self-check replays only what a change can reach (lane/selfselect)

`make -C java selfcheck SELECT=1 [COV=dir]` replays only the stored
recordings that ran code changed since a coverage data set was made
(java/tests/SelfSelect.java through selfcheck.sh --select). JaCoCo now
instruments netherite.* beside net.minecraft.* (COVOPTS), so a harness change
maps by method too; CovReport keeps mods/ in the per-recording data only and
marks a recording whose data has classes of another build (recs/NAME.stale).
make coverage also writes fingerprints.tsv (per class a header hash:
supertypes, annotations, instance fields in order; per static field and per
method a hash of its declaration and resolved bytecode, debug attributes and
frames left out), inputs.tsv (tests/selinputs.sh: the dry-run replay recipe,
blanks squeezed, and the pool scripts) and state. A recording is picked when
it ran a changed or removed method, or any method of a class touched as a
whole or of its subclasses: a changed header, instance field or static
field, a new constant or hiding field, a new static initializer, or a new
member that overrides or hides a supertype's (our fingerprints, then the JDK
and libraries by reflection). New, not-OK and stale recordings are always
picked. It runs every recording, with a FALLBACK line, when the replay recipe
or pool scripts differ, a pool class changes (Pool, Rewind, PoolAgent,
PoolGl, PoolMouse run outside the job's coverage window) or a class or method in
tests/selfselect.racy changes (thread-timing coverage from lane/covcache's
proof, plus the pooled-vs-fresh gap measured here: 45 pooled recordings
against fresh coverage of the same harness, 276 fresh-only method
sightings, every one on the list). Stale coverage is sound, only wider: the
selection maps everything changed since the data's tree.

History proof (java/tests/selhist.sh, selhist-eval.sh): 13 oracle trees from
c996bbc6^1 to 9e64d273 replayed fresh with JaCoCo (each merge's recordings
by their move-in time, plus the six pre-pin tapes and pf-deadtrade-g7's
pre-agentscreens tape), 7,316 replays in about 6.5 h at load 75 to 155.
Over the 12 Java-changing merges (clientrand, agentscreens and the ten since
the self-check): 6,444 recordings judged, 9 changed outcome (the six pre-pin
tapes at c996bbc6, pf-deadtrade-g7 at b6398fb6 t=280, two FAIL-to-OK at
05847e58), 9 selected, 0 misses; 4,749 selected (73.7%, 73.8% of the replay
seconds). 39f2a890, 7c254f9a (seed1chain's GoldBot) and d21aae26 (chainfuzz's
Snapshot.structures) select none; 4 merges fall back (pool classes or
scripts); the rest change code every replay runs (Main.configure,
Oracle.commands, Coverage.dump, Act.<init>, Block's collision box). A

## 2026-09-28 Agent-form fuzzing: RL-policy inputs and what they broke (lane/rlfuzz)

native/tests/playfuzz/agentgen.py writes RL-policy-shaped agent scripts
(per-tick chords, press bursts, hotbar keys, look deltas up to 180
degrees, pitch at its limits, gui ops in any state including the refused
ones, portals, long idles, input under open screens; dev kits on dev
starts), and agentrun.sh records each on the Java oracle (`make -C java
script`) from a seed-1 start or a seed-42 checkpoint and checks it row by
row (test_snapshots and play_check.sh), one results.tsv line per case.
628 case runs checked 1,835,006 rows. The pass rate went 5/12, 30/46,
26/40, 33/40, 36/40, 89/100, 94/100, then 97/100 on each of two fresh
rounds (seeds 701..900: 200 cases, 663,751 rows); 4 of those 6 are fixed.

The causes, each with its vanilla source: tracker timing (a portal
traveller's S13 goes through the player's destroyedItemsNetCache and is
sent by the player's own onUpdate, this tick when the traveller was ahead
of it, else the next; Java has a tracker per world, so the old instance is
tracked anew in the destination; an egg hatchling's S0F is sent at the
spawn, before its first move; func_85172_a shows a chunk's dead items),
the client world (an ageable's copy spawns at the constructor size and
setScaleForAge shrinks the box from its min corner, off centre for the pick
until the next move, which starts from the centred box: moving the copy
the way the skewed box implies made pix-sheared-s1's frame worse; every S08 of a pump gets its C06, five pearls in one tick
included; an S07 into another dimension closes an inventory or container
screen; the instant break sends no C07 2; the dig tick over a block gone
to air does nothing), shared block bounds (the ladder's, like the
fences': a meta outside 2..5 reports the last ladder's; Snapshot.java's
blockBounds carries it), canEntityBeSeen's ray trace on a C02 interact
(it writes a Teleporter portal's axis meta), repeated onDeath (no
once-only gate), and the Nether's and End's own lists and pools. Where
lane/playfuzz2 fixed the same bug differently (the window mirror, the
twin's list place, placement boxes, the client blaze fall), master's is
kept. The enderman scream fix (a scream set and reset in one tick dirties
the watcher, so the tracker's update runs) made g14-583's rows exact but
moved the client copies in the cr-sweep g10, g14 and g23 golden frames
where Java's stay still (pxdiff: the enderman's legs mid-stride against
straight in the golden); it is reverted and g14-583 is open again. 73
fixed cases are pinned: scripts in native/tests/playfuzz/agentpins/
(agentpins.txt), whole recordings out/java/snapshots/rf-* (950 MB). Open,
with their rows in out/report.md: s1-814 (the client placement precheck
reads BlockStairs' bounds after native's mouseover, Java's after a
collision), g14-583, s1-803, s1-520, s1-509, s1-644, g16-135, g25-234,

## 2026-09-28 the native client's input fuzzed against the Java client: generated sessions, eleven divergences (lane/rawfuzz)

native/tests/rawfuzz/gen.py writes a seeded stand-in person as a RawDrive
step list: walking with W A S D held, swapped and tapped (sometimes inside
one frame), sprinting by control or a double W, sneaking, jumps, a mouse
that flicks with an overshoot, drifts and sweeps past the pitch limits, the
hotbar keys and the wheel (several in a frame), Q and Q with either control,
mining, placing and eating, fights, the middle button, F1, F3 (with shift,
H, B, F, A, P) and F5, one-frame chords of keys, buttons and the wheel,
towers and falls, and every container gesture (left, right, middle and side
clicks at an offset inside the slot, shift with either shift key before or
in the click's frame, left and right drags gliding over slots, double
clicks, number keys and Q or control-Q over a hovered slot, clicks outside,
pointer wandering, the wheel, closing with E or Escape mid-drag or with a
key held); a fresh start first chops logs and crafts planks and a table, a
checkpoint start builds a table and a chest or a furnace from its planks
and opens them. RawDrive gained the steps this needs (hover, point, glide,
slot offsets and paces, finditem by index, close with a key, tap only under
a screen, a press without motion), X's autorepeat for held keys (660 ms,
25 a second, what LWJGL queues flagged repeat), and the death screen (R,
then the Respawn button). native/tests/rawfuzz/run.sh plays each case on
the Java client (rawplay.sh, now with a checkpoint start) and judges it
(rawjudge.sh --budgets out/java/rawfuzz/budget.txt); review.sh surveys the
frames with pxdiff before --accept; keep.sh keeps a session as a rawjudge
directory with its start snapshot.

Divergences, each fixed (session, first tick):
1. Control or shift pressed in the frame of a Q over a slot or a click
   (rf-fresh-1 t=256, [click 0 36 1 4] against 0 4; rf-fresh-2 t=1546;
   rf-S5-2 t=1154, a shift-click): GuiScreen's isCtrlKeyDown and
   isShiftKeyDown read the poll that delivered the tick's events; gui_input
   read the last drawn frame's. gui_input now reads the modifiers after the
   queued events; RawGui (the GUI judge's oracle half) sets them the same
   way.
2. F5 held (rf-G5-2 t=763, rf-S10-2 t=632): Java's act holds
   key.togglePerspective [1,0] (its press is taken in the key's own event);
   play mapped F5 to nothing. key_for maps it, held only.
3. Keys after a close key in one tick (rf-S15-3 t=179, rf-S18-3, rf-G2-3,
   rf-G8-3, rf-G14-3, rf-G20-3: Escape, E, Q in one frame): handleInput's
   loop goes on over the closed GuiContainer, whose keyTyped closes again,
   swaps a hotbar key with the hovered slot or drops it, the click landing
   on the inventory container (window 0: the server applies it). The act
   keeps its closes in place among the clicks (closes, close_at), the
   tape writes them in order, gui_input_closed runs the later keys,
   surv_client_click_closed predicts them, the server half closes before
   the later clicks, and Act.applyGui replays them (the oracle's own replay
   of these tapes diverged at the tick before).
4. The input block ran natively in the tick a GuiGameOver opened
   (rf-S15-3 t=942): input_ran kept the last tick's value on the early
   returns; surv_client_input clears it first.
5. R respawned natively (rf-S6-4 t=569, rf-G4-4 t=930, rf-S20-4, rf-S12-4):
   GuiGameOver takes no key in vanilla. Removed; the button stays.
6. A key held through a screen's close went on walking natively (directed
   rf-repeat-1 t=52, key.forward [0,0] against [1,2] on master): SDL's
   autorepeat set the binding held; Keyboard.next skips repeats in game.

7. The wheel under a container screen is a motion to its position (a held
   button's mouseClickMove: the pressed slot joins a drag), and the side

8. A close that kills (rf-S7-5 t=544: dead in the inventory, Escape, E, 9):

9. A wheel notch in a frame that runs no tick, taken by a late tick

10. Frames: rawjudge drew each golden in its own replay, so the pointer's

## 2026-09-28 Coverage reruns in seconds: a per-recording cache and coverage pool members (lane/covcache)

`make -C java coverage` no longer replays every recording in a fresh JVM.
Each recording's run is cached like any replay (tests/oraclecache.sh learns
`--coverage FILE` as an output and `--key` for the JaCoCo version and agent
options; entries under COVROOT, ~/.cache/netherite-coverage, 5000 MB, apart
from the shared cache that sits at its 20 GB cap). coverage.sh first asks
the cache only (CACHEONLY=1, `--lookup`, nproc at once, HARNESS computed
once), then replays the misses J at a time, J = hardware threads less the
1-minute load, 4 to 3/4 of the threads. A miss goes to a coverage member of
the shared pool (poolauto.sh's 15th argument names the agent; key
HARNESS-cov..., so normal runs never meet one), else a fresh JVM. CovReport
reuses a recording's analysis when its exec file and the class files are
those of the last report (recs/NAME.key).

A member's data is cut per job (Coverage.java): what the JVM start ran,
then the class initializers a fresh JVM would have run by the job's end,
then the job's own probes (reset after Pool.init and after each teardown),
three JaCoCo dumps that read as one file. The initializers are the hard
part: Pool.init forces every one. CovInit.java (loaded by PoolAgent only
beside JaCoCo's agent, after it, so class ids match a fresh JVM's) marks
every new/getstatic/putstatic/invokestatic target and each <clinit>'s entry
and exit, keeps each forced initializer's own probes and touches, and adds
the closure the job reached. It also puts each static Gson's adapter cache
back per job (Rewind leaves Gson opaque; EnumTypeAdapterFactory.create was
missing in 108 pooled recordings). Rewind skips JaCoCo's $jacocoData.
A member no longer dumps when its watchdog ends it (SIGTERM ran
Oracle.onShutdown with the last job's path and overwrote that file: two
recordings in one cold run).

On master's 586 recordings (trade-s1 held out, harness 5d2b27025255): cold
2,842 s at J=4 (load 78 falling to 25), 569 on members and 17 fresh, report
14 s; warm rerun 6.4 s with unexecuted.tsv, summary.txt, methods.tsv and
lines.tsv byte-identical to the cold run's; trade-s1 put back, the rerun
replayed only it, 11.6 s; the next rerun 6.4 s. 7,693 of 10,040 in-scope
methods run. lane/javacov's fresh-only run was 2,436 s at J=10 for 530.
Equality: covered-method sets, not bytes (the exec header carries a session
id and times). Against lane/javacov's fresh-JVM data on 564 recordings the
union of covered methods is identical (8,590 = 8,590); per recording 157
match exactly and the rest differ only at four timing sites, each seen in
both directions: NetHandlerPlayServer.onConnectionStateTransition (netty's
event loop sets the state; two fresh JVMs differ in 7 of 14), the NBT
double and float readers (AnvilChunkLoader.loadChunk reads ChunkIO's save
in flight or the region file, by writer-thread timing; line coverage shows
the branch), MinecraftServer.outputPercentRemaining (a 1-second wall clock)
and SkinManager's executor callback. Gate 5/5; `make -s -C native test` rc
0 on the tree merged with master.

## 2026-09-28 memslot: the waiting was the lock; admission by real use (lane/memslot2)

The brief read make test's waiting column (12,188 job-seconds in
playfuzz2's trial) as jobs queueing for memory. Instrumented on the dev host, it
was the machine-wide lock: every job held /tmp/netherite-mem/lock while it
forked a cat per reservation and ls, sort and date, about 160 ms a hold at
load 50 to 75 on 32 threads (nv2.slice at CPUWeight 20). An instrumented
suite (TESTJ=48) spent 19 s a reserved job in flock (46 s at worst), 7 ms
holding it, 0.28 s before it, and every admission passed its memory check
on the first try; /proc/locks showed the lock held 58% of a minute by
older copies' short holds. memslot.sh now forks nothing under the lock
(read builtins, globs, EPOCHSECONDS), looks peaks up through grep -F (awk
alone over the 574,000-line peaks file cost 0.1 s CPU a job), and takes
its own lock.r, so the checkouts that have not merged this cannot stall
it; an older copy's decision can overlap this one's, bounded by that one
job's reservation (the margin covers it). Checkouts get this only when
they merge master.

Admission by real use: a job is admitted while nv2.slice's committed memory
(memory.current less active_file, inactive_file and slab_reclaimable; the
page cache was 33 of 58 GB at 2:14 am) plus what each live job may still
grow by plus its own reservation fits under min(budget, memory.max) less
MARGIN 3000 MB. A job may grow by its reservation less the resident size
of its process tree (another reservation's subtree excluded: play_check's
oracle JVM holds its own) for RAMP s after admission, then by at most
TAIL: native 10 s/0, oracle 30 s/0, pool member 60 s/400 MB; a job outside
the slice (the orchestrator's session runs test-map there) counts its whole
use. native/tests/memstate.awk computes it into /tmp/netherite-mem/snap
(one refresh a second, shared by every waiting job, 50 ms). The fair queue
and the oracle half cap are kept; an older copy at the head of the queue
(want.T.PID; this one writes want.T.r.PID) is also left room in
reservation terms, so it cannot starve. Without cgroup v2, gawk or a fresh
snapshot the old reservation sum applies, under the old lock.

Measured with the new sampler (native/tests/memsample.sh: the slice's
memory.stat against every live reservation each second, each job's
resident size, 3,561 samples over 1.25 h of every lane's work, 15,769
jobs). Peaks rarely coincide: at the busiest moment (3:06 am, 66 jobs, 19
oracle JVMs) the reservations summed 63.7 GB and committed memory was 43.9
GB. Native checks peak within 0 to 3 s; an oracle run's growth after 20 s
was at most 156 MB; pool members grow while they run jobs (1 GB after 30 s,
459 MB after 60 s). The rule was scored by D(t) = the most committed
memory reached in the next 10 minutes (less the reservations of jobs
admitted meanwhile) minus what the rule projected at t: its largest value
was -777 MB (never passed), 1,335 MB with no pool tail, 5,536 MB counting
committed memory alone. MARGIN 3000 covers what the hour did not show: the
largest run past its reservation in a day of peaks (1,029 MB, an oracle
run; 619 of 6,341 oracle runs over, median 8 MB) and one older copy's
overlapping admission. Memory outside any job (agents, builds, Xvfb) was
1.9 GB median, 4.0 GB p99, which the old sum never counted. At the moments
the reservations passed 55 GB the rule left 0.4 to 4.1 GB more room than
the old sum, margin included; oom_kill stayed 0.

Before and after, full suites at TESTJ=48 TESTCACHE= (1,736 jobs)
alternated under the live load, 2:27 to 3:40 am: old memslot 10,893, 8,009
and 4,293 job-seconds waiting (wall 342, 301, 279 s); this one 548, 646 and
257 (wall 292, 301, 403 s); 94% less waiting. Wall did not move beyond the
noise: the suite is CPU-bound at that load, and jobs that no longer queue
run side by side (running job-seconds 4,498 to 6,337 before, 9,737 to
11,932 after). 0 OOM kills in nv2.slice through every run. `make -s -C
native test` on the tree merged with master: rc 0.

## 2026-09-28 the warm pool fails loudly: a job that throws reruns fresh, never passes (lane/poolfix)

lane/chainfuzz saw a member answer rc 0 for a next-start Snapshot that ran
out of heap. The cause is general: Snapshot.parallel wraps a worker's
OutOfMemoryError in an IllegalStateException, the script's run command
turns that into an error reply, and the script ends with rc 0 and no
manifest, in a member or a fresh JVM alike (reproduced on master's
classes: a fresh JVM at -Xmx800M on G30 answered rc 0 with no manifest;
Snapshot.run's own thread also caught only Exception, so an Error there
gave an ok reply with no result).
Now a job's Throwable is a fault (Oracle.threw, Oracle.fault, Pool.fault):
in a member any Throwable from a command, the launch, an uncaught one on
any thread, or the JVM exiting under the job (a crash report's
System.exit, a kill) prints ORACLE FAULT with the error, sends POOL-FAULT
and rc 71, and the member ends (port and pid files first). pool.sh then
exits 124, as it also does when a member ends with no rc, and the Makefile
runs the job in a fresh JVM, never in another member. In a fresh JVM an
Error (wrapped or not) or an uncaught Throwable ends the run with rc 71; an
Exception's error reply is unchanged. Every oracle JVM runs
-XX:+ExitOnOutOfMemoryError (JVMOOM), so no catch can swallow a heap OOM.
Heap: a fresh next-start snapshot of the largest chain checkpoints (G30,
S23; G29 and S22 in the End, 966 chunks) OOMs at -Xmx800M and passes at
1100M (RSS 1.55 to 1.6 GB at 3G); a member's idle live set is 173 MB, so
members keep -Xmx3G. Their memslot reservation is now the largest of the
last 20 member peaks, not 3 (793 members: 531 to 3,329 MB, median 2,539).
--save-at-end: Main.configurePool always refused it, but pool.sh asked a
member first (4,978 such refusals and 792 --snap-at in the shared members'
logs); pool.sh now refuses the flags the pool never runs by rule, before
connecting, and poolauto.sh uses the same list (pool.sh --never).

Proof: -Xmx800M members on G30, with and without ExitOnOutOfMemoryError:
the member ended ("Terminating due to java.lang.OutOfMemoryError", and
"ORACLE FAULT run Snapshot ... OutOfMemoryError", rc 71), the fresh rerun
wrote a snapshot equal to a plain fresh one in every file; a member killed
mid-job gave POOL-FAULT and a fresh rerun equal to fresh. pool-proof on 16
recordings (seeds 1 and 42, dev, checkpoint starts, --detail) record and
replay: fresh = pool in every file and verdict; a SAVEEND replay went
fresh by rule with no member asked. selfcheck through six local members:
587/587 OK (474 answered by members, 0 faults). make gate 5/5.

## 2026-09-27 lane/inputorder: one ordered client packet list, runTick's consumer order (RL-01, RL-03, RL-04, RL-10, SR-07)

struct client_out kept one fixed array per packet type (c07[8], c08[8],
c02[8], c02_use[8], one c09_slot) and surv_server_tick_start drained them
as all C07s, then C02 interacts, C08s, C02 attacks, then the window
clicks; surv_client_input ran the use presses before the attack presses.
Now the input block's packets go into one list (survival.h struct
client_pkt, CLIENT_PKT_CAP 256, abort past it) in Java's send order, each
consumer's syncCurrentPlayItem C09 inline ahead of its own packet (each
sender syncs, so a press that sends nothing sends no C09); the server
applies updateController's C09, the confirms, the respawn C16, the gui ops
(clicks, trsel, close: handleInput runs before the input block), then the
list in arrival order. The attack presses run before the use presses. The
list is too big for a tick frame: session_row takes client_out from the
env stack. The in-order drain exposed three bugs the type order had
hidden: the C08 tail treated a sword as having no use duration (it now
reads surv_item_use_duration), the in-air C08 ran a full
detectAndSendChanges where Java runs the quantity-only one (a drop the
same tick never reaches the client), and a player's or projectile's hit
skipped EntityAnimal.attackEntityFrom's override (inLove kept; it is now
in living_attack_entity_from_attacker), with the client's copy losing its
love to a same-tick attack press before its feed. SR-07:
surv_same_tool_and_block compares the tag (held_tag). New scenes, all
failing on master and passing after (test_snapshots and play_check, 0
mismatches): input-chord-s1 (row 50 d.ents: a fed cow hit and fed again
in one tick), drop-hotbar-s1 (row 23 d.ents: the drop came from the new

tool-swap-s1 (row 24 d.blk: the dig did not restart on a pickaxe swap),

the tree merged with master 6c6ec3a6: rc 0, 480 recordings and 480 play
checks.

## 2026-09-27 lane/testselect: make test reruns only the jobs a change can reach (TESTSELECT)

`make -s -C native test` used to key its result cache on the test
binary's SHA-1, and every binary links the whole engine, so any edit to
native/src reran all jobs. Now a job replays its recorded log while
every function it executed, every file it read, probed or ran, and its
recording are unchanged (TESTSELECT=1, on whenever TESTCACHE is;
TESTCACHE= still runs everything, so the merge trial is unchanged).
`make -C native test-map` records the jobs: a -finstrument-functions-once
build (out/native/fncov, hook tests/fncov_rt.h) runs every job under
strace and writes ~/.cache/netherite-testcache/sel; incremental, 7 to 11
min for every job at load 70 to 200. tests/fnkey.c keys a record on the
normal build's objects: each executed function's machine code with its
relocations resolved to names, data objects by content (hashed over
strongly connected components), the compiler and flags, the job line and
the recorded files. Every build now uses -ffunction-sections (without it
an intra-file call is a fixed distance, so one edit moved the hash of
every later function in the file; placement only, same code), and
objects depend on a stamp of the flags. regioncache.c reads its build
hash through an opaque object, else every replay keyed by the image
reran on any change. History check (tests/testsel_history.py, the last
30 master merges from lane/bot7 to lane/clientrand, each merge's jobs
selected on its parent's records against both trees' runs): 0 misses,
421 jobs that changed outcome or log all selected, 57.9% of jobs
selected overall; 12 merges selected everything (struct env, phase.c,
det.c or the flags changed), the other 18 a mean 29%, lowest 5.0%
(lane/rerecaudit). Real fixes reverted on the merged tree (1,438 jobs;
full suite 251 s at load 81): playfuzz's tripwire pin ca360079 reran
476 (197 s at load 87, pf-endlight-g29 failed), bigtree's serverreplay.c
memset reran 168 (142 s at load 98, 17 failed), the render fix cf6885ab
in raster_entities.c reran 488 (160 s at load 120, 13 failed). With no
change, 1,436 of 1,438 replay in 54 to 72 s: rawjudge.sh (Java, never
replayed) is the floor, 19 s running plus 23 s waiting on memslot at
load 107. Final suite on the tree merged with master 350b4434: TESTCACHE=
rc 0, 1,469 jobs, 0 FAILED, 204 s; default rc 0, same lines (it reran
all 1,469: lane/tabledup's new block, item and biome tables are read by
every job).

## 2026-09-27 lane/tabledup: the block, item and biome tables defined once

blocks.h, items.h and biomes.h declared their tables `static const`, so
every unit that included them carried its own copy: master's
out/native/test_snapshots (48 MB) held 57 copies of BLOCKS (416 KB each),
26 of ITEMS (192 KB) and 13 of BIOMES (12 KB), 28.9 MB of data against
3.3 MB of code, and a clean `make -C native all` wrote 2.89 GB (du) over
61 binaries. The generators (BlockTable, ItemTable, BiomeTable; make -C
java blocks-h items-h biomes-h) now write the structs and `extern`
declarations to the header and the tables (MATERIALS, BLOCKS, FIRE_FLAM,
TOOL_MATERIALS, ITEMS, BIOMES) once to native/src/blocks_table.c,
items_table.c and biomes_table.c, which the archive picks up; the table
bodies are byte for byte the old ones. stats_table.h, pick_table.h and
enchants.h have one includer each and stay as they are. After: no binary
under out/native holds a symbol of 16 KB or more twice, test_snapshots is
17.6 MB (0.67 MB data), a clean build's output is 1.06 GB (du), and
rusage counts 3.18 GB written before against 1.31 GB after (the two trees
built side by side, mold --no-fork so its writes are counted; wall 37.6 s
against 30.1 s, then 70.2 s against 70.4 s at load 120 to 180). night-s1
replays in 65.12 billion user instructions against 65.33 before, so the
table reads no longer folded to constants cost nothing. The CUDA programs
copy BIOMES rows on the host (cuda/cugen_tables.c), unchanged; cuda-chunkgen,
cuda-dimgen and the cuda and culight test_snapshots build. Suite, smoke,
globals, order, callgraph, stack and clangcheck clean; make -C java gate
5/5.

## 2026-09-27 every lane's oracle runs go to shared warm members, started on demand (lane/autopool)

prof.py at 1:55 am counted 1,135 oracle runs in 2 hours on the dev host (214
min, a replay 13 s and a script 9 s on average) and not one pool member
alive: the warm pool served only the tree that ran `make pool-start`, and
no lane did. Now `make script` and `make replay` (after the result cache
and the tree's own members, if any) hand their run to
java/tests/poolauto.sh: a free member of the machine-wide pool whose key
matches takes it, where the key is the harness hash plus a hash of the
JVM, its flags, and the real paths of the libraries, natives, client jar
and assets. Every tree on master's harness shares those members, whichever
tree started them. A run that finds none free runs fresh as before and
starts one in the background (one start at a time per key), so the next
run finds it. Members live under ~/dev/nw/oraclepool/KEY/m/N, on disk, not
/tmp's RAM disk (their game dirs keep every run's save). Each runs from a
frozen copy of the classes that started it (13 MB), so a lane worktree can
be removed under it. Each runs in its own systemd scope under nv2.slice
(MemoryMax 6G), so stopping the lane that started it leaves it up and its
memory is not charged to that lane. Each reserves memory through memslot
as pool-member (held.oracle.PID, sized by past members' peaks). At most
POOLMAX (8) members run, and together they reserve at most half the job
budget. A watchdog in the member's scope retires it under its lock (port
and pid files first, then a kill by its own pid file) after POOLIDLE (600
s) without a run or past POOLMAXMB (2500 MB). The member itself also ends
after a run over --pool-max-mb (lane/oracletick). `make pool-status` lists
the members, `make pool-shared-stop` stops them, events.log records every
start and retirement. What a run resolves stays the calling tree's: its
arguments are absolute, the checkpoint root comes from its run directory,
and its outputs land where a fresh JVM in that tree writes them.
pool-proof.sh gains a `shared` mode, where ALT=DIR runs every second run
from another checkout: the cross-tree case.

Byte identity also needed one harness fix. A member's det.nbt listed
EnchantmentHelper's and the enchantment table's split Randoms where a
fresh JVM had not initialized those classes yet (the pool initializes
every class at start). This was the one pool-versus-fresh file difference
lane/warmoracle and lane/oracletick left. EnchantmentHelper's split
appears in a fresh JVM only when something first touches the class: a
dungeon chest's enchanted book in seed 1's spawn chunks, the first damage
to an entity, never in a short checkpoint start. PoolAgent.java, a
-javaagent that only members load, rewrites the five split owners
(through the JDK's internal ASM) so that each constructor and static
method marks its class. Pool clears the marks when a run's world
launches. Snapshot lists a split only if its owner was initialized before
the pristine point, was touched by the run, or the split was drawn.

Proof on the merged tree (harness 2489c0d73121, the dev host at load 70 to 85):
18 recordings (hudkeys-s1, dev-world-s1, scen-water-lava-s1,
mobattack-overlap-s1, idx-flypig-s1, smoke-s1, smoke-s42, fall-s42,
