## 2026-09-27 the region store's seed world is built once per distinct input (lane/regioncache)

Every replay that joins a seed world built the seed world's spawn area
into its region store at the first chunk load (serverreplay.c
sr_ensure_saved: seedworld_build's 625 chunks, population, the creatures'
entity pass): 14.3 to 16.5 G instructions and 170,000 to 186,000
allocations, 0.9 to 2.1 s at load 85 to 110, in 58 of 261 recordings and
about 80 times per suite (interleave, rawjudge, the judges), and on every
fuzz case and session check that starts fresh. native/src/regioncache.c
keeps the build's result as an image on disk (~/.cache/
netherite-regioncache, 11 to 12 MB each, LRU past 4000 MB, a flock per
key so a concurrent miss waits and then hits) and every later replay with
the same key maps it. The key holds what decides the build and nothing
else: a build hash of native/src, the compiler and its flags (the
Makefile's RC_BUILD, without the checkout's path), the struct sizes, the
seed, the quiet-join pin, the run_config and the big-tree state (zero
since lane/bigtree). The image is the seed world's chunks in slot order
(struct, chunk_pack's deflated sections, tile entities, pending ticks),
the creatures after their pass, and the env state the build leaves: the
big-tree state, the entity chunk stamp's advance, and the item tags it
used, as texts in first-use order (itemtag.c now journals lookups and
interns while a capture runs), which interned again on any tag table make
exactly the entries the build would have made there; tile entity stack
tags are stored as positions in that list. A miss builds, captures the
image and applies it as a hit does, so one path follows the build either
way. Found on the way: the liquid springs' shared arrays
(features_springs, BlockDynamicLiquid's instance fields, rewritten before
every read) were the only key input that varied between recordings (12
keys instead of 3); they are scratch the replay's own liquid updates left,
so the build's writes to them are now put back after it. An entity's
Random padding (a struct copy of a stack det_rng) made two builds of one
key differ in bytes; the image clears it.

The switch is a flag, not an environment variable: --region-cache
on|off|verify|verify:DIR|DIR on test_snapshots and test_interleave, make
-C native test REGIONCACHE=off|verify (passed to the snapshot and
interleave jobs, like TESTCACHE). verify builds every time, exits 3 when a
stored image differs from the build, and audits struct env after the
build: a byte changed outside what the image carries and what only decides
addresses or is scratch (pools, block worklist, pack buffer, NBT pools and
memo, the stronghold's biome-box memo, light-cap and phase counters) stops
it. test_relocate's twins run with the cache off: one twin missing beside
the other hitting parts their heaps, which breaks its twin-diff rebasing
(reload-genwalk failed at row 1542 with a cold cache; both building or
both hitting pass).

The checkpoint path was already lazy (it lists the save's chunks and reads
each at its first load); its cost was two loops quadratic in the
snapshot's seed ticks. They now go through a sorted index built once per
store build (same order, same results): stats-s1 (44,967 seed ticks) 995
ms to 12 ms. gold-g30-s42's build row 18356 is 10.6 ms and 25 M
instructions with a warm page cache here (the 1.13 s the GPU re-profile
measured on the GPU host was I/O); a region cache has nothing to save there, and
no region byte is ever cached: a one-byte change to a chunk in
flow-walk-s1's save/ overlay (a copy under this lane's
out/java/regioncache) changes the built store's block digest
(e0bdad3f8399faff to 16b080df069bdcf5) while the seed image still hits.

Evidence (the dev host, load 60 to 190 from other lanes throughout, so time is
quoted beside instructions): the build row (phase profile, allocount)
fresh-play-s1 16.542 G instructions and 169,552 allocations on master, a

(the capture packs all 625 chunks); gen-walk-s42 14.313 G, 186,261

## 2026-09-27 GPU plan L17: S6 on the device, the engine's own C compiled for the GPU (lane/gpus6)

S6 (servertick_chunk_loop: mood and relight, the light flags, lightning,
ice and snow, the random ticks through the block worklist and update_tick,
World.rand and updateLCG) runs on the GPU as the C engine itself, not a port:
cuda/s6.mk compiles every native/src file twice with clang 21, once to
x86-64 objects for the harness and once to nvptx64 bitcode, both through an
LLVM plugin (cuda/nwpass.cpp) whose nw-rename gives every internal symbol the
name FILE$NAME in both builds. The device module keeps what the kernel
reaches by direct calls plus five host callbacks it stores in the image
(S6_CALLBACKS: st_on_block, st_drop_sink, st_tnt_prime, st_block_env_drop,
sr_on_spawn), is optimized (inline threshold 25), stubbed (a function it
lacks flags the run and returns zero) and given a symbol table, split in 24
parts and each compiled on its own (ptxas -c peaks near 130 MB; one ptxas on
the whole engine was OOM-killed at 8 GB), then nvlinked. A forked child holds
the device (the grave faults on driver threads, as in L15 and L16): it
empties the image window before cuInit and reserves device memory at each
image's own address, so every image pointer is the same on host and device.
Globals and functions differ: memory always holds host addresses and
registers device ones, by the nw-dev pass (every pointer load through
nwdev_in, every pointer store through nwdev_out, every indirect call
checked); mutable globals get the host's bytes by name from the executable's
symbol table (975 of 1,001 device symbols bound, 18 mutable). Every store,
memset, memcpy and atomic passes a write barrier (nwdev_wb) that lists the
image pages the block wrote; those come back and the host imports them. Per
environment the device holds a 2 MB granule wherever a page was nonzero
(combat-mobs-s1: 106 granules, 224 MB) and one shared zero granule over the
rest of the live extents; a write there, a call to a host function the
module lacks (a chunk load from the loaded edge: sr_provide and the Nether's
and End's, a pressure plate's entity query, a portal pigman), a device-only
address stored into the image or an abort flags the run: its written pages
are restored from the host and C runs S6 instead. One thread block per
environment, one thread; 32 KB of device stack (8.7 GB reserved per context).

test_snapshots --phase-kernel S6 --phase-kernel-cuda (out/native/s6cuda/)
runs it through L13's harness in place of the stand-in; cuda/s6batch.c runs
several replays on a baton in one process and launches all their S6 at once
(one block each); --phase-kernel-cuda-diff runs the device then C and
compares every page the device wrote. make -C native s6-check runs every
recording in batches (cuda/s6_sweep.sh: up to 8 per launch within a memory
budget, C traces cached by the C build's hash).

Gate, on this lane before the last master merge (af051912): `make -C native
s6-check S6_SWEEP_J=2`: 231 of 231 recordings pass, every row's S6 digests
equal to C's trace and every row exact, 614,239 S6 runs on the device and
3,856 (0.63%) flagged and redone in C, 47:51 wall; one launch held 8
recordings (swim-s42, walk300-s1, walk300-s42, hudkeys-s1,
surv_fall20-late-s42, auditfixa-rain-s1, cat-fall-s1, gold-g2-s42), 13 held 6.
act2-s1 with --phase-kernel-cuda-diff: 369 runs, 31,384 pages the device
wrote, all byte-equal to C's; 2,050 pages C wrote and the device did not,
all already equal on the device (zeroed freed blocks). Device time,
combat-mobs-s1, 400 rows, per launch, on GPU 0 (another project's job at
100% and 31 GB on it; load 16 to 25): 1 environment 26.95 ms, 8 copies 26.94
ms, 64 copies 24.66 ms, so 26.95, 3.37 and 0.385 ms per environment-row; on
GPU 3 with no other process on it (load about 80): 11.27, 11.39 and 12.47 ms
(11.27, 1.42 and 0.195 per environment-row). C's S6 on the host is 1.15 ms
and 1.72 M instructions per row (phase profile, load about 80). The round trip it pays per row at 1 environment: 570
pages down (2.3 MB) and 231 up (0.95 MB); host export 0.52 M user + 2.63 M
kernel instructions, import 0.06 M + 0.55 M; the child's upload and
download 0.22 and 0.20 ms on the idle GPU (3.9 and 2.4 ms shared), 20.3 and
9.8 ms at 64 environments (132 and 126 ms shared), serial per environment. Also
fixed: survival.c's client_harvest_player passed an empty slot's item -1 as
the held item (ITEMS[-1]; gcc's layout hid it, clang's segfaulted act2-s1).

## 2026-09-27 the spawn area's big trees grow from a fresh JVM's state (lane/bigtree)

lane/rerecaudit's re-recordings of 15 seed-1 recordings (auditfix-far-s1,
death-drown-s1, death-lava-s1, surv_cactus-s1, surv_death-s1,
surv_drop-s1, surv_drown-s1, surv_eat-s1, surv_fall12-s1, surv_fall20-s1,
surv_food-s1, surv_lava-s1, surv_starve-s1, surv_suffocate-s1,
walk300-s1) failed natively because their snapshots now carry
worldstate.nbt's bigTree (jungle 21=6, jungle hills 22=11). In vanilla
WorldGenBigTree.generate draws heightLimit only while it is 0 (java/src
WorldGenBigTree.java:494) and each biome object keeps its one instance, so
the Java run grew the spawn area's jungle big trees from 0 and the
snapshot holds what they left. Native loaded that state
(serverreplay.c:885) before seedworld_build rebuilt the same spawn area,
so the rebuild's jungle big trees grew from the end state and the unsaved
spawn-area chunks came out different. The fix zeroes decorator.bigtree_state
for seedworld_build and puts the snapshot's state back after
(serverreplay.c sr seed-world load). The 15 re-recorded under master's

## 2026-09-26 the Java oracle runs once per distinct input: a result cache under make script and make replay (lane/oraclecache)

The oracle is deterministic, yet the lanes re-ran it for results they
already had (a lane that changes only C code replays the same tapes again).
java/tests/oraclecache.sh now sits under `make -C java script` and `make
-C java replay`, and so under session.sh's check, anytick, keyframes,
rerecord, rawjudge, native/play/check.sh and every fuzz or frame capture
built on them. The key is a sha256 of: the harness hash, the JVM version,
the library listing and the Mesa package (memoized per binary and package
database time), the cache script's own hash, the kind, and every oracle
argument with each input replaced by its content (the script, the replayed
tape, world.conf, a raw GUI file, any existing file a script names outside
out/frame/blobs/post; a --from checkpoint by its path, which the tape
header records, and its manifest's sha256; a replayed tape's checkpoint
start as Main.configure resolves it: recorded, or the tree's copy by its
manifest sha) and each output path replaced by its role (TAPE, FRAMES,
SNAPDIR, SAVEEND with its basename, which becomes the checkpoint's name,
TRACE). Output paths, POOL and the host are not in it. An unknown oracle
argument bypasses the cache; a CLASSES other than the tree's own build
(pool-proof's MAKEX) or CACHE=0 runs fresh. The value is every file the run
wrote (newer than a marker under the declared outputs, the run's
replay.jsonl and latest.log, every path its ORACLE lines name and every
path its script names; empty directories too: a checkpoint's save keeps
DIM-1 and DIM1), plus its merged log. Paths of the output roots inside
stored text (tape rows name their frames, the log its snapshots, a
fallback checkpoint start is named through the run directory) are stored
as role tokens and written back as the new run's paths in one
longest-match pass that leaves key-determined paths alone. A hit copies
the files back (copies, not links: a later run truncates its outputs in
place), deletes the files a Snapshot deletes before writing, prints the
log and one `oracle cache: hit` line on stderr, with no JVM and no memory
reservation; a hit whose checkpoint directory exists runs fresh, since the
oracle refuses to overwrite one. A miss runs `make KIND CACHE=0` (the
command-line variables reach it through MAKEFLAGS) under a per-key flock,
so an identical concurrent miss waits and then hits, and stores only rc 0.
Entries live in ~/.cache/netherite-oracle (OCROOT, shared by every checkout;
OCCAP 20000 MB, least recently used evicted); OCROOT/stats.tsv logs every
lookup and `make -C java cache-stats` sums it. The gate and pool-proof's
pool mode pass CACHE=0. Two bugs found on the way: `sort -u` under the
en_US locale merged DIM-1 and DIM1 (the script runs in LC_ALL=C, the oracle
in the caller's locale), and bash's tab IFS collapses an empty field.

Proof on the GPU host (load average 110 to 120; out/java/oc/batch.sh, each case
run twice from an empty cache): anytick fight-zombie-s1 (replay, SNAPAT, 55
snapshots, 127 MB) 86.9 s then 17.5 s, the 55 snapshot directories
identical, 55/55 resume; a playfuzz case (pf-g3-302, from checkpoint G3 by
the fallback path) with SAVEEND 36.5 s then a hit in 0.4 s, checkpoint,
pre snapshot, save and rows identical; make rerecord of fight-zombie-s1
and gold-g2-s42 (script, FROM G1, a save) 43.7 s then 4.3 s, rr1 = rr2 in
every file and = a CACHE=0 root in every file pool-proof compares; the

Java runs hits, checkpoints and start snapshots identical; a frame capture

## 2026-09-26 GPU plan L13: env_export, env_import and the per-phase kernel harness (lane/gpuharness)

src/imgxfer.[ch] is the env image's transfer format: pages of the image by
index (a zero page carries no bytes) and the address the image had, which
its remaining pointers name (a device reads p as its own base + (p - base)).
env_export reads the whole image (every resident nonzero page of
image_extents) or, with a write tracker, the pages written since the image
was last in step with its copy; env_import writes a transfer into an image
of the same layout. The tracker is one userfaultfd in asynchronous
write-protect mode (UFFD_USER_MODE_ONLY, allowed unprivileged) with remap
events, and PAGEMAP_SCAN returns and re-protects the written pages. Three
kernel facts shaped it: asynchronous mode implies WP_UNPOPULATED, so a
write-protect of the whole 32 GB mapping builds page tables for all of it
(every scan then cost 435 M kernel instructions; the tracker protects by one
scan instead); a scan reports each empty entry of a page table it walks
once, and a zapped page reads as unwritten, so a freed heap block's pages go
in a zap log in struct env_image (image_free, IMG_ZAP_MAX 128; past it the
block's resident pages are cleared by writes) and an export drops reported
pages that hold no memory and are not in the log; and reading an empty page
maps the zero page, which the tracker takes for a write, so the whole-image
export and the verify compare read resident pages only (mincore; this took a
host scan from 6.4 M to 2.2 M kernel instructions and the first row's flood
from 273,000 pages to 2,154). image_move (mremap) moves an image to another
slot and keeps its protection (the tracker's thread acknowledges the remap
events).

test_snapshots --phase-kernel LIST|all (tests/phasekernel.h) replays in an
image environment H with a device copy D in another slot. At each tested
phase's start the host's writes go down (env_export of H, env_import into
D), H's mapping is moved aside and D's onto H's address, and the stand-in
kernel, the C phase itself, runs there on nothing but what the transfers
carried; at its end D's writes come back (env_export of D, the mappings
moved back, env_import into H) and the tracer digests P's classes in H.
--phase-kernel-ref TRACE compares every row's digests with a --phase-trace
of the same recording; --phase-kernel-plant ROW:LABEL:WHAT flips a byte of
D; --phase-kernel-verify N compares H and D over every live page every N
rows. phase.c calls the harness's hook (phase_env.kernel) for the phases in
kernel_mask; without a reference the tracer stays off (PHASE_KERNEL) so a
cost run counts the phases' own writes. A CUDA kernel takes the stand-in's
place. `make -C native phase-kernel-check [PHASES=all] [RECS=...]
[VERIFY=N]` runs the trace and the kernel run per recording; `make -C native
phase-kernel-cost [PHASES=S6] [RECS=...]` tabulates the round trip per row
over the audit's twelve.

## 2026-09-26 GPU plan L16: the light engine on the device, byte-equal on every call (lane/gpulight)

World.updateLightByType (func_147463_c), func_147451_t, Chunk.func_150811_f's
column checks (func_150809_p's 256 columns and func_150801_a's edge) and
enqueueRelightChecks are block-level CUDA device functions
(native/cuda/culight_dev.cuh) over chunks laid out as the env image lays
them out (struct chunk, bands by bandoff). One block runs an update as C's
FIFO queue a window at a time: up to blockDim entries are evaluated against
the state before the window, a writer map (atomicMin per cell) finds the
first entry that read a cell an earlier entry of the window changed, a
duplicate of an earlier writer's cell is resolved in place (the decrease
left it 0, the spread left it at the light it computes), a write that makes
a section ends the window (generateSkylightMap runs on the device), and a
cub scan places the committed entries' appends and write epochs where the
sequential run puts them, with the 32,768 cap applied as C applies it. So
the queue, every write, its order and the chunk stamps are C's.

The gate is a capture (native/src/lightcap.[ch], test_snapshots --light-cap
count|cuda [--light-drivers]): a hook in world.c's update_light_by_type
(nw_env->light.cap, off by default) keeps a mirror of chunk slots on the
device in step with C and streams each call with C's result and every
written chunk after it; a forked child (cuda/culight_cap.c, as
cugen_ahead.c) replays the stream and compares the return value, queue
length, cap hits, epoch and write sequence, the chunks written, and each
written chunk's mask, height and precipitation maps, stamps, band storage
and all 16 bands' sky and block light. A chunk is re-sent when its write
sequence, or its height, precipitation, mask, cursor or populated flag,
differs from the mirror's: Chunk.relightBlock rewrites a column's height
and sky between the light calls of one setBlock without moving the chunk's
write sequence (fight-skeleton-s1, call 36, was the first stale mirror).
Only bands whose hash changed are sent; calls the 17-block box refuses send
nothing. With --light-drivers the three loops are captured whole and the
device runs them; a relight whose facing chunk is not loaded (C would load
it on a block read) is left to its calls. The replay batches: a call whose
computed light equals the stored light writes nothing, so a run of such
calls is evaluated a thread each against one state up to the first whose
queue starts; a driver lists its calls from block ids (light never changes
them) and relists after a call makes a section.

## 2026-09-26 GPU plan L12: a relocatable env image, one RNG table (lane/gpuimage)

An environment made with env_new is now one mapping (src/image.[ch]) in a
fixed address window: struct env, its arena, then a heap of power-of-two
blocks named by offsets. src/envheap.h, included ahead of every source,
routes malloc, calloc, realloc, free and strdup to the current env's heap
while session_open and session_tick run, and fixed arrays of an image env
are heap blocks, so everything the tick reads or writes lies in the image.
Chunk structs are slots of a new arena chunk pool; struct world's slot[]
and near[] hold chunkref (slot + 1) and a chunk names its bands by offset
(bandoff), so a chunk holds no address. struct rng_table in struct env holds
every Random kept from row to row outside an entity: each world's World.rand
and updateLCG, the replay's Det, Collections.shuffle's Random, the three
worldTeleporter Randoms, the block singletons' static Randoms and
BlockFire's. The providers' and MapGenBase Randoms stay with their
providers: every use reseeds them first, so they carry nothing between rows.
The image's directory (img_dir) gives the session, snapshot, replay, each
server world, each dimension state and the client world as offsets. The
grave's records are per env and it sweeps an image's env and heap; a freed
heap block is zeroed (pages past the first go back by madvise), so no stale
pointer is left in the image. tests/test_relocate.c runs each recording of a
set twice in two image envs on one baton; every Nth row the first run's
image is copied to a new mapping at another address, the words that point
into it and differ from the twin's are rebased (image_relocate), the old
mapping is unmapped, and the run continues there. Sets (out/java/relocate):
reload-genwalk (play-reload2-s1 with gen-walk-s42 interleaved, every 250
rows), nether-trip (nether-trip-s1, every 100), gold-g30 (gold-g30-s42,
every 1000): all exact, 10 to 19 moves each; no-rebase (a plain copy)
faults. Rebased words per move, the absolute pointers the image still
holds: 5,597 mean on nether-trip-s1, 10,052 on play-reload2-s1, 25,959 on
gen-walk-s42, 222,181 on gold-g30-s42, most of them the harness's tape rows
(tape.c) and the snapshot's NBT trees (nbtjson.c); in the tick's state the
largest are the scheduled-tick heap (ticks.c heap_push, 9,073 on gen-walk-s42),
four pointer fields per living and one per chunk. Words naming run memory
outside the image: up to 8,535 per move, nearly all the entity digest's NBT
memo buffers (env.h nbtbin memo), made outside session_tick. Instructions
(perf, the first env, not an image): play-reload2-s1 41.68 G to 42.10 G
(+1.0%), combat-mobs-s1 11.53 G to 11.62 G (+0.8%). test_relocate and
test_interleave give runner threads no guard pages (glibc 2.43 keeps the
guard inside the stack mapping, which the grave's sweep read). Globals 582
(master 587), allow list unchanged; index check 1776 ok. `make -s -C native
test PLAYCHECK=1` rc 0 on the merged tree (1517 jobs: master's plus the
three relocate sets).

S3 (ChunkProviderServer.unloadQueuedChunks) deflated every chunk it parked
in the region store. Now sr_store_chunk parks the chunk as its bands and
notes it; serverreplay_park packs the row's parked chunks after the tick
(session_row, sub-mark PARK), raw deflate at level 1 with no zlib header or
adler32 (20% fewer instructions than compress2; levels 2 and 6, Z_RLE and
Huffman-only measured larger or slower). The adopted Nether and End region
chunks a snapshot carries (saved-chunks.bin.gz) entered the store as bands:
54 MB of gold-g15-s42 and 59 MB of gold-g30-s42; they are packed as they
enter. Nothing reads a parked chunk's cells until it loads again, and the
phase digests hash the store by count and write sequence, so every row and
digest is unchanged.

## 2026-09-26 GPU plan L15: chunk generation served ahead of the step, from the CUDA kernels (lane/gpugen)

Raw generation is a pure function of (seed, dimension, cx, cz), so
native/src/genahead.c makes it before the tick that asks for it. Before each
step it predicts, per environment, the chunks the next tick may generate:
the player's square at max(view + 1, 9) (view + 1 where reads do not
generate and only the player manager loads; two rings more in the Nether,
whose hidden lava populates outward), a 50-block pathfinder window around
every living, a Nether portal's destination (the player's portal timer, or a
living in a portal), the End's entrance when an End portal is within two
blocks, the dragon, the scheduled ticks due next within six blocks of a
chunk edge (a liquid's flow search reads five out), and a row's Dev tp
target (test_snapshots passes it as a hint). The new requests go to a
generator in one batch; each result is built with the C provider's own
constructors (chunkgen_construct and world_dim_construct, split out of
provide_chunk and load_dim_chunk) and kept in the environment's cache.
chunk_backend (world.h) gains take and owed: world_chunk_request takes the
cached chunk and world_gen_state applies the provider state its generation
leaves (the overworld's topBlock entries the chunk's columns wrote,
surface_tops_merge, and the provider rand; the Nether's or the End's rand,
the provider built on first use); an owed generation applies a state-only
entry; anything else falls back to C and is counted. The kernels now return
the provider rand after the surface pass (k_surface, k_dim_surface) and
cugen hands back its topBlock tables. `test_snapshots --gen-ahead c` runs the
seam with the C engine as the generator; `--gen-ahead cuda` in
out/native/cuda/test_snapshots (make -C native gen-ahead-cuda) serves it from
cugen and cudim in a forked child process, because grave.c's scan of every
private anonymous mapping faulted on a CUDA driver thread's stack inside the
replay's process (swamp-night-s2, rc 139). `make -C native gen-ahead-check
[GEN=c] [RECS=...]` replays every snapshot recording that way, and `make -C
native phase-profile GEN=cuda` profiles with it.

## 2026-09-26 GPU plan L11: the s2c queues rotated by index, big parts out of line (lane/gpuq)

Every row copied the 270 KB struct s2c_queue twice (session.c: the
client's copy of what the last server tick sent, then the server's queue
into the sent one): 25.6 k instructions per tick, memory bound, the bulk
of the profile's `(between)` time. The three queues now live in the env
(survival.s2c, struct s2c_ring) and a row hands them on by index:
s2c_receive at the row's start (the client reads the sent queue),
s2c_send at its end (the server's queue becomes the sent one). The
server's queue is copy-on-write: s2c_clear, the tick's first open, takes
a free queue without a copy; s2c_out copies the used part only when a
tick appends to a queue that is still the sent or the client's one (the
dev ops and the ender pearl, which queue without opening first). The
pump's end-of-drain `n = 0` became s2c_drain (the client index goes to
-1), so it no longer empties a shared queue. The S30's 40 stacks, the
S3F's recipe list and the S2D's title moved out of struct s2c_pkt (2,112
to 104 bytes) into a per-queue side store (s2c_side_new, s2c_side),
sized for 128 full recipe lists so it never fills before the packets do;
only n packets and nside bytes of a queue are ever touched. The players'
s2c fields, session's s2c_prev and the unused surv_client_receive are
gone. Phase profile on the plan's twelve recordings (load 80 to 160):
~S2CCOPY never runs (0 on all twelve), `(between)` 0.10 to 1.61% of tick
time (base 7 to 32%), instructions per tick down 25.6 k on every one
(persist-village-s42 1,590.3 k to 1,564.4 k, gold-g30-s42 3,907.3 k to
3,881.5 k); envmem "other" 1.3 to 1.6 MB on base to 0.6 to 0.9 MB (0.7
to 0.8 MB less; total 38.3 to 37.5 MB on persist-village-s42). Wall-time
pairs base/new at load 80 to 170 went both ways by up to 2x, noise.

## 2026-09-26 a whole game in sittings: session.sh chains checked sessions (lane/humanrun)

A human can now play the native client from a fresh seed-1 world across
many sittings with every sitting checked on Java: native/play/session.sh
[--run NAME] plays the next session (out/native/play from the run's
latest verified start), and when the window closes checks it and chains
it. The Java oracle starts only from the seed or a Checkpoint (a save
and a rejoin), never from a Snapshot, so the chain has the golden chain's
shape: a new replay flag, Main --save-at-end DIR (make replay SAVEEND=dir),
ends the replay of the played tape with the script save's Save and Quit
at its last tick; the native whole-server check (test_snapshots, and play
--check, the client's own tick pair) compares every row of Java's replay
from the session's snapshot; beside it a Java script from that checkpoint
writes its Snapshot at tick 2, which becomes the next session's start for
play and for its check. A FAIL runs out/native/diverge on the check dir,
drops the attempt's checkpoint and start, and leaves the session next.
State is out/human/NAME (next, sessions.tsv, start/, play/, cp/);
--status prints each attempt, rows, the last checkpoint, whether the End
was reached (sp.dim 1 in the rows), the exit portal (cp.gui GuiWinGame)
and the dragon (the credits, or an EntityDragon in the loaded End of the
checkpoint's own snapshot). On the Mac play runs locally with the start
rsynced from the GPU host and the check runs on the GPU host over ssh (not run here).

flow-walk-s1's recorded inputs split into four sessions and played
through play's SDL input path (--input-script, dummy video driver) from

from the previous check's checkpoint), session 4 with a planted fault

## 2026-09-26 any-tick snapshots across the whole golden chain (lane/anytick2)

The any-tick sweep (`make -C java anytick`, 30 early and 25 spread ticks,
200 rows each) now passes on every golden segment from G12 to G30, the
dragon's death included, where lane/anytick left four open failures and
never swept G14 on. Each cause was state a snapshot lacked or the native
load dropped, ported from the vanilla code:

- gold-g13 t523, t1995 and t2485 (d.sseed, w.ents): a snapshot's
  saved-chunk EntityArrow reloaded through sr_restore_checkpoint_entity's
  own Arrow branch, which pointed the living world's iew at a fake Det whose
  streams sit in DET_OTHER while proj_spawn_arrow draws on the iew's role:
  the arrow took the next id without spending it (two entities with one id)
  and its Random and UUID draws never happened. It now goes through
  sr_restore_arrow, the run's own saved-arrow path.
- gold-g12 t11314 (d.ents): zombie 9874's attackTarget is villager 8835,
  whose chunk had unloaded. World.updateEntities drops such an entity from
  the lists but not from whoever holds it; it stays alive where it stood,
  and the zombie keeps walking at it. Snapshot.java wrote only "e:8835".
  Now EntityState collects every entity an rt value names, and
  writeEntities writes the unlisted living ones (and theirs) to
  ghosts.jsonl in the entities' form; the native load builds each as a
  living outside every list, chunk and count (as sr_cl_event leaves an
  unloaded chunk's living) and rt_living resolves ids to them.
- gold-g14 t3466 (w.bc, a big oak's canopy): BiomeGenBase keeps one
  WorldGenBigTree per biome, and generate() sets heightLimit once and never
  clears it (a failed validTreeLocation shortens it), so the next big tree of
  that biome starts from it for the JVM's life. worldstate.nbt carries
  bigTree (each biome id's heightLimit), loaded into decorator.c's
  bigtree_state and kept across the lazy seed-world build.
- gold-g16 t3466 (w.ents at the t % 900 save): ChunkProviderServer's
  chunksToUnload is a ConcurrentHashMap set whose table only grows; the
  native rebuilt it fresh, so the save marks' keys landed in other bins and
  a different 100 chunks unloaded. worlds.nbt carries unloadBins (the table
  length); the restored set is made at that size (cs_init_bins).
- gold-g29 t3 (a chunk kept instead of another): a bin of 10 keys is a
  TreeBin, whose list order is its history's (puts prepend); re-adding the
  keys cannot rebuild it. cs_restamp gives the restored keys their captured
  order as list stamps; later adds append after and prepend before them.
- gold-g15 t11229 (an item pushed out the wrong way): BlockFence's and
  BlockStairs' bounds are one object's fields that the last collision or ray
  trace left, and getCollisionBoundingBoxFromPool reports them for every
  fence and stair. worldstate.nbt carries blockBounds for the two fences
  and the twelve stairs; the load sets collide.c's fence_bounds and
  stairs_octant.
- gold-g30 t11367 to t17412 (an enderman's yaw): its entityToAttack is the
  EntityDragon that hit it; rt_living now resolves the dragon's id to the
  End's shadow living, which is what native livings hold.
- gold-g30 t2299, t5322, t9100, t9856, t10611 (the sword hit on the dragon
  missed natively, the case lane/keyframes named on endbot-s1): the bind
  walked the overworld's list with the player in the End, so the dragon's
  tracker entry started fresh, unwatched (its chunk no longer watched,
  while Java keeps a watched entry until it leaves range) and its client
  copy came from a spawn at the server's position. pickobj_bind now walks
  the player's dimension, restores the entry's watched state from trkrt,
  builds the client dragon from clientents (position, setPositionAndRotation2
  target and steps, serverPos, the ring buffer EntityState now writes as
  "dd:", health, death ticks) with its parts placed, and queues the
  client's pending moves, velocities and destroys for it.

The sweep's tool: diverge on a kept tNNNN, then an oracle snapshot at the
failing tick (make replay SNAPAT=... ARGS="--until N") to find the state the
resume lacked.

## 2026-09-26 an environment's memory under 80 MB: shared bands, the client and renderer copies (lane/gpumem)

GPU audit item L9, the part lane/worldmem left. Measured first:
`test_snapshots --mem DIR` (src/envmem.c) walks one environment after every
row and prints its bytes by owner at the first row and at the peak. What
grows counts what it holds (a chunk: its struct, its bands once however
many chunks share them, its packed blob; a table its capacity; a pool its
live slots); fixed structs and reserve-and-commit mappings count the pages
written (mincore); the snapshot and tape are the harness's. `play --bench
TAPE --mem` adds the renderer. The audit's 441 MB model predates worldmem's
bands; on master (bd573b6's tree, this measure) the peaks were 97.1 MB
(play-reload2-s1, row 2412) and 91.2 MB (gen-walk-s42, row 2374), and the
starts 81.2 and 56.0. By owner at the peak, before and after (MB):

| owner | play-reload2-s1 | gen-walk-s42 |
|---|---|---|
| server chunks | 22.7 / 22.5 | 33.3 / 33.3 |
| client (chunks, particles, entities) | 36.3 / 26.4 | 5.3 / 1.5 |
| pending ticks | 18.0 / 0.3 | 18.0 / 1.1 |
| entities (livings) | 9.0 / 9.1 | 20.8 / 20.8 |
| region store | 4.3 / 4.4 | 5.4 / 5.4 |
| worlds, scratch, other | 6.9 / 7.0 | 8.3 / 8.3 |
| total | 97.1 / 69.5 | 91.2 / 70.5 |

Starts: 81.2 to 48.0 and 56.0 to 49.0. What changed, every recording exact:

- A band (struct chunk_sec) counts the chunks sharing it. chunk_share
  copies a chunk with its bands shared; a store of a different value into
  a shared band first copies it for the chunk that writes (chunk_sec_own,
  in the inline setters and chunk_sec_make), and a release drops the count.
  Each chunk reads exactly what it read with bands of its own, so nothing
  observable moves (the client's light is its own and is read: place.c's
  mushroom check on the client world). The client's copies at a chunk
  packet, the prefill, an old snapshot's start and the S26 in flight share:
  the client's 27.6 MB of chunks at the start of play-reload2-s1 is 1.4 MB;
  at the peak it holds 17.7 MB of bands the server has rewritten since (its
  light) or unloaded (it keeps 525 chunks, the server 428).
- The pending tick set grows its heap by a quarter, fills its membership
  table to three quarters, and gives both back as the worldgen backlog
  (about 160,000 entries) drains: 18.0 MB to 10.9 during the backlog and
  0.3 to 1.1 after. The heap's order is its comparison's (a total order),
  so where the entries sit is not state.
- play's renderer: the window of 328 KB byte records (27x27 for
  play-reload2-s1, 240 MB reserved, 173 MB written) is a window of chunk
  records sharing the server's bands, refreshed where and when the byte
  records were (render_blocks.c reads either form); 1.4 MB at the start,
  5.7 at the peak. Meshes of sections outside the drawn square are dropped
  (they re-mesh from their record if they return). Every bench frame of
  both recordings hashes the same as master's play (2,553 and 2,460), and
  shots at four ticks each are byte-identical with the cache check exact.
  The section mesh cache is what remains of the renderer: play peaks at
  149.0 MB (play-reload2-s1, 74 MB of meshes) and 97.5 MB (gen-walk-s42).

## 2026-09-26 the tick as phases with digests (lane/gpuphase)

GPU audit item L6. A row is now a sequence of phase functions, each between
two PHASE_RUN marks and with an entry in native/src/phase.c's table (its
Java, its C function, the state classes it reads and the ones it may
write): R0 (MobMove setups), C1 (client chunk and block sync), C2 (client
player tick), TP (paused save), DV (Dev ops); per world in worldServers
order S1 (weather, sleep), S2 (spawner), S1T (skylight, clocks), S3
(unload queue), S4 (scheduled ticks), S5 (the player's light check), S6
(func_147456_g's chunk loop, the audit's S6 to S8: vanilla interleaves them
per chunk on one World.rand), SG (siege), S9 (player instances, stale
portals, villages), S10 (bolts), S11 (entity pass), S12 (tile entities), NT
(tracker), S13 (the blkHash fold), or SE for a world without chunks; then N1
(processPlayer), N2 (updateMountedMovingPlayer), N1E (action end), N3
(tracker packets), T (t % 900 unload marks). Twelve state classes:
scalars, World.rand, Det, blocks (the chunks a phase wrote, whole, in (cx,
cz) order, plus the chunk maps and each provider's unload set and player
manager), pending ticks (as a set), entities (pass order, NBT), tile
entities (NBT), the write record, villages and portal caches, the server
player, the tracker, the client. A phase's digest hashes its write classes
after it ran: the state it wrote, not the order it wrote it in. Chunks carry
a write sequence (wseq) that every block, metadata and light write and every
insertion moves.

test_snapshots --phase-trace FILE writes each row's digests (one line per
row, `0.S4=...`), --phase-digest keeps their hash, --phase-check digests
every class at both ends of every phase and fails a change to an undeclared
class. `make -C native phase-check`: 225 of 225 recordings pass. The write
matrix it observed (runs in which a phase changed a class, summed over all
225) is what the GPU port can lean on: S5 draws World.rand whenever its
world has the player and writes light in 289 runs; S1T touches only
scalars; S13 only the record; NT only the tracker and the player; T only
the unload set; S11 and N1 write every server class. Declared but never
seen (kept, they are reachable): SG's everything but scalars, World.rand
and villages; S10's blocks and World.rand; S4's and S6's player and tracker.

Gates. The traces of night-s1, play-reload2-s1, gen-walk-s42,
end-dragon-s1, gold-g30-s42 and nether-trip-s1 are byte-identical across
two runs and against the same recording interleaved with another in one
process (test_interleave --phase-trace; new pair night-gold: night-s1 with
gold-g30-s42, both exact). Negative checks: drop-one-write first differs
at row 2 in S13 alone; --fault scalar@150 at row 151 from DV (World.rand).

## 2026-09-26 iteration order as data; chunk loads as requests (lane/gpuorder)

GPU audit item L4. The JDK containers whose iteration order is game state
are now keys plus a computed order, with no bucket chains:

- The spawner's eligible set and World.activeChunkSet: jorder.c's
  jord_ccp_window sorts the (2r+1)^2 window around the player's chunk by
  JDK bin (512 bins for the spawner's 289 keys), insertion order inside a
  bin, with a 2 KB count array: no map, computable from the player's chunk.
- The explosion's affected set: jord_set3, the rays' first adds as keys,
  an open-addressed index for contains, per-bin counts for the treeify
  guard, the HashSet order a counting sort by bin.
- activePotionsMap: effects by id, a held mask and insertion stamps;
  potion_map_order walks the bins (a 16-bin table pairs b and b + 16 by
  stamp). No node pool, no pointers; a copy is a struct copy.
- chunksToUnload (chunkset.c): a ConcurrentHashMap bin's list is only
  appended to (plain put), prepended to (tree put) and unlinked from, and a
  split keeps order, so each key carries a stamp and the order is a sort by
  (bin, stamp). Bins keep a count and a TreeBin root: the red-black tree
  (index links) decides only the untreeify on remove. Membership is an
  open-addressed index; slots are reused. The unload drain computes the
  order once and walks it while no key is added.
- world_chunk_request (world.h): every chunk a server world gains
  (CREQ_GENERATE, CREQ_STORED for the region store's and saved set's,
  CREQ_SUPPLIED for a snapshot's) and every generation (CREQ_OWED) goes
  through it; it records the request (a count per kind, the last 256) and
  generates through the world's chunk_backend (chunk_backend_c:
  provide_chunk and the Nether's and End's providers), the seam for
  native/cuda. provide_chunk is referenced only by world.o (nm), and
  load_dim_chunk is world.c's static, both only from the backend;
  world_put_chunk is left to the chunk stores and client copies.

tests/order_test.c (make -C native order, run by make test) keeps the five
old emulations as references and checks each new order against them over
randomised keys: 20,000 player chunks each for the spawner and active set
(views -1 to 12), 378,761 explosion keys (equal-hash keys, tables to
32,768), 403,874 potion operations, 872,749 chunksToUnload operations over
colliding keys (119,063 tree bins sampled: treeify, split, untreeify).
Mutating a tree put to append, dropping the untreeify shape check, or
rebuilding a kept TreeBin each fails it.

Found, not changed (the old emulations had the same behaviour; follow-ups):
JDK 8 treeifies a HashMap bin of 9 at 64 bins or more, and a
ChunkCoordIntPair window does that for 0.17% of player chunks within 300
chunks of the origin at the spawner's r 8 (0.03% for the view-10 active
set); 29% (80%) of those bins hold equal 32-bit hashes, whose TreeNode
order goes by identityHashCode. A probe build
over all 225 snapshot and 10 spawning recordings found no such position.
And ConcurrentHashMap.transfer rebuilds a plain bin's run before lastRun
reversed: Java 8 iterates keys 1, 17, 33, 49, 2..10 put into
newSetFromMap(new ConcurrentHashMap()) as 33 1 2 ... 10 17 49; the
emulation (old and new) gives 1 33 ....

## 2026-09-26 the env arena: entity pools, handles, fixed capacities (lane/gpuarena)

GPU audit item L3 (out/plan/gpu-audit-2026-09-25.md). The environment now
owns one arena (native/src/arena.[ch]): a reserved mapping made with the
env, committed as written, carved into fixed-capacity slot pools with free
chains and per-slot generations (livings, living-world list entries,
item-world and falling/hanging entities, paths, village doors, chunk bands),
the pathfinder's arrays and a list slab (size-class blocks, named by
offset). What changed, every recording exact:

- Entity references are handles, not addresses: `lref` (tag, slot
  generation, slot) for every living one entity keeps of another (targets,
  attackers, riders and mounts, task partners, the senses cache, village
  aggressors, projectile shooters, the list entry's living, the probe and
  replay player twins); `ieref` and `fhref` for a list entry's item and a
  leash's knot; the worlds' lists and the chunk section lists hold pool
  slots; the pass order and the region store's live instances are
  (pool, slot); village doors are door-pool slots and a village its index
  in the collection. A getter whose generation does not match stops the
  program. The grave (between rows) recognises tagged handles besides
  addresses and scans the pools up to their high-water marks.
- struct living is a 6,960-byte hot record (was 23,440): the AI task
  lists, senses and door list, the villager's trades and the probe
  player's inventory are per-slot parts beside it in the arena.
- The tick allocates nothing outside chunk load/unload and entity creation:
  the spawner's eligible map (index chains in env scratch), ticks_peek,
  the active set, the spawner's records and boxes, the tick's write/spawn
  lists, the pass order, the player manager's sets and queues, the tracker
  queues, the explosion's affected set and lists, chunk bands and paths are
  fixed or pooled; collision lists, activate's act_env and the explosion's
  entity frames come from scoped env scratch stacks. malloc counted with an
  LD_PRELOAD hook over every in-tick call stack, per row, master 83d3566 /
  this lane: play-reload2-s1 418.2 / 24.7 (all chunk load/unload, 91% of it
  GenLayer arrays, plus 11 enchantment tags at mob creation), mobspawn-final-s1
  406.9 / 22.9, combat-mobs-s1 309.5 / 0.02 (34 creation-time tags); 0 of
  any other kind in all three.
- Found on the way: the ghast probe's pass read an item its world had
  already freed (it now reads the removal record); the snapshot runtime's
  living-reference fields were written as addresses; a mob's equipment and
  the items sharing its stack linked counts by address into another entity
  (now a living slot or an item slot the pool keeps until reuse, as the
  freed record the address named).

## 2026-09-26 recursion to explicit worklists (lane/gpuworklist)

GPU audit item L7. `make -C native callgraph` (new: gcc -fcallgraph-info on
a build without inlining, native/tests/callgraph.py) lists the cycles
reachable from session_tick with worldgen cut (chunk provide, populate and
load). At f79e9d9 it found 12 outside worldgen; now none (only the
GenLayer stack and the chunk loader's populate, both worldgen):

- The block-callback cycle (58 functions: world_set_block, the flag-1
  world_set_meta, the notifications, every callback in blockcb.c, the
  immediate schedule, liquid_update_tick and the static liquid, the falling
  block) runs on an explicit frame stack in struct env (native/src/blockwl.h,
  blockwl.c). Each call in progress is a frame (an op, a resume point, its
  locals); a step emits the calls vanilla makes next and the run loop
  pushes them so they execute in emission order, each with everything it
  triggers, before the frame resumes: vanilla's depth-first order. A body
  that goes on after a nested call is split there (World.setBlock around
  breakBlock and onBlockAdded, the notification one neighbour per step, the
  dynamic liquid's three phases, the door, the rail reshape, the chest's
  facings, the tripwire runs, the torch, trapdoor and bed tails). A block
  read or a drop after an emit in the same step aborts (bwl_quiet), which
  every recording ran through without tripping. The public entry points
  keep their names and push one frame.
- flow_cost walks a four-frame stack; retrySlotClick runs as a loop after
  the click (its last act); the spider jockey's rider and the spawner's
  jockey riders run their own onSpawnWithEgg instead of re-entering the
  dispatch; the craft result and the merchant's slot 2 store without the
  notification they never trigger; EntityCritFX's constructor calls its own
  onUpdate; the tick set's regrow reinserts without the grow check;
  getBlockLightValue_do's neighbour reads take the stored value;
  nbt_free, nbt_render, nbt_parse and parsePotionEffects walk explicit
  stacks; an entity's NBT walks its riding chain.

`make -C native worklist-depth` (new) builds with NETHERITE_WL_DEPTH and
names the deepest point of each stack over every test's data (1,260 runs):
block worklist 895 frames (test_populate pop42_11, a spring cascade under
the immediate flag; in a replay 636, sh-bot-s42; BWL_CAP 4096 of 192
bytes), 11 ops emitted by one step (BWL_EMIT_CAP 128), flow_cost 4 (its
bound), NBT walks 9 (gold-g10-s42; cap 64), potion splits 5
(fight-witch-s1; cap 32), riding chain 2 (gold-g10-s42; cap 16).
With function pointers resolved (POINTERS=1) one cycle is left, 57

## 2026-09-26 the native world's resident memory (lane/worldmem)

Measured first (GNU time per job, an LD_PRELOAD live-bytes profiler per
call site): the heavy jobs were terrain and one table. struct chunk held
four flat 64K-cell arrays (330,376 bytes, every byte written at
construction): 5,847 of them are 1.84 GB of test_projectiles proj-2,
5,303 are 1.67 GB of portals seed2 and sblocks vi2-b. A snapshot replay
added the region store's checkpoint build (every chunk the playthrough
ever saved: 4,301 for gold-g15, 1.36 GB), per-section entity lists with
2,048 fixed slots (a 256 MB table), 39 KB livings and a path finder per
living (up to 655 KB of points each, never freed with a dead one). What
changed, the output unchanged:

- A chunk's cells live in 16-block bands (struct chunk_sec, world.h) made
  on the first nonzero write, in ExtendedBlockStorage's own form: the id's
  low byte, its high nibble only for an id above 255 (none of 1.7.10's),
  NibbleArrays for metadata, sky and block light: 10 KB a band, about 4.7
  bands a chunk. Storage is independent of the section mask and holds every
  nonzero cell, so a band with no storage reads 0 as the flat arrays did.
  Every access goes through chunk_cell_* and chunk_set_*; a store past a
  field's range stops the program. The snapshot and probe hashes stream
  from the bands (the same FNV values).
- The region store reads a checkpoint's chunk at its first load
  (sr_saved_read_region), and a chunk it parks (unloads, the seed world's
  spawn area) is one deflated blob until it loads again (chunk_pack).
- Livings 39,192 to 23,456 bytes: task lists hold 16 (the villager's 15
  plus the leash task; more stops the program), the move-through-village
  door list is kept once per living. One path finder scratch serves every
  search, as Java builds a PathFinder per search. Chunk section entity
  lists grow from 8 (entity_list_room). grave.c sweeps at 96 MB buried
  (256), and vacated or grown list memory is zeroed so stale copies pin
  fewer dead livings.

## 2026-09-26 a warm pool of oracle JVMs, byte-identical to fresh ones (lane/warmoracle)

`make -C java pool-start` starts a long-lived oracle JVM (Pool.java) that
`make script` and `make replay` hand their run to over a local port
(tests/pool.sh); with none free, or a run the pool refuses, they start a fresh
JVM as before (POOL=0 always does). A pool JVM starts like any agent run and,
where a fresh run would launch its world, takes the pristine snapshot instead:
it initializes every class the oracle compiles (BiomeGenBase first, at the
same seeder draw as a fresh run's WorldConf.pruneSpawns) and Rewind.java
records every object under every static field (vanilla and harness classes,
java.util collections and Randoms, atomics, guava, gson, arrays: 70k objects
in 113 ms). Between runs the server stops without a save (as a halted fresh
run never saves), the client world goes, the packet counters, replay reader,
RowHash workers and chunk writer quiesce, the GL textures the run loaded are
deleted, Rewind writes back every changed field (6 to 16 ms), the animated
sprites' frame 0 goes back into the atlases, and PoolMouse warps the X pointer
back and rewrites LWJGL's mouse state (a GUI hover highlight reads the pointer:
smoke-s1's inventory frame lost one on the second pool run without it). What
the rewind finds for itself: the block singletons' spill Randoms, the biome
decorators' tree generators, every static cache and counter, the client's
renderers and GUI counters, key bindings, the harness statics. What it cannot
see was found by hand and handled: the one class initializer that draws from
a Det seeder after a fresh run's reset is GuiScreen's (a RenderItem Random,
at the first JoinScreen), which JoinScreen repeats in a pool; Pool.init
watches every initializer's draws (Det.clinitWatch) and refuses all runs on

## 2026-09-26 replay harness memory (lane/replaymem)

Peak RSS per job, measured with /usr/bin/time on every snapshot
recording and every other suite job, then an LD_PRELOAD live-bytes
profiler on the worst. What held it, and the fix, each with the output
unchanged:

- Livings that left the world were never freed. swamp-night-s2 purges
  mobs every tick (Dev purge) and the spawner refills about 51 squid a
  tick: 153,452 livings of 42 KB, 6.3 GiB. They cannot be freed on
  removal, since other entities keep pointers to a dead one the way
  Java's references do. grave.c buries each living an_tick_one removes
  and each one dev_purge drops (and the old player twin); past 256 MB
  buried, at a row boundary, it scans the program's data, every writable
  anonymous mapping and the stack for a word pointing into a buried
  object, then the kept ones to a fixed point, and clears and frees the
  rest. nbtjson's interned-key cache (keyed by address, checked by
  content) is registered as not a root. Only test_snapshots enables it
  (Linux x86-64). Checked with a build that fills a swept living with
  0xA5 instead of freeing it, sweeping every 20 rows: all 198 logs
  identical.
- The pending-tick set's backward-shift delete decremented used_slots
  once per shifted entry, so the count underflowed and every later add
  doubled the table (gen-walk-s42: 512 MB + 256 MB).
- tape_next never freed the row before (every parsed row stayed:
  130 to 280 MB on the long tapes).
- ie_chunk, an_chunk and fh_chunk zeroed 16 fixed section lists (256 KB)
  per chunk an entity ever entered; only the header is zeroed now
  (test_projectiles proj-2 held a 2 GB table).

Peaks, master's tip (9c10235) against this lane, GiB: swamp-night-s2
6.30 to 0.87, gen-walk-s42 1.22 to 0.46, gold-g9-s42 0.93 to 0.53,
inhabit-s42 0.60 to 0.32 (not the 7 GB seen on the GPU host on 2026-09-25,
which predates lane/replayspeed); the 198 recordings sum 88.2 to 70.9.
test_projectiles proj-2 3.19 to 1.87 and proj-42 2.00 to 1.18. What
remains in sblocks, portals and projectiles (1.66 to 1.87) is terrain:
struct chunk is 330 KB, with metadata and both light arrays a byte per
block. memslot.sh pools follow the measurement: spawning and servertick
now run free. `make -s -C native test TESTJ=16` on the tree merged with
master: rc 0, no FAILED job, 198 OK and 742 PASS lines, the log
identical to master's tip but elapsed times (88.8 s against 81.2 s back
to back at load 30 to 35; swamp-night-s2's 24 sweeps cost about what its
7 GB of page faults did). index/check.py: 1721 ok, 0 with errors.

## 2026-09-26 item stack tags everywhere Java carries them (lane/itemtags)

Every native stack now carries ItemStack.stackTagCompound as one int: an
index into native/src/itemtag.c's store of interned compounds (canonical
NBT text in a fixed arena, a hash index, and the keys the game reads
decoded per entry: ench, StoredEnchantments, display color and Name,
RepairCost, Unbreakable). Equal compounds share an index, so
areItemStackTagsEqual and areItemStacksEqual are int compares; writes
(addEnchantment, the book's StoredEnchantments, the leather dye and
removeColor, setStackDisplayName) intern a new entry and never mutate one,
so a copy is an assignment. Chosen over a per-stack tree for the GPU
contract: flat arrays, no per-stack allocation; the store never frees and
stops the process when full (16,384 tags, 4 MB of text), far above what a
survival session reaches. surv_stack lost its ench/display/name fields,
craft_stack its nbt tree, te_stack/loot_stack/trade_stack their text,
equip_slot its enchant array, and ie_ent, spill_item, dig_ent, fh_ent
(item frames), fh_drop, the S3F trade list and the tile windows'
sent-slot mirror gained the tag. The tag now travels through the
inventory (storePartialItemStack's tag test and fresh-slot copy),
container seeding and copy-back both ways (player, chest, ender, furnace,
merchant, cursor), the open-window S2Fs, S30, trades (the enchanted
priest tools and books), mob equipment (enchantEquipment, drops, the
pickup swap and its hasTagCompound clause), item entities (combineItems'
tag test, the Item NBT, adoption from spills, frames, chunk reloads and
snapshots), chest spills, Q drops, pickups, frames, and every snapshot
and checkpoint loader; a use that returns another item clears the tag.
Also fixed on the way, each needed by the recording: the client's
block-break tool damage rolls Unbreaking on the client player's Random;
SlotMerchantResult's onCrafting counts stat.craftItem; the mine stat
keyed on the dig's tick counter instead of the harvested block; the
replay seeded the Collections.shuffle Random from det.nbt's state as if
it were a seed, and a dev summon dropped the pointer to it (any shuffled
villager offer list diverged or crashed); and lane/suitestart's
build-at-first-load ran the seed world's build inside a tick and left
randomtick's Det and World.rand pointing at the build's dead locals, so
a lava spring's fizz in chunks populated right after drew Math.random
into nothing. test_snapshots now also compares every container's Items

## 2026-09-25 per-recording startup made cheap (lane/suitestart)

The suite was bound by fixed work each recording repeats before its
first row. What went, with every output unchanged:

- Snapshot load no longer generates terrain it then overwrites
  (world_insert_chunk: generation's bookkeeping, the chunkstate's biome
  array). The provider state a skipped generation would leave is kept
  exact: the overworld's (the biome objects' topBlock) by replaying the
  skipped generations before the next real one (pay_owed, only while
  gen.owed says chunkgen_init has not run since), the Nether's and End's
  (hellRNG, endRNG) by generating the last chunk (world_owed_last). The
  same insert path serves test_activate's and test_dig's start chunks
  and test_populate's overworld raw chunks.
- Each chunks.bin.gz record is read straight into the chunk load_world
  inserts; the snapshot's bytes pointer borrows the chunk (no second copy:
  pick-shapes-s1 111.8K page faults to 73.8K).
- gunzip.c: an inflater that copies matches a word at a time (zlib 1.3's
  inflate_fast copies overlapping matches a byte at a time, and these
  streams are 80:1 runs of zero bytes), whole-file and streaming
  (gunzip_open/read/gets/close, zlib as the fallback), the trailer CRC by
  PCLMULQDQ folding. Identical to zlib's gzread on all 1474 .gz files
  under out/java (111 GB inflated, random read sizes), 3.4x less time.
  Used for the snapshot chunk and tick files, the probe tests'
  final.bin.gz and start.bin.gz, populate's raw.bin.gz and the mob tests.
- The chunk hash check folds zero-byte runs into one multiply by P^k
  (snapshot_fnv; 93.5% of chunk bytes are zero), for the snapshot check
  and probe.h's hash_around. An AVX-512 lane version was fewer
  instructions but more cycles on Zen 5 (vpmullq, gathers) and was
  dropped.
- Pending-tick lines are read without a JSON tree (tick_fields; the same
  structs as json_parse on 31.8M lines). nbt_render writes integers and
  float bits without vsnprintf.
- The whole-server replay builds the seed world at the first chunk load
  instead of the first unload; an unload before it sets the globals the
  build leaves (sr_saved_context). 35 of 180 recordings never load a
  chunk and no longer build it.
- native/Makefile starts RUN_FIRST's jobs (7-14 s each), then RUN_MID's,
  then the snapshot replays longest tape first; logs keep PAIRS order.

## 2026-09-25 the Java oracle records and replays 6 to 8 times faster (lane/oraclespeed)

Replays of night-s1 (13182 ticks) went from 117 to 121 s to 13.7 to 20 s on
The GPU host (the spread is the machine's load, 6 to 47), gold-g5-s42 (6192 ticks)
from 55 to 57 s to 7.2 to 7.9 s; recording night-s1 went from 122 s to 17 to
20 s, gold-g3-s42 from 28 s to 11 s. The row bytes are unchanged. Where the
time went, in order: (1) options.txt pinned maxFps:120, and
Minecraft.runGameLoop's Display.sync held an agent run, which ticks once a
pass, to 115 ticks a second; an agent run now writes maxFps:260 (unlimited;
play keeps 120; frames only render on request and wait for every chunk
rebuild in agent mode, so no frame depends on it). (2) Rows.capture
serialized and SHA-1 hashed every loaded server entity's NBT on the client
thread every tick, about 25 s of CPU in night-s1. RowHash now starts that
work when the server's tick ends: workers and the idle server thread
serialize while the client drains, captures and runs its next tick
(Lockstep waits for serialization before the next permit), the SHA-1 runs
beside the server tick and is reused when an entity's bytes equal its last
row's (94% of them), and a direct NBT writer makes CompressedStreamTools'
bytes (checked against it on the first entity of each class). The row is
held and written at the next capture, before any reply or command, and at
close. (3) Det.Born called System.getenv on every draw. (4) Chunk writes
ran on the server thread; ChunkIO writes them on its own thread and
settles before every chunk load, waitForFinish, command and replay setup.
(5) Tape writes blocked on the disk; they go to a writer thread, a replay's
rows are parsed ahead, and a row whose text equals the tape line skips the
per-leaf diff. What is left is vanilla: in night-s1 about 7 s of server
ticks, 2.4 s of client ticks, 3.6 s of startup (1.1 s client, 2.3 s for the
625 spawn chunks), and a slow first 2000 ticks while the JIT warms; the
tick phase runs about 1200 ticks a second (1500 to 1900 once warm). JVM
flags (GC threads, heap sizing, NUMA, huge pages, G1, compile thresholds)
changed nothing beyond noise. java/src gains two one-line hooks
(AnvilChunkLoader.loadChunk, ThreadedFileIOBase.waitForFinish) and the
queueIO hook becomes one line. Re-recorded in this lane, byte-identical to
master's tapes apart from the header's harness hash: gold-g1-s42,
gold-g2-s42 (gold-chain.sh's steps, lane-local checkpoints), cat-fall-s1,
night-s1, nf-mobs-s42; gold-g3-s42 equals master's harness and differs from
master's tape only by cp.fur, which that tape predates. The forest scene's
frame is identical to master's harness. `make -C java gate`: 5 passed.

## 2026-09-25 the replay harness 5.6x faster (lane/replayspeed)

The per-row d.ents digest was 82% of a snapshot replay (night-s1:
13,180 rows in 32.9 s on the dev host, 2.4M entity NBT trees built, written,
SHA-1 hashed and freed). The digest's values are unchanged; only the
native side moved. sha1.c picks the x86 SHA extensions at run time
(cpuid; the portable rounds stay, checked equal on 200,000 random
messages), 2.76 GB/s against 0.32. nbtbin_long_memo keys a memo slot by
entity id: 92% of entities build the same tree as last row, and a build
now lives in an nbt scratch region that starts at the same address on
zeroed memory, so equal scratch bytes and root mean an equal tree and
the value is reused after a memcmp; otherwise the bytes are written and
SHA-1 resumes from the slot's state at the first changed 64-byte block.
nbtjson.c allocates trees from size-class free lists, interns compound
keys and short string values (String.hashCode taken once), and nbt_put
is a macro that interns a literal key once per call site
(__builtin_constant_p); the binary writer reads the tree directly
(nbtjson_tree.h). The digest skips worlds with empty pass lists. The
snapshot's chunk check reads each chunk's memory in place (struct
chunk's fields are the oracle layout) and runs eight FNV chains side by
side. Two O(n^2) walks per tick went: spawner_track's record lookup
(an id index, same first match) and combat_server_finish's tracker
liveness check (sorted live ids).

Evidence: instructions for night-s1 492.2G to 88.3G, inhabit-s42 451.5G
to 78.7G, gold-g5-s42 190.1G to 42.9G, end-dragon-s1 74.4G to 42.0G.
Wall on a quiet dev host (load 4): night-s1 32.9 s at d171ea0 against
5.8 s for this lane's commits before its last two (which cut another
4.5% of instructions); at load 25, 51.3 s against 6.5 s. All four OK
with 0 field mismatches. `make -s -C native test TESTJ=16` on the tree
merged with master: rc 0, no FAILED job, 176 snapshot recordings OK,
211 s against 238 s for master's tip without this lane (both at load
about 45); after the last master merge rc 0, no FAILED job, 178 OK,
154 s (load about 40). Short recordings are now 59% snapshot_load (terrain generated
per loaded chunk before its bytes are copied in), the next suite cost.

## 2026-09-25 CUDA Nether and End provideChunk (lane/cudanetherend)

`native/cuda/cudim_*.cu` extend the CUDA chunk generator to
ChunkProviderHell.provideChunk (the 5x17x5 density field, the netherrack
and lava-ocean fill, the soul sand, gravel and bedrock pass with the
provider rand, MapGenCavesHell) and ChunkProviderEnd.provideChunk (the
3x33x3 island field, the end stone fill, the literal no-op surface pass),
ported from nether.c and end.c as one pipeline over (seed, dim, cx, cz), so
a batch mixes both dimensions and any seeds. Kernels: k_dim_seeds (both
providers' noise per world seed), k_dim_density (a block per chunk, a
thread per sample, then a thread per cell block of the fill, plus the
Nether's three surface noises), k_dim_surface and k_dim_caves (a thread
per chunk, C's draw order), k_dim_construct (the 128-high raw array into
the chunk and the provider's biome). They reuse the overworld's
octaves_at and noise shuffle (now exported) and its --fmad=false rules;
the Nether's cos height curve is computed on the host with libm, since the
device cos is not glibc's. Each new unit peaks at 105 to 107 MB of cicc
RSS. C change: nether.c's and end.c's density_field are public as
nether_field and end_field for the field check.

`make -C native cuda-dimgen-check` runs `cuda_dimgen` on GPU 3 over the 9
dimension dumps (out/java/dims), the 4 Nether and End seed-world spawn
areas (seeds 2 and 42, built as test_seedworld builds them) and the 17x17
chunks around the End's obsidian platform for each End seed: 3494 unique
chunks (1936 Nether, 1558 End), each compared at field (bits), terrain,
surface, caves (Nether) and the finished chunk from world_generate_chunk
(ids, metas, biome array), 0 differ at batch 1, 37, 1024 and 4096 (staged)
and 4096 (product path), device errors 0. Five negative controls (field,
terrain, surface, caves, construct) are each caught first at their own
stage in every dimension they touch, and the other dimension stays clean.
The overworld check still passes (6848 chunks, 0 differ). Timing on a
shared GPU, not representative: 4151 chunks/s at batch 1024 against 3579
for C on one core; the kernels are not profiled yet.

## 2026-09-25 first CUDA phase: overworld provideChunk on the GPU (lane/l10cudagen)

`native/cuda/` is ChunkProviderGenerate.provideChunk for the overworld as
batched kernels over (seed, cx, cz) requests, ported from the C engine that
is its oracle (the GPU audit's L10). Kernels: k_seeds (chunkgen_init's
noise permutations, layer world seeds, Mesa bands and carver longs, a thread
per world seed), k_layers (the 44-node GenLayer graph with no malloc: each
node gets one fixed area per chunk, the union of what its consumers read,
evaluated bottom up in 17,444 bytes of shared memory, a thread per cell),
k_density (the 825-sample FP64 field, the trilinear fill and the surface
stone noise, a block per chunk), k_surface, k_caves and k_ravines (a thread
per chunk, one sequential Random each, C's order), k_construct. Built with
--fmad=false, IEEE division and square root, -ftz=false. `make -C native
cuda-chunkgen` builds it (out of `all` and `test`); `make -C native
cuda-chunkgen-check` runs `cuda_chunkgen` on GPU 3 over every chunk dump and
every overworld seed-world spawn area, comparing each stage with the C
function that computes it.

The first attempt was one 1,895-line .cu and cicc reached 8.8 GB on it (OOM,
twice). Split into six units (host, seeds, layers, density, surface, carve)
compiled one at a time with -rdc=true, and the heavy functions out of line
(`__noinline__`, `#pragma unroll 1` in noise_init): each unit now peaks at
94 to 115 MB of cicc RSS and compiles in under a second.

Result: 6848 unique chunks (3938 from the 23 chunk dumps, 4443 from the 8
overworld seed-world spawn areas, 8 seeds), 0 differ at every stage (sin
table, 10x10 and 16x16 biomes, field bits, terrain, surface ids and metas,
caves, ravines, final ids, metas and biome array), device errors 0, at batch

## 2026-09-25 exact memo for the light re-check retries (lane/l5lightmemo)

The GPU audit's L5. Chunk.func_150809_p is retried every tick on chunks one
ring inside the loaded edge; nearly every retry fails at the unloaded edge
and writes nothing, and it was 54 to 81% of the tick. `native/src/world.c`
now skips a retry exactly when nothing it reads has changed since the last
attempt that failed and wrote nothing. A failed no-write attempt reads only
the loaded mask of the 5x5 chunks around it, the chunk's own ids, heights,
sections and light, and the edge column of each of the four neighbours that
faces it (every light pass it runs finds computed == stored, queues nothing
and writes nothing, so the 32,768-entry light queue is never touched).
Every block and light write stamps its chunk with a new world epoch
(`struct world.epoch`, `struct chunk.stamp`), plus the stamp of the edge it
lies on (`edge_stamp[4]`; a write that makes a section, and an insertion,
stamps every edge). Metadata writes do not stamp: no light path reads
metadata, and leaf decay's metadata writes were most of the misses in a
first 5x5-wide version (S6 only fell to 42-71%). enqueueRelightChecks has no
memo: its cursor never repeats a step, and it is inside the audit's 1 to 2%
chunk_load column. `make -C native lightmemo-check` builds test_snapshots
with NETHERITE_LIGHT_MEMO_CHECK, which re-runs every skipped retry in full
and compares the sky and block light bytes of its 5x5 before and after:
play-reload2-s1 49,035, mobspawn-final-s1 73,642, combat-mobs-s1 74,799,
persist-village-s42 870 skipped retries re-run, all identical, every row
exact. S6 (the audit's chunk_flags column, its hook and table.py): play-reload2-s1
57 to 8%, mobspawn-final-s1 53 to 4%, combat-mobs-s1 73 to 7%,
persist-village-s42 81 to 21% (1.19 ms of its S6 is the first tick's first
attempt on 30 edge chunks, which has nothing earlier to reuse; ticks 2 to 30
are at 3.3%). Steady ms/tick 1.54/1.14/1.71/0.84 to 0.60/0.47/0.41/0.22.
Suite on the merged tree: `make -s -C native test TESTJ=16` rc 0, no FAILED
job, 138 snapshot replays OK.

## 2026-09-25 seed ticks and the tiletick clock on one seed save (lane/auditfixa merge)

Merging master brought lane/tickclock's per-chunk unload clock
(worlds.nbt w0.unloadClock) into the same seed-save loop in
sr_ensure_saved that this lane's seedticks.jsonl.gz replaced. Resolution
from java/src: readChunkFromNBT hands every TileTicks entry to
WorldServer.func_147446_b, which schedules it at t + getWorldTotalTime(),
so the region file's t at snapshot time is exactly what the next load
merges. writeChunkToNBT wrote that t as scheduledTime minus the clock of
whichever save was last (getPendingBlockUpdates(chunk, false) leaves the
entries live, so a chunk loaded and unloaded again after the join has a
newer save). seedticks carries the region state itself, so a v3
snapshot takes each chunk's entries verbatim; a snapshot without it
(every older recording, including death-drown-s1 and death-lava-s1)
re-derives the join unload save from the seedworld with the clock that
unload ran at (unloadClock tick - 1, or 1 when unrecorded). One source
per chunk, never a mix; master's early return in sr_chunk_unload_cb
stays and applies to both. After the merge death-drown-s1,
death-lava-s1, auditfixa-night-s1, auditfixa-rain-s1,
auditfixa-easy-fight-s1, surv_drown-s1, play-reload2-s1, gen-walk-s42 and
cp-mobs-s1 print OK, and make -s -C native test TESTJ=16 exits 0 with
no FAILED job.

## 2026-09-25 the tiletick clock: the join's unload saves restore at their own clock (lane/tickclock)

death-drown-s1 and death-lava-s1 now replay whole-server with 0 field
mismatches; surv_drown-s1, play-reload2-s1, gen-walk-s42, cp-mobs-s1 and
all of master's shared recordings stay at 0.

Root cause: a v2 snapshot's world is built at replay time from the seed
world for every chunk the join unloaded, and the whole-server replay
restores a chunk's pending ticks from the seed save as
delay + total-at-restore, where delay is what the chunk's unload save
wrote. AnvilChunkLoader.writeChunkToNBT writes each entry's delay as
scheduledTime - getTotalWorldTime() at the moment ChunkProviderServer
.unloadQueuedChunks ran — tick 2's first 100-chunk batch saves with the
clock still at 1 (the drain runs before WorldInfo.incrementTotalWorldTime),
tick 3's rest with 2. The native's seed save used clock 1 for every
chunk, so every tick-3-batch chunk's entries reloaded one tick late: 152
unloaded chunks split 71 clock-1 / 66 clock-2 in the death-drown census
(out/census_c.json, per-chunk C = snapshot_sched - saved_delay over the
region file's TileTicks; larger C values are recycled (x,y,z,block) keys
whose entry was ticked and re-scheduled after the save, and 14 chunks
have no snapshot twin because every entry fired between save and
snapshot). Chunk (18,10)'s 292 entries all delayed 0 at a snapshot sched
of 2 were the first visible divergence.

The unload set's drain order is the JDK 8 ConcurrentHashMap's, which the
native's chunkset reimplements, but the batch split still depends on the
run's own mark history, so the fix records it instead of deriving it:
UnloadClock.onUnload (one hook line in ChunkProviderServer
.unloadQueuedChunks, always on) keeps chunk -> tickCounter in a TreeMap,
and Snapshot.worldsState dumps it as worlds.nbt w0.unloadClock
("ia:cx,cz,tick,..."). serverreplay_load parses it and sr_ensure_saved's
seed save uses each chunk's own clock (tick - 1); snapshots without the
record keep the old clock-1 behavior. Both death recordings were
re-recorded with the new oracle.

Two smaller fixes on the way:

- sr_chunk_unload_cb returned early when the world does not hold the
  chunk: the join replay's unload steps (the login's radius-10 marks,
  ticks 2-3) hit chunks the snapshot world never loads, and the callback
  read the live pending set, found nothing and replaced the saved
  entries with an empty set.
- A dead player's air refills to 300 (EntityLivingBase.onEntityUpdate's
  else branch: isEntityAlive() is false, so the drowning branch is
  skipped). Found by dumping the per-entity NBT hashes at the death row:
  the native's player NBT kept Air 0 while the oracle's showed 300, and
  the 19-row divergence window (death to respawn) closed at the respawn.

## 2026-09-25 entity persistence across chunk unload/reload (lane/persist2)

lane/persist2: villagers, an iron golem, paintings, item frames and the
player now survive whole-server replay across a chunk unload and reload,
gated by three new scenarios.

The oracle gates: persist-village-s42 (two villagers and an iron golem
summoned into 2x2 pits at the seed-42 village site, teleported away and
back), persist-hanging-s1 (a painting and an item frame placed by the new
dev hanging op on a built platform at (400,101,-303.5), four site
round-trips), persist-walkback-s1 (a fresh seed-1 world, sprint-jumped
out and back twice over real terrain, a purge and a MobFree before the
snapshot). All three: the java oracle replay OK and the native snapshot
replay OK with zero field mismatches; the full suite make -s -C native
test TESTJ=16 has zero FAILED jobs.

The new dev op "hanging" places an EntityPainting or an EntityItemFrame
through its constructor (kind, the tile x/y/z, dir, art or item/meta/
rot), and "summon" maps the IronGolem alias to the EntityList name
VillagerGolem (mirrored in native dev.c).

Root causes hit on the way, all worked around by scenario design except
the first:

1. The snapshot's NBT restore loses the active AI path and
   hurtResistantTime, and a moving entity (a falling block, a bouncing
   item) hits a 1-ulp box-restore difference: Java's live box is the
   accumulated one while the restore recomputes it from Pos. Every
   snapshot entity must stand still, unhurt and at rest. Enforced with
   pits, purge and delayed snapshots.
2. A 1x1 pit suffocates a 1.4-wide golem; golem pits are 2x2.
3. A dev tp into unloaded territory leaves addedToChunk=false; tps stay
   between loaded, never-unloaded areas.
4. The hanging tape's "vanish" was the player dying: the away tp at
   y=90 dropped it 20 blocks (fall damage); dead players leave
   loadedEntityList. Away tp destinations sit at ground level (y=70 on
   seed 1).
5. The chunk-boundary client-chunk gap: the v2 replay model re-sends
   chunks from the PlayerManager's (int)pos>>4 chunk, but a player
   standing on a chunk boundary (pos z=-304.5, feet block z=-305) has
   its feet chunk outside the first sent ring, so the restored (empty)
   client world drops the player through the void for a tick and the
   server og digest diverges. Tp destinations avoid .5-negative
   boundaries (z=-303.5 style).

Also learned: the vanilla falling-block NBT restore does NOT re-run the
full constructor (the plain World ctor only sets the hurt fields), so a
restored falling block keeps Entity's default 0.6x1.8 box and yOffset 0
in Java too; adding the constructor fields to the native NBT restore
broke play-reload2-s1 and was reverted. Worldgen animals keep wandering
forever, so a walkback snapshot needs a MobFree plus purge first; the
purge alone leaves the hostiles that spawn afterwards.

Native changes: snapshot_entities.c restores the villager trade list
inline from the Offers tag (trades_from_nbt dropped), serverreplay.c/h
export sr_constructor_begin/end and sr_order_push for the hanging

   now does the same on sv.erand. Visible only in rows after the death row.

3. The player rand forked on every poison damage tick. The player's
   java.util.Random exists twice natively: the living twin's l->rand and the
   survival sv->erand. surv_server_potion_tick copies sv->erand into
   l->rand, the potion-particle bool draw advances l->rand, then the poison
   damage goes through external_attack (sr_player_attack) into
   surv_server_damage_by, which draws setBeenAttacked's double and the two
   hurt-sound floats on sv->erand - from the pre-bool state, and the result
   is discarded when surv_server_potion_tick copies l->rand back. Each of
   the nine poison damage ticks lost three draws (27 LCG steps), drifting
   sv.erand until the death-drop motions diverged at row 265. sr_player_attack
   now syncs sv->erand = l->rand before surv_server_damage_by and
   l->rand = sv->erand after, so the twin's and survival's copies stay one
   stream whatever the caller advanced.

  0.2F/0.8F exhaustion even while dead. Found by diffing the player NBT
  (foodExhaustionLevel off by exactly 0.2) at the creeper fight's death row.

  (right after the block write) and fish B from dropBlockAsItemWithChance in

  survival.c's surv_dig_adopt constructs the living through a fake det that
  maps DET_OTHER onto the real SERVER math stream so living_init's three
  EntityLivingBase ctor math draws advance the real math stream, then
  overwrites the identity from the record and replays
  spawnExplosionParticle's draws (20 x 3 gaussian + 3 float on the fish's own
  Random; both spawn sites call it). The fish record's rand_state carries the

Tooling notes: d.smath is the raw Random seed of the SERVER math stream
(Det.mathState), so a divergence there can be traced by env-gating
Det.mathRandom and grepping for the previous row's seed hex to find the exact
draw window. The silverfish row-129 d.smath divergence was
EntityLivingBase.<init>'s three mathRandom calls (field_70770_ap,
field_70769_ao, rotationYaw) that native living_init draws on DET_OTHER

sets (oracle: a Rows.onTickEntries hook; native: the tick_updates pop

(286, 20, 158) block 13: sched 122 in the oracle, 123 in the native).
Those entries are created on the chunk-load path, not func_147454_a:
the oracle schedules them in WorldServer.func_147446_b (AnvilChunkLoader's
TileTicks read at reload; confirmed with a site-distinguished schedule
dump), the native in ticks_load_chunk_entry via sr_restore_chunk_ticks.
