## 2026-09-25 particles: the alpha-cut regression on the dragon's death frames (lane/particles)

The merge queue's trial failed two render scenes that never touched particles:
`mobs2b_dragon_death_f006` (3164 px over its 3145) and `mobs2b_dragon_death_f041`
(24581 over 24509). The cause was the lane's own `alpha_cut` change in
`raster_entities.c`: `entity_alpha_cut = t->alpha_cut ? t->alpha_cut : 25`
gave every entity pass a default ref of 25/255 (0.098039...) where master's
code fell through to `alpha_ref`, and the dragon's death passes set
`alpha_ref = deathTicks/200` (3/200 at f006, 38/200 at f041), so the exploding
texture's discard threshold changed on exactly those two frames. The fix keeps
the fallthrough: `alpha_cut` only applies when the pass sets it, and the
particle passes now carry their own default (`t.alpha_cut = 25`, the
GREATER 0.1 that drawBlockDamageTexture re-enables, matching the old
behaviour; layers 0-2 override with `alpha_cut = 1` for the 1/255 ref).
Both frames measure their old budget values exactly (0.494577/3145 px and
3.586122/2.303147/2.028506/24509 px); the seven other mobs2b views and the
four particle scenes are unchanged and pass. The full suite
(`make -s -C native test TESTJ=16`) is green.

## 2026-09-25 player potion effects in the whole-server replay (lane/potions)

The player's potion effects are now exact in the whole-server loop, covered
by three new recordings that replay byte-exact:
`out/java/pot-snapshots/pot-poison-s1` (a cave spider's bite applies poison,
then spider eye and rotten flesh are eaten, 397 rows),
`pot-witch-s1` (a night witch throwing splash potions and drinking when
hurt, the witch never lands a hit, 561 rows) and `pot-apple-s1` (dev-given
golden apples, normal and enchanted, eaten while hurt, 202 rows); each gates
clean through `out/native/test_snapshots out/java/pot-snapshots/<name>` and
the full suite (`make -s -C native test TESTJ=16`, 45 gates "0 failures",
no FAILED jobs).

The server side lives on the player's living twin (`sr->player_living`):
`living_add_potion_effect` runs the vanilla combine/new-effect hooks, and
its `on_potion_event` callback writes the S1D/S1E onto the player's s2c
queue at the potion call's point in the tick, ahead of the tracker pass
(`sr_potion_event`, native/src/serverreplay.c). `surv_server_potion_tick`
runs where EntityLivingBase.updatePotionEffects sits in onEntityUpdate:
PotionEffect.onUpdate's performEffect (regeneration heals, poison and
wither damage through living_attack_entity_from, hunger exhaustion) plus the
duration decrement, in the twin's map bucket order, with the twin's rand
synced to the player's sv.erand. Food effects ride `surv_server_eat_tick`
after the burp draw (`sr_pot_food_effect`): ItemFood.onFoodEaten's
potionId/duration/amplifier/probability draw from surv.world_rand, and
ItemAppleGold.onFoodEaten's absorption plus, for the enchanted apple, regen
600 amp4, resistance 6000 and fireRes 6000 (no meta-0 super draw for meta
1). After the food's effect lands, sv.health/absorption sync back from the
twin so the next potion tick cannot overwrite the twin's absorption from a
stale sv value.

The client mirror (native/src/survival.c): the S1D pump puts the effect
into the client's map, sets potions_need_update and marks it fresh; the
client potion loop runs PotionEffect.onUpdate's decrement and perform
(hunger exhaustion only; EntityClientPlayerMP.heal is an empty override at
java/src/client/entity/EntityClientPlayerMP.java:75, so the client's own
health moves only through the S06's setPlayerSPHealth) and then the
mobSpell particle draw from sv.erand, skipping perform+decrement for the
fresh S1D so the client's decrement stream trails the server's by one row,
which is exactly the lag the tapes show (sp heals t134, cp t135). The
client never removes expired effects (server-only in vanilla) and S1E is a
plain map remove. Snapshots carry the effect map and absorption
(ent_nbt_player writes Potion tag compounds; load_common reads
AbsorptionAmount), so the tapes round-trip from the snapshot's tick 18.

Also in this lane: the suite's test target now scans multiple data dirs per
test (`DATA_snapshots = pot-snapshots snapshots`, the per-pair loop walks
the pair's dir list), so a lane can gate its own recordings without
copying into the shared out/java tree.

## 2026-09-25 mobs3: the Ender Dragon and the End crystal

The native renderer now draws the Ender Dragon and the End crystal. The dragon
is `ModelDragon` in full: the neck chain (five spine cubes whose rotation
points accumulate from the previous cube's angles), the head and its jaw child,
the body, the two wing/leg passes (the second mirrored by `glScalef(-1,1,1)`
with `glCullFace(GL_FRONT)`), and the twelve-cube tail chain, all driven by the
24 `getMovementOffsets` samples the recorder dumps. On top of the model sit
`RenderDragon`'s extra passes: the death sequence's exploding texture under a
`deathTicks/200` alpha threshold with the normal texture drawn afterwards under
`GL_DEPTH_FUNC EQUAL`, the 200-tick explosion's `new Random(432L)` triangle fans
(`SRC_ALPHA, ONE`, per-vertex white-to-magenta), the model's own 50% red hurt
pass plus `RendererLivingEntity`'s 40% one (drawn twice, once per
`inheritRenderPass`), the additive eyes pass at full block light, and
`RenderDragon.doRender`'s healing beam, a nine-pair triangle strip whose texture
scrolls with `ticksExisted`. The End crystal is `ModelEnderCrystal`'s
scale/translate/arbitrary-axis rotation chain around `innerRotation`.

`native/src/raster_mobs.c` grew a 3x4 affine matrix stack that composes exactly
as the GL calls are issued (post-multiplied translate, then rotateZ/Y/X) with
Mesa's float degrees-to-radians rounding, so `ModelRenderer.render`'s and
`ModelDragon.render`'s inline transforms both fall out of it; the box face
emitter was split out of `draw_box` and is shared. `entity_raster_target` gained
`cull_front`, `cull_none`, `depth_equal`, `alpha_ref`, `alpha_test_off`,
`overlay_alpha`, and a per-clip-vertex `color[4]` behind `vertex_color`. The five
existing mob kinds keep the old path byte for byte.

Three transform bugs cost most of the time, each caught by measuring against the
oracle frames: the part chains were built on the outer matrix as well as applied
to it (the model was transformed twice, and the yaw came out mirrored); `xf_scale`
scaled the matrix rows instead of the columns, so `glScalef(-1,-1,1)` behaved
differently as soon as a rotation preceded it; and the mirrored wing pass still
culled back faces where vanilla culls front faces. With those fixed the in-motion
views are clean (pxdiff reports no cluster above its default threshold, mean
error 0.014 and 0.029 per channel).

The recording side: `RenderStateProbe` dumps the dragon's `animTime`, the 24
interpolated movement offsets, `deathTicks` and the healing beam's inputs, plus a
new `crystals` array (an End crystal is not an `EntityLivingBase`), and reads
back the five new textures; `SceneSetup` stages `dragon` and `ender_crystal`
entities and can pose a dragon's `anim`, `deathTicks` and healing crystal.

Five new source recordings in this lane - `mobs2b_dragon` (a dragon flying for
96 ticks off a bedrock platform), `mobs2b_dragon_death` (health 0, the exploding
texture and the explosion), `mobs2b_dragon_hurt` (hurtTime set, the red flash),
`mobs2b_crystal` (two crystals spinning), `mobs2b_beam` (a dragon with a crystal
9 blocks away, the healing beam) - and nine frame views with measured budgets in
`native/tests/render_budget.txt`. Residuals, all named by pxdiff: the death
explosion's rays are the right shape but about 15% off in additive brightness
(content/shading-offset on the rays, the whole of that view's 3.58 mean); the
hurt flash's red is 8% darker than the oracle's and covers about 60% of its
pixels; the two crystal views differ on the base plate and the cubes by a texel
(cutout-sky+/content with coincident cluster boxes).

`out/native/play` draws both kinds as models (`--shot-model dragon` and
`--shot-model ender_crystal`), with the staged pose documented as staged: the

## 2026-09-25 the Nether in the whole-server replay, portal travel both ways

The native replay now carries the player through a lit portal and back, the
way 1.7.10 does. The overworld and the Nether each own a replay state (entity
pools, pass order, spawner, player manager, region store, pending ticks) that
is swapped in before any world tick or player action touches it. The portal
countdown runs at the head of processPlayer's onUpdateEntity, and the
transfer is ServerConfigurationManager's: S07, the Teleporter search (it
generates and populates the Nether from the seed), makePortal, the player
manager swap, S08, the window items. The player is an entry of its world's
loadedEntityList, so the entity digest walks both worlds in worldServers
order. The client swaps to an empty WorldClient on the S07 and waits for the
chunk bulks EntityPlayerMP.onUpdate sends five at a time.

Once live the Nether ticks in full: its own spawn lists and
MapGenNetherBridge's fortress list (pigmen, ghasts, magma cubes, blazes,
wither skeletons, pigman chicken jockeys), the entity pass with the vehicle
updating its rider, unloadAllChunks while no player is in it, and the region
store that reloads its chunks with their entities and pending ticks on the
second visit. Root causes found on the way: the DerivedWorldInfo clock the
Nether's spawner reads is already advanced, Nether chunks carried no random
tick counts, the despawn check treated an empty world as a distant player, a
dead vehicle's rider got two updates, BlockPortal's random tick draws, and
the spawner walk's chunk loads populate before the tick body sets its hooks.

Recordings (staged with dev fill, seed 1 and 42): `nether-trip-s1` (Nether
at 111, 600+ ticks there with spawning on, back at 809, a 200-tick walk,
1020 replayed rows) and `nether-trip2-s42` (Nether at 117, back at 818, a
second entry through the same portal at 1091 and a second return at 1258
through the overworld Teleporter's cached destination, 1301 rows). Both
report 0 native field mismatches and `ORACLE REPLAY OK` in Java.

ready chunk. At the player's place in the entity pass the replay sends one
S26 bulk of up to five chunks that are loaded and ready (Chunk.func_150802_k:
ticked, terrain and light populated). A v2 snapshot's client world is empty
(clientworld.nbt), so the replay rebuilds the join: the radius-10 queue, the
tick-1 bulk over the snapshot's chunk flags, then the drop to the view
distance. serverreplay_sync_client_chunks applies the packets at the next
client tick. play's render world is a window around the player that fills
and clears records from those packets, re-centres as the player walks, and
keeps the section meshes of chunks that stay (raster_live_rebase). Older
snapshots keep the old whole-server client world.

gen-walk-s42 (fresh seed-42 world, quiet join, 2440 ticks of sprint-jumping
north-west then west with a 30-degree weave) walks from (-250, -130) to
(-673, -303): 1015 chunk loads, 391 populations, 935 unloads. North of spawn
is a forest hill the player cannot cross, hence the heading. Walking out of
the spawn area exposed server gaps, all fixed: the spawner ran before the
block-write and World.rand hooks were installed (its chunk loads populate);
a population inside an entity's tick drew a stale World.rand; the active
set's floor(pos/16) square reaches a chunk past the player manager's
(int)pos >> 4 window, and Java loads it; hostile mobs, bats, items and orbs
were dropped when their chunk unloaded (now saved as NBT and rebuilt through
the constructor draws and readFromNBT, in the chunk section's arrival order,
with setRotation's % 360 and the setPosition after readEntityFromNBT that
centres a baby zombie); tile entities stayed in the tick list after their
chunk unloaded; the chest re-read two neighbours every tick (vanilla caches
func_145979_i and reruns it from invalidate on the added-list merge, which
is what loads the neighbour chunk); a double plant's upper half rolled a
drop. The tile entity registry was process-global, so the replay's
world_free of its discarded world freed the snapshot's tile entities (ASan:
heap-use-after-free in tileticks_pass); it is per world now. Four tile
entity recordings passed only because that freed memory was not reused.

Evidence: `out/native/test_snapshots out/java/snapshots/gen-walk-s42`: OK,
0 field mismatches over 2460 rows; the Java oracle replays it OK; the
client's chunk set equals Java's clientworld.nbt at a mid-walk snapshot.
`out/native/play` replaying its inputs ends at the tape's position with the
mesh cache exact against a full re-mesh; bench frame mean 8.4 ms, p95
10.6 ms, max 61 ms (128 threads). `make -s -C native test TESTJ=16` on the
merged tree: rc 0, no FAILED, 91 snapshot recordings OK. Other walk

## 2026-09-25 worldfx: dropped items and orbs, rain and snow, the screen overlays

The native renderer now draws every world effect the fast profile shows and the
oracle's frames carry. New C: `raster_worldfx.c` (EntityRenderer.renderRainSnow
and ItemRenderer.renderOverlays), the item and orb quads in `raster_entities.c`
(shared by the recorded rows and the live client), the pumpkin blur and the
portal swirl in `raster_hud.c`, and `renderstate.c`'s matrix helpers plus
`renderstate_hand_fov` for the renderHand projection the overlays draw with.

Root causes found while matching the goldens, all measured:

- Rain and snow are 64x256 in 1.7.10 (four 64x64 frames stacked, the v
  coordinate scrolling through them). Sampling them as 64x64 cost 35,841 pixels
  over 25; with the recorded size the rain scene is 20 px over 25 and the
  up-view scene is 0.
- World.getSkyColor's rain and thunder dimming was missing on the recorded path
  (the sky was rebuilt from the biome colour and the celestial daylight, which
  is that value with no rain). The recorded `g.sky` now feeds the sky pass
  directly; the no-weather control `worldfx_skyup` is byte-exact.
- A recording's `render_items.jsonl`/`render_orbs.jsonl` rows are written by
  MeshProbe at the end of the frame's tick, and an orb's tint is
  (sin((xpColor+pt)/2), 255, sin((xpColor+pt)/2+4.1887903)*25.5): a colour that
  moves fast, so one tick of drift in the probe's `xpColor` is a large error.
- The entity pass has GL_BLEND disabled: RenderXPOrb sets the colour's alpha to
  128, but the orbs are written opaquely. Drawing them alpha-blended left the
  green channel 1.5x too dark (a consistent ratio across four orbs).
- The first-person overlays draw after renderWorld clears the depth buffer, so
  they cover the whole frame; without that clear they only drew over the sky.

New recordings (each with its own `tape.jsonl`, `state/`, `golden.png`): 
`worldfx_rain_level`, `worldfx_rain_up`, `worldfx_snow_level`, `worldfx_snow_up`
(seed 7 plains at 1020.5,75,-675.5; seed 2 ice plains at -797.5,75,-3197.5),

(a fire block under the player, which is what the client's on-fire flag follows),

sword, bread and 24 sticks at three screen positions), `worldfx_orbs` (five orbs,
values 1..2477), and `worldfx_skyup` (an up-view frame with no weather at all,
byte-exact). Their budget lines and measured pxdiff causes are in

recording's orb state does not describe its frame - a follow-up. The flat items,

`out/native/play` draws all of it live: the weather and the screen overlays are

## 2026-09-25 mobs2b: the rest of the living models, two shared bugs fixed

Nine more kinds render through the shared ModelRenderer path: zombie pigman,
ghast (scale by `attackCounter`/20 and the shooting texture), blaze's twelve
rods, magma cube's squish, villager (0.9375 scale, five profession textures),
iron golem (the `rotateCorpse` body sway), squid (replacing the approximate
squid that lived in `raster_entities.c`), bat (0.35 scale, hanging and flying)
and mooshroom with its three mushrooms. Twelve staged scenes and 24 frame views
under `out/java/render`, all inside `native/tests/render_budget.txt`.

Two bugs in the shared machinery were what made most of the residuals:

- **The mirrored box sampled the wrong texture rows.** `ModelBox`'s mirror
  swaps the x corners and keeps each corner's own texture position; the native
  box reversed the corner order for the winding and left v alone, so every
  mirrored box read the wrong rows. Fixing v inside the face (`raster_mobs.c`
  `draw_box`) took the iron golem from 355/270 px over threshold to 29/14, the
  pigman from 525/491 to 14/3, professions from 359/329 to 11/9 and the villager
  from 71/65 to 3/4. What had looked like "the pigman's held golden sword" was
  this: no ItemRenderer pass is needed to explain any line now.
- **The entity rasterizer culled by winding.** `RendererLivingEntity.doRender`
  disables `GL_CULL_FACE` for the whole model (and `RenderManager` around the
  paintings), so both windings draw. `raster_triangle` dropped a negative-area
  triangle; it now flips it. The bat's feet box and its left wing were the
  visible casualties. Every scene improved or held: bat_close 297 -> 10 px,
  painting 12042 -> 10930 px, zombie 95/65/62 -> 68/41/36. A handful of frames
  with flat or thin geometry moved by a few pixels (the mooshroom's mushroom
  quads, the sheep's inner faces); those lines record the new measurement.

The bat's old frame views put it 17x25 px away, too small to gate its model, so
`mobs2b_bat_close` is the same pose 2.5 blocks from the camera (hanging at t=7,
flying at t=12). Its remaining 329 px are a 1-2 px content outline along the
flying bat's 1-unit-thick, near edge-on wing membranes, where the coverage of
the coplanar front and back faces differs by a pixel from GL. The ghast's 500 px
are rows 200-201: the terrain horizon sits two rows higher in the native, the
same terrain-edge row `terrain_nearest` and `village` carry, and the ghast's own
pixels have none over threshold.

`out/native/play` draws them as models (not wireframes). Squid and bat from
`out/native/play` on `mobspawn-final-s1`; mooshroom, iron golem, magma cube,
pigman and blaze from `out/native/play-dev` with a `--dev-ops` sidecar that
summons them (four names were added to `dev.c`'s summon table: IronGolem,
ZombiePigman, Blaze, MagmaCube; MushroomCow was already there). Villager and
ghast cannot be shown that way yet and both crash the play client: `an->village_collection`
and the ghast's `an->user_data` are only ever set by `tests/test_villagers.c`
and `tests/test_ghasts.c`, so a summoned villager dies in `vc_add_villager_position`
and a ghast in `gh_closest_vulnerable_player`. That is a pre-existing gap in the
play/replay world setup, left as a follow-up.

Final gates: `make -s -C native test TESTJ=16` exits 0 with no FAIL, and
`make -C java gate` passes 5/5 (the render scenes are Java-recorded, not
re-run by the gates).

## 2026-09-25 movement and hazard scenarios: ten staged whole-server recordings

Ten dev-staged seed-1 recordings now cover the special blocks and hazards a
playthrough walks through, each a flat stone platform inside the snapshot's
loaded area (stone floor, air cleared above, mechanic placed): `scen-web-s1`
(fall 6 blocks into a cobweb, walk out; max client fall distance 4.84),
`scen-soulsand-ice-s1` (sprint over soul sand then packed ice then ice, stop
and slide), `scen-ladder-vine-s1` (ladder column to y 93.2 and back, sneak
hold, then a vine column), `scen-fences-s1` (fence, cobblestone wall, closed
gate; the jumps peak at y 131.17, short of the 1.5-block top, then a walk
along the fence top at y 131.5), `scen-slabs-stairs-s1` (stairs, slab path,
upside-down slab), `scen-snow-farmland-s1` (snow layers 1 to 7, then a fall
onto farmland that tramples to dirt for 2 damage), `scen-cactus-s1` (contact
damage down to 19), `scen-water-lava-s1` (flowing-water push, lava for 4
damage, water extinguish), `scen-drown-s1` (air 300 to 249, one drown tick for
2 damage, surface), `scen-suffocate-s1` (sand dropped inside the head, health
20 to 16, dug out). All ten live under `out/java/snapshots/<name>` in this
lane, scripts in `java/tests/scen-*.jsonl`.

The take-over commit's native work was partly wrong. `push_out_of_blocks` drew
`this.rand.nextFloat()` for its push velocity; vanilla `EntityPlayerSP.func_145771_j` uses a
constant `0.1F`, so that draw is now gone. The server player's `handleFalling`
had vanilla's nesting flattened to `if (onGround && fd > 0) ... else if (dy < 0)`,
which accumulates fall distance while grounded; the WIP commit masked it with
an end-of-tick `fall_distance = 0` when grounded in water or a web. Vanilla's
`else if` binds to `onGround` (`Entity.updateFallState`), so the fix is the
nesting itself and the mask is removed. Evidence: without it `scen-web-s1`
diffs at row 106 and `scen-drown-s1` at row 83, both in `d.ents`, where the
server player's `FallDistance` was 0.0147/0.0155 in native. An oracle probe
(the server row's `fallDistance`/`air`/`onGround` printed for one re-record)
showed the oracle at 0.0 while `sp.y` fell from 130.014671 to 130.0 on that
same row. Kept: the water `fire = 0` on entering water in `sp_process_player`
(`Entity.handleWaterMovement` sets it) and the farmland trample before fall
damage in `surv_server_fall` (`BlockFarmland.onFallenUpon` draws one
`World.rand` float and writes dirt).

`make -s -C native test TESTJ=16` exits 0, 388 PASS, 0 FAIL, including all ten.
The take-over commit had also left six half-finished `diag-*` recordings in
`out/java/snapshots` (each with a second Snapshot as its last op, so
`test_snapshots` refused them with "the tape has no rows after the snapshot to
compare"); they are scratch and were removed from the suite's directory.
Follow-ups: the ten scenes are seed 1 only, and the cactus contact fires one
damage tick because the player is blocked before it can press further in.

`--detail` variant (`out/java/snapshots-lane/fresh-play-s1-detail` in
lane/freshs1) showed a naturally spawned skeleton (id 390) placed after the
chicken pack that spawned after it (391 to 394). In a v2 snapshot the replay
orders new entities by id behind the snapshot's own entities, and the boundary
between the two (`initial_ent_count`) never moved when a snapshot entity was
removed. Seed 1's spawn area drops about 20 of its 179 snapshot entities in
the first rows (w.ents 157 at row 2), so new entities sat below the stale
boundary and were appended unsorted. Every
removal now goes through `sr_order_remove`, which moves the boundary and the
player's slot together; Dev purge resets it. Seed 42 had not removed a
snapshot entity before a spawn landed out of id order, so it passed.

The play client now loads v2 snapshots the way test_snapshots does: it accepts
them without onlyPlayers, binds the player by its entity flag instead of
`ents[0]`, reads the quiet-join pin from the tape header, and leaves chunk
generation on unless the manifest pins it off (v1 snapshots still pin it).
`out/native/play` and `native/play/check.sh` now default to fresh-play-s1.
`out/native/play --shot --ticks 200` from it draws 98 entities; with
`--shot-near-mob` a sheep model and the HUD are in frame.

`out/native/test_snapshots out/java/snapshots/fresh-play-s1`: 0 field
mismatches over 300 rows. `make -s -C native test TESTJ=16`: rc 0, no FAILED,
68 snapshot recordings OK.

## 2026-09-25 checkpoints: whole-server replay with live mobs

A script's `{"cmd":"save","name":N}` runs the vanilla Save and Quit path
(MinecraftServer.stopServer) between tick pairs and copies the save to
`out/java/checkpoints/<seed>/<N>/` with a manifest (seed, world, harness,
TotalTime, player dimension and position, dev, parent manifest sha256,
producing tape path and sha256, quiescence) and a Snapshot taken just before
the quit (`pre/`). `make script FROM=dir` starts on a copy of that save with
Det reset from mix(seed, TotalTime). The quiet join pin (server entities other
than players do not tick until the player has joined) is on in every new tape
and recorded in a header `start` block; a tape without one replays as before.
`{"cmd":"run","class":"Roundtrip"}` compares the pre-save Snapshot with the
post-join one: blocks, tiles, player and entity NBT equal, every other
difference counted on a named reset list (rotation-wrap: Entity.setRotation
takes yaw % 360 on load; stale-save: Save and Quit skips an unmodified chunk,
so its older TileTicks come back).

Snapshot now writes every world's chunks and pending ticks tagged by
dimension, the unload queue, the structure maps (structures.json), Det's
worldSeed, and per entity its own Random now, at birth (Det.Born) and its
cached Gaussian. Native builds every snapshot entity from class, NBT, id and
those Randoms (living kinds, items, orbs, falling blocks, paintings, item
frames, arrows) and drops the onlyPlayers restriction for v2 snapshots.

Chunk generation on exposed native gaps, all fixed: a read that reaches an
unloaded chunk now loads it through the provider (saved copy or new chunk,
populate rule, recreateStructures reseeding World.rand), including the path
finder's ChunkCache window and the spawner's reads in Java's order; the
populate rule reads isTerrainPopulated; the saved-chunk store no longer skips
chunks while it drains the seed world; reloaded creatures were pushed twice
inside the entity pass; the seed creatures are not stepped under the quiet
join. Mobs exposed four older bugs: animals watched players at 8 blocks
instead of 6, isAnyLiquid missed the negative-side column, lava counted as
passable for path shortcuts, and mob damage ignored worn armor and Protection
and skipped the enchantmentRand draw.

`fresh-s42` (fresh world, quiet join, 600 ticks walking, two chunks generated
and one populated mid-tape) and `cp-mobs-s1` (seed 1, 1202 ticks played with
mobs then saved, `--from` that checkpoint, 600 ticks among 301 entities) both
report 0 field mismatches over 600 whole-server rows; Java replays OK; the
roundtrip passes. `make -s -C native test TESTJ=16`: no FAIL, 56 of 56
snapshot recordings OK. `make -C java gate`: 5 passed.

Merged with master (combat, right-click, screens, hand, mob models). The
farm-animal watch radius was fixed identically on both sides and merged once.
Master's dev purge now resets the player's place in the entity order. After
the merge, all 63 snapshot recordings pass, the gate passes, and cp-mobs-s1
and fresh-s42 still replay OK in Java.

## 2026-09-24 dev staging and whole-server replay

Agent scripts can queue `dev` commands at the head of a server tick with
`DEV=1`. The oracle records ordered `Dev` setup entries and `dev:true` in the
tape and snapshot manifest. Java replay queues the same entries at the same
tick. Native replay applies them before its first world tick, carries their
block writes into the row digest and next client update, and fails on unknown
post-snapshot setup classes. The product play binary has no `dev_` symbols and
refuses dev snapshots and tapes. `play-dev` accepts a JSONL sidecar and folds
its entries into the tape header.

The first exact paths cover give, slot, clear, same-dimension teleport, player
state, XP, time, weather, two gamerules, setblock including destroy drops,
fill, supported mob summons, and purge. The server player's Random had to be
added to snapshots for CommandGive's drop motion. Native item drops needed the
server player's 1.62 eye height and Java's float rounding. A new S08
acknowledgement and the delayed health and food packet timing made staged
teleports exact; eating particles also consume the server Math stream.

Seed 1 recordings `dev-give-s1` (104 replayed rows), `dev-pen-s1` (400 rows),
and `dev-world-s1` (12 rows) each report 0 native field mismatches and replay
with `ORACLE REPLAY OK` in Java. `make -C java gate` passed 5/5 and

## 2026-09-22 oracle harness: lockstep, determinism, replay gates

Decision (user): rebuild on 1.7.10 from scratch on the GPU host; v1 (1.11.2) frozen.
Reason v1 used 1.11.2 was Malmo; v2 replaces Malmo with its own harness.

Toolchain: MCP 9.08 (from `~/dev/minecraft/legacy-cold/mc-oracle.tar.zst`,
sha256 23acbf23...) in a python2 Docker image decompiles the owned client jar
(md5 e6b7a531..., matches MCP) to 1,370 files; MCP's own recompile is clean.
We skip MCP afterwards: `make oracle` is one javac over vanilla + hooks +
harness, 3.0 s on the GPU host. No Forge: its patches are behavior until proven
otherwise, and 1.7.10 has no supported Mixin.

Found and fixed, in order (each broke run-to-run or play-to-replay identity):

1. Static shared Randoms seeded in class-init order, which races between the
   client and server threads at startup. Now seeded by field name.
2. The blank join screen paused the game (doesGuiPauseGame), so the server
   ran its pause-save at join, queued chunk unloads, and hit vanilla's
   background chunk-writer race. Join screen no longer pauses; chunk IO is
   synchronous in the oracle.
3. Concurrent runs shared one save directory. One game dir per run.
4. Agent frames: GuiAchievement, enchant glint and end-portal scroll read the
   wall clock. `getSystemTime()` is tick time in agent mode.
5. Multi-tick steps applied held keys on the first tick only (the step action
   was consumed). Per-tick copies.
6. Re-rendering the same tick changed pixels. Causes, all render-history
   state in vanilla: dirty chunk renderers discovered 10 per frame;
   renderers repositioned inside sortAndRender after the frame's rebuild;
   renderers compiled this frame kept a stale not-in-frustum flag;
   translucent sort keyed to movement since the last drawn frame; entity
   rendering skipped for the first 2 frames after world load; vignette
   brightness smoothed per frame. Agent mode now syncs all of it to the
   current camera before drawing.
7. Human tape replay diverged in server entity IDs at t=24-31.
   `TileEntityMobSpawnerRenderer` builds the spawner's display entity on first
   render; that consumed client RNG and the JVM-global `Entity.nextEntityID`,
   which shifted the particle seed in `doVoidFogParticles` and then the IDs of
   server-spawned sheep. Fix: per-role entity-ID ranges (server from 0,
   client 1<<24, render 2<<24, other 3<<24) and a RENDER role for everything
   the client thread does while drawing.
8. Transcendental math: 175 `Math.sin/cos/atan2/pow/...` calls (AI, projectiles,
   worldgen) now use `StrictMath` (fdlibm). JDK 8 on x86 intrinsifies them with
   x87 instructions that are not bit-reproducible across machines; fdlibm is
   identical on every JVM and portable to C. `Math.sqrt` is exact and stays.

Gates green at the end of the day (the GPU host): see SPEC.md table. Throughput with
per-tick digests of every server entity: about 115 paired ticks/s in agent
mode without frames (34k ticks in 300 s on a loaded box).

Mac: `oracle/tools/mac_play.sh` runs the client natively on Apple Silicon (v1 Zulu
JDK 8 aarch64 + arm64 LWJGL 2.9.4) and replays the tape on the GPU host: 393-tick
session exact across arm64 and x86 JVMs.

Known open items: no real human session yet; `--detail`
tapes are large; the header records the harness hash but not the client jar
md5; RENDER-role consumption is not digested, by design.

## 2026-09-22 native worldgen through the surface pass; Tier 1 strip

Oracle `chunks` command (`ChunkDump`): replays `provideChunk` one step at a
time on a fresh `ChunkProviderGenerate` and writes every stage per chunk, then
checks the last stage against a real `provideChunk`, so staging cannot drift.
`BiomeTable` writes `native/src/biomes.h` from the live biome objects.

Native C: java.util.Random, the GenLayer stack, improved/octave/simplex/Perlin
noise, the density pass and the surface pass. Exact on 1,415 chunks: four
17x17 grids at 50-chunk stride (seeds 2, 42, -7777, 123456789), seed 1 8x8,
and three step-1 regions of seed 123456789 found with the native layers
(Mesa Bryce and Mesa M, Mega Spruce Taiga, Jungle M). Same on clang (Mac) and
gcc (the GPU host).

Vanilla quirks the port keeps (the first two and the Mesa one showed up as
failures; the rest were ported as read):

- Hills layer: the zoom chain of its second parent is never world-seeded.
- Biome slot 161 holds the 160 object; the stored id is the object's id.
- Surface writes world column (x, z) at `(z*16 + x)*256 + y`, transposed
  against the density pass, and reads the biome and stone-noise arrays
  transposed the same way.
- Mesa spire noise comes from `Random(0)` in a fresh JVM
  (`field_150622_aD` is read before it is first assigned); the clay bands
  come from `Random(world seed)`. Seeding the spire noise from the world seed
  breaks 41 of 121 Bryce chunks.
- The swamp water-and-lily loop never places anything: it stops at y 255
  because it counts null (air) as a hit.
- A mutated biome runs its base object's surface, temperature included.
- Biome height weighting is float; build with `-ffp-contract=off`.

Tier 1 strip (delegated to an Opus 5.5 subagent, reviewed and merged):
Realms, Twitch, the usage snooper, multiplayer and LAN, all menus, demo mode.
83 files deleted, 15 edited, 1,379 to 1,296 sources. The menu escape paths
(game over, disconnect, out of memory) now shut the client down. Merged tree:
`make gate` 5/5 on the GPU host and the five baseline tapes replay exact.
Follow-ups it listed but left alone: dead user-properties and HttpUtil code,
the TCP server stack (handshake, status, ping), and `MinecraftServer.tick`'s
wall-clock-timed player sampling Random, which no digest covers.

## 2026-09-22 caves and ravines: the raw chunk is exact

`provideChunk` without structures now matches on 1,526 chunks (the earlier
1,415 plus 111 around Extreme Hills where caves expose stone tops). Caves
carve in 1,070 of them, ravines in 269. Clang and gcc agree.

- `MathHelper.SIN_TABLE`: libm's `sin` reproduces Java's float table exactly.
  Every entry's double is at least 2,502 ulps from a float rounding midpoint,
  so any sin under 1 ulp of error rounds the same (checked on both hosts).
- Both carvers put the biome object's current `topBlock` back over dirt
  exposed under grass. Hills, mega taiga and Savanna M rewrite that field per
  surface column, so the native surface pass tracks it per object. The
  Extreme Hills regions hold 48 such non-grass re-tops; forcing grass there
  fails the gate.
- Caves and ravines seed their per-chunk Random identically (both reseed
  from the world seed), so their start chunks are correlated in vanilla.
- Java evaluates operands left to right; C does not. Every expression that
  draws twice from one Random is split into statements.
- Apple's make 3.81 compares mtimes at 1 s resolution: an edit and a build in
  the same second leave a stale binary. `make -B` when scripting edits.

Workers are DeepSeek V4.1 Flash through OMP on the GPU host, one git worktree per lane
(`make lane NAME=x`), each with a mechanical "done when" check I rerun before
merging. Inco's fast tier was 3.6x faster per turn (5.2 s vs 18.5 s on the
same lane) until its credit ran out at 02:17 UTC; lanes fell back to
OpenRouter and resume from their files with a restart note.

Merged, each exact against the oracle:

- trace: matched Java/C tracepoints and trace_diff.
- light: raw chunk height map and sky light (1,526 chunks).
- probe, world: setBlock fuzz probe; native world core (chunk map, setBlock,
  the queued light engine) matches 15,000 ops over 6 probes.
- structprobe, mineshaft, temple, village, stronghold: every overworld
  structure start (349 mineshafts, 507 temples, 100 villages, 24 strongholds
  over 8 seeds) as canonical NBT.
- registry: generated block, material, item and tool tables.
- moveprobe: Entity.moveEntity probe (10,000 moves).
- ores: the population feature probe and WorldGenMinable (1,200 cases).

- loot: all eleven chest loot tables and enchanted books (27,500 draws).
- meshprobe: the client's chunk meshes and atlas, the pixel track reference.

Findings worth keeping:

- Enchantment choice depends on Java 8 HashMap bucket order
  (mapEnchantmentData); the loot lane reproduces it in C. Population's
  structure order (structureMap) needs the same.
- StructureStrongholdPieces: the RightTurn weight builds a LeftTurn (RightTurn
  does not override findValidPlacement), and Corridor.func_74992_a tests size
  var9 - 1 and returns var9.
- Oracle.finish uses Runtime.halt, which skips shutdown hooks: anything that
  must reach disk at exit flushes as it goes (Trace does).
- The oracle traces its own spawn-area generation before a script command; a
  chunk dump restarts the trace file so it holds only the dump.
- `xvfb-run -a` races under parallel runs; tests/headless.sh fixes it.
- A client chunk the client has not been sent is an EmptyChunk (all air): a
  client-side probe must wait for the chunks (MeshProbe throws if not).

Shared-file conflicts were the merge cost: native/Makefile now takes sources
and tests by wildcard and runs test_X on out/java/X/ by itself, the oracle has
a generic `run` command (a probe is one new class), and lanes append rows to
the shared feature and structure tables.

11:40: replay2 (a lane on the native tape replay). Two gaps closed and a
third named. (1) The entity digest: `d.ents` is the first eight bytes of
SHA-1 over each entity's binary NBT chained by entity id, in the world's
list order. Native has that writer now (native/src/nbtbin.c, sha1.c,
entity_nbt.c): Minecraft's tag ids, `writeUTF`, and `NBTTagCompound`'s
HashMap order (bucket index ascending, insertion order inside a bucket,
capacity 16 doubled while size > capacity * 0.75), so the native trees must
be built in the order Java's `writeToNBT` sets the keys, which is why
`entity_nbt.c` puts them itself rather than copying a sorted canonical text.
The player's NBT needed the server living tick: health, air, the food stats
with exhaustion from moving, jumping and swimming plus the regeneration
timer and the food/saturation decrement, the unsaved sprint modifier that
still leaves an empty `Modifiers` tag on the movementSpeed attribute,
`EntityPlayerMP.getEyeHeight()`'s 1.62 for the water check, and the wet
extinguish. (2) The chunk-border light: the snapshot recorded each chunk's
`queuedLightChecks` and populated flags and `load_world` never copied them,
so every native chunk ran `enqueueRelightChecks` eight cursor steps per tick
in the active set and native's block light was ahead of the oracle's from
tick 2 in a handful of chunks, growing to 47 by tick 1500. The border tick
(1512 on the rain tape) is only where that first changed a draw: the mood
sound's `rand.nextInt(8)` and from there the world Random and updateLCG
streams. The other half of the border case is `defaultEmptyChunk`: an
active-set chunk the provider never loaded is still ticked by Java, and
native now models its draws (servertick.c `tick_empty_chunk`). Six mob-free
tapes (five re-recorded scripts plus the walk script on seed 42) are exact
row for row, natively and on the oracle, with `d.ents` compared, and the
suite is 465 PASS. Two more things a tape needs, both found here: the entity
pass must model `World.updateEntityWithOptionalForce`'s 32 block chunk guard
and the world tick must run before the row's `processPlayer` (MinecraftServer
ticks the world first); and `WorldServer.tick`'s `super.tick()` call, which
the animals merge had deleted, is restored, since without it `updateWeather`
never runs and a fresh recording cannot match. Named, not fixed: a tape whose
player crosses chunk borders is still not exact (out/java/snapshots-wip/
replay2-rain-s1 is exact to row 2310, replay2-walk2-s1 with 40 crossings parts
at row 151) because `PlayerInstance`'s constructor calls `loadChunk`
explicitly and MobFree's `loadChunkOnProvideRequest = false` only gates the
implicit path; the replay's chunkload engine would have to load and generate
mid-tape to follow it.

## 2026-09-23 the GPU host outage: the flywheel filled 60 GB; memory cap, lane-share

The GPU host hung at 11:50 MT and was power-cycled at 12:41; the journal stops with
no shutdown. From 11:37 the kernel was OOM-killing: 24 test_populate, 19
test_sblocks, 20 test_snapshots and 7 test_seedworld were resident at once
(33 GB), from five lanes each running the whole suite 128-wide. The lanes
predated d66a06f, so their memslot.sh still slotted by data size and let the
world-building checks run free. A second reset at 13:13 came with someone at
the machine (keyboard plugged in, NIC link flapping 12:59-13:08 on the port
that came up after the first reboot); that one was not memory.

Fixes:
- Every lane worker, and the merge queue's suites, run in one systemd user
  slice, nv2.slice: MemoryMax 36G, MemoryHigh 32G, MemorySwapMax 0, set at
  runtime by out/flywheel/bin/slice.sh (systemd forgets it at reboot, so every
  launcher calls it). Over the cap the kernel kills lane processes inside the
  slice; the GPU host and the other projects keep their memory. Checked: a 400 MB
  write under a 200 MB scope cap dies with 137.
- The flywheel scripts moved from /tmp (tmpfs, wiped by the reboot) to
  out/flywheel/bin.
- `make lane-share NAME=x` replaces the SHARED list: it links every area of
  master's out/java but builds and scratch, skips what the lane has, and
  re-runs on a live lane. The activate lane was made before the place
  recordings existed, so its suite skipped test_place without a word and a
  drop regression reached the trial merge.

test_place: sampling its per-case hash (every 64th case and the last, final
world compared, rerun with every case hashed on failure) took it 126 -> 31 s
and the suite 127 -> 37 s. A block planted at case 12345 fails at case 13247
(the next sampled hash near it) and is localized to 12345.

Activate review (15e63a8), three fixes beyond the lane's report:
1. world_remove_tile_entity had been changed to skip World.getTileEntity's
   demand creation, with a comment saying the Java lookup never
   demand-creates. It does (World.java:2701 -> Chunk.func_150806_e). The real
   differences: native removed the tile entity after the abort re-check and
   the metadata store rather than at breakBlock's tail, and test_activate
   loaded the scattered region without the tile entities the scatter's
   setBlock had made (their constructor Randoms were spent before
   det_seeder_start). Both fixed, vanilla lookup restored.
2. The drop_item_stack split returned early outside a tick environment
   instead of taking the placement probe's path (place case 28738: a tall
   grass popped by a redstone ore placement dropped nothing).
3. A lane's own suite passing is not evidence when its out/java lacks areas;
   the trial merge in a full checkout is what caught 2.

Hostiles (DeepSeek) stopped BLOCKED on a probe bug: the loop absorbing
onSpawnWithEgg's children indexes loadedEntityList by position, so a spider
jockey records the spider twice and its skeleton never. Relaunched on Gemini
as the scaffold only (probe fixed by identity, a kinds option, the monster
base plus the zombie); skeleton, creeper and spider fan out after it.

## 2026-09-23 two more the GPU host outages: network/power, not memory

After the memory cap went in, the GPU host still dropped twice more: ~1:13 pm (a
hard reset with someone at the keyboard, the NIC link flapping) and 2:01 pm
(network gone, no clean shutdown in the journal, back at 2:08). Neither was
OOM: the nv2.slice cap (36G, no swap) held both times, and the second boot's
journal shows no OOM or panic before it. Three outages in ~2.5 hours with a
flapping link points at hardware, power, or the cable, not software; it needs
hands at the machine. The cap is runtime-only (systemd forgets it at reboot),
so out/flywheel/bin/slice.sh re-applies it and every launcher calls it.

The six lanes (spawning, pickaxe, ghasts, slimes on omp; hostiles, crossings

## 2026-09-23 lane/slimes: EntitySlime and EntityMagmaCube exact, 4x2,400 ticks

`native/src/slimes.{c,h}` and `native/tests/test_slimes.c` against
`java/mods/netherite/oracle/SlimeProbe.java`: 60 mobs of sizes 1, 2 and 4 over
2,400 ticks, on seeds 2 and 42, overworld slimes and Nether magma cubes, all
four recordings compare clean (spawns, splits, deaths, drops, player hits,
removals, the four Det streams and the final blocks). A second recording of one
is byte-identical.

Four things cost the time, and three of them are shared code, not the slime:

- `Entity.getBoundingBox()` returns null in 1.7.10 and `getCollisionBox` returns
  null, so `World.getCollidingBoundingBoxes`' entity half adds nothing. The
  block-only collision list was already exact; a first cut that added entity
  boxes to `moveEntity` broke tick 0 immediately.
- `World.isBlockNormalCubeDefault` reads `provideChunk`, which answers null when
  `loadChunkOnProvideRequest` is off; `blockcb.c` was generating a chunk there.
  Fixed to honour `w.no_generate`.
- A spawned entity is visible to the same tick's queries only once it is in a
  chunk, so `EntitySlime.setDead`'s children are constructed at their final
  position (the reference registers them with `spawnEntityInWorld` after
  `setLocationAndAngles`, not at the origin).
- The checks need `w.dim` set from the manifest: the Nether run's ring had
  overworld terrain on the native side. The probe also keeps every entity inside
  the loaded region (it aborts otherwise) and its wall now starts at the surface,
  because a size-1 slime is 0.6 high and walks through a wall that begins one
  block up, out to where the oracle's world still holds the populated spawn
  chunks.

spawn a background task, and idle-wait on it for up to 6 hours. Two lanes sat
idle 15 and 82 min this way with nothing running on the GPU host. The remote-lane

idle-wait on a background task. Watch for a Gemini lane whose jsonl stops

## 2026-09-24 spider: the jockey, the web override and the player's damage exhaustion exact over 2,400 ticks

The spider port (native/src/hostiles_spider.{c,h}, HK_SPIDER 13 / HK_CAVE_SPIDER
23) was in place but its recordings failed from tick 0. Nine porting slips, each
found with the trace tool against the oracle:

1. EntityCreature.updateEntityActionState's follow loop: the C computed var5z
   without the (int)(width + 1) * 0.5 Java adds to x and z, and its distance test
   included the point's height difference. Java passes var5.yCoord as the y
   argument of squareDistanceTo, so the y term cancels and the cursor advances on
   x and z only. Both dropped the spider onto a shorter path, off by up to 2
   blocks in z from tick 0.
2. EntityMob.attackEntity's touch needs distance < 2.0F.
3. EntitySpider.attackEntity's leap takes MathHelper.sqrt_double over a double
   sum; the port's float helper rounded the sum to float first (1e-8 drift that
   the dense cluster amplified into a visible divergence).
4. EntitySpider.attackEntityAsMob damages with DamageSource.causeMobDamage, whose
   hungerDamage is 0.3F; the port passed DMG_GENERIC, so the player's food
   exhaustion was short by 0.3 per hit from the first cave-spider hit.
5. EntitySpider.setInWeb is an empty override: Entity.setInWeb (the flag and the
   fall-distance reset) never runs for a spider, so a spider in the probe's web
   patch keeps its speed. entity_set_in_web is now a virtual and the spider
   installs a no-op.
6. The jockey rider must run the whole EntityLiving.onSpawnWithEgg chain for
   itself (the follow-range spawn bonus), not only the skeleton's part.
7. Entity.applyEntityCollision's guard (a rider and its vehicle never push each
   other) was missing, so the rider drifted while its spider walked.
8. EntityLivingBase.isPotionApplicable is the target's rule; the port called the
   *spider's* override for every target, so a cave spider's poison never landed
   on the player (and any poison on a non-spider was silently refused).
9. an_write_state's probe kind for the cave spider, and the probe's spawn record
   gained a construct flag: a spider's jockey rider is recorded as a spawn the
   setup made on its own, and the replay takes the entity the spider built
   instead of spawning a second one.

## 2026-09-24 hud lane: the 2D overlay pass

`native/src/raster_hud.c` draws GuiIngame's overlay and GuiAchievement's toast,
dispatched by one call in `raster_render` after the entity pass. Its inputs are
the render-state dump's new `hud` member: the scaled resolution, both ends of
the toast's animation clock (`getSystemTime` is tick time in agent mode), the
player's HUD numbers, the inventory and armour slots, and the GUI textures the
recorder reads back from GL into `state/gui.json` and `state/gui_*.rgba`
(ascii, widgets, icons, achievement_background, vignette, the stitched items
atlas). A scene without the member draws nothing and stays byte-identical:
all nine scenes in `out/java/render` render the same bytes with and without the
call.

The blend factors come from the GL state the client leaves: the overlay uses
GL_SRC_ALPHA/GL_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA, the crosshair
GL_ONE_MINUS_DST_COLOR/GL_ONE_MINUS_SRC_COLOR (one minus the destination, not
the destination plus one: reading 769 as GL_ONE gave a wrong crosshair), and
the vignette GL_ZERO/GL_ONE_MINUS_SRC_COLOR. The source texel and its
modulation are rounded to eight bits and the blend result is rounded; a font
space advances four pixels like `renderCharAtPos`, not its loaded width.

A scene recorded before the member existed draws nothing, so the pass is only
live where the state was recorded with the extended probe. `terrain_nearest`'s
shared state predates it; the lane's copy of `out/java/render/terrain_nearest`
is therefore a re-recording of that scene from the committed source (`--mip 0
--renderstate <dir>/state`), golden byte-identical to master's
(`d57198893ae99b3585bb648db1d2c3be`), which is what makes the tooltip cluster
go away: pxdiff 18 clusters to 4, the surviving 4 identical entry for entry to
the same scene rendered with the member deleted (the world's fringe). The toast
rectangle `534,0,854,64` goes from 72/20480 pixels exact to 20480/20480. Master's
own copy needs the same re-record once this merges. The same tape with F1 off
(`out/java/render/terrain_hudbar`) confirms the vignette, crosshair, hotbar,
hearts, food and experience bar against a golden; what is left is the
first-person hand (the world pass's business) and a +-1 rounding difference in
4.9% of the vignette's pixels. Deferred: chat, player list, scoreboard, debug
screen, pumpkin/portal/sleep overlays, and the item paths that need item models
(isometric blocks, layers, enchant glint) or the durability bar's HSB colour.

Follow-up on that "+-1 rounding difference": two model fixes in `raster_hud.c` cut
it in half, both found by reproducing the pass's arithmetic in a throwaway numpy
model and sweeping candidate blend rules against the golden (`out/report.md` has
the counts). The bilinear result in `tex_sample` is rounded to eight bits before
the modulation, because the filtered texel leaves the fixed-function texture
stage as eight bits; and `quant` converts with a half-up round instead of
`lrintf`'s round-half-to-even, which is the conversion the same software
rasterizer uses. On the `hide` 0 frame pixels differing by exactly 1 go from
20200 to 13320 and differing pixels from 38821 to 31933, with no region further
from the golden than before and none of it above pxdiff's 25 threshold.

## 2026-09-24 waterdepth: the beach water gap is the recording's mesh radius

`out/report.md` listed "translucent water depth absorption" as a renderer gap on
the beach scene. It is not one. The water path in `raster.c` is exact wherever
the meshed world agrees: on both beach recordings the mean absolute error over
every water pixel within 10 blocks of the camera is [0.34, 0.42, 0.25] and at
10-20 blocks [0.94, 1.51, 1.80], and 1.7.10 has no water depth term to match in
the first place (`RenderBlocks.renderBlockFluids` tints water with
`colorMultiplier` and calls `setColorOpaque_F`, so the transparency is
`water_still.png`'s own per-texel alpha, 168..220).

Every water cluster is instead water composited over world the recording does
not carry. The golden is rendered by the real client at render distance 8 (128
blocks, linear fog 96..128) while `MeshProbe` meshed radius 4 (64 blocks), so the
water between the mesh edge and the fog end blends over an unmeshed seafloor and
a fogged void. Bucketing the beach water pixels by their distance and by whether
a terrain fragment was already in the framebuffer shows it directly: error [1.78,
3.31, 4.37] where terrain is present against [18.7, 18.1, 24.3] where it is not.

`out/java/render/beach6` is the same seed, pose and tick as `beach` with
`MeshProbe radius 6`.
The client will not hand MeshProbe a bigger disc than renderDistance - 2 chunks
(radius 7 and 8 fail with "chunk is not loaded yet" at render distance 8). The water region (y >= 200) then matches at [2.36,
2.22, 0.85] against [5.31, 5.05, 5.48], pixels over 16 levels of error drop from
155953 to 94397, and the shallow water is unchanged at about [0.28, 0.25, 0.30].
The residue is the fogged ring the loader cannot reach plus the inventory HUD
prompt the native does not draw.

Two more gaps this lane named were closed by other lanes while it worked: the
10..128 block water residue is texture minification (lane/cutout's
`raster_texture.c`), and the dark stepped patch in the beach water is the squid
(lane/entities' `raster_entities.c`). Record render scenes at a mesh radius that
covers the render distance from now on.

## 2026-09-24 waterdepth, continued: radius = render distance, and the first entry's cap was wrong

The entry above concluded that the client would not hand MeshProbe a disc bigger
than renderDistance - 2. That is wrong, and the beach water region closes to
[0.37, 0.46, 0.33] mean absolute error once it is. MeshProbe refused any chunk
whose `isEmpty()` was true, and `World.getChunkFromChunkCoords` answers with the
provider's single shared blank `EmptyChunk` for a chunk the client never
received, at the requested call's coordinates but with `xPosition` 0. The chunks
that failed at radius 7 and 8 were the square's corners, which the client's disc
never loads; the straight lines out to 8 chunks were there the whole time.

`MeshProbe` now takes `"allowEmpty": true`: an empty chunk is meshed as nothing
and recorded in `chunks.bin` as the air the client itself renders there
(`manifest.chunks_unloaded` counts them, 81 of the 289 at radius 8). The default
is unchanged and still refuses an unloaded world, byte for byte: re-recording
radius 6 without the flag reproduces `beach6`'s `sha1_meshes`
83bdec214942cb74d70a85c1e36059cc10338438, `sha1_pass0` 41f6304b..., `sha1_pass1`
e4a6c23d... exactly, and radius 8 without the flag still fails with
"chunk (-23,-17) is not loaded yet". `native/` is untouched by this lane.

`out/java/render/beach8` is the same seed, pose, tick and golden frame as
`beach`, meshed radius 8 (128 blocks, so it covers the render distance 8 whose
linear fog runs 96..128). The water region (y >= 200, bluish) mean absolute
error is [6.01, 5.84, 6.68] at radius 4, [2.93, 2.79, 0.95] at radius 6, and
[0.37, 0.46, 0.33] at radius 8; the whole frame outside the HUD box goes from
[3.41, 3.23, 3.50] to [1.48, 1.38, 0.53] to [0.21, 0.25, 0.18], and the
recording's own `native.png` at radius 4 was the only reason the water ever
looked like a shader.

The depth question is settled the same way it was, only harder: with the world
present the error is flat across the golden's own brightness, which is the water
column's depth seen from outside. Bucketing the beach8 water pixels by golden
luminance 50-60 (darkest deep water), 60-70, 70-80, 80-100, 100-128, 128-160,
160-256 (brightest shallow sand through water) gives mean absolute error 0.40,
0.37, 0.32, 0.28, 0.52, 0.57, 0.33. A depth-dependent transparency would show
as a slope across that range; there is none, because
`RenderBlocks.renderBlockFluids` sets alpha 1 and the transparency is
`water_still.png`'s per-texel alpha (168..220). Deep water is dark in the golden
because the seafloor behind it is dark, and the native reproduces that seafloor.

What is left on beach8 is two clusters: the inventory HUD prompt (20408 px,
never drawn natively) and two dark squid patches (98 px, blobs at 287,659 and
320,700 in 8-connected terms). The first entry credited the second to
lane/entities; it is not closed. The scene carries no `squid.rgba` because no
probe dumps entity textures, and copying master's `out/java/render/painting/
squid.rgba` into beach8 makes it worse: the survey goes from 2 clusters to 20
(largest 673 px, in flat water) and the outside-HUD mean absolute error rises to
about 0.6 per channel, so the squid quads land somewhere the golden's do not.
That is the entity pass (model, its one-tick-later `entities.jsonl` snapshot, or
both), not the water.

`make -C native test` exits 0 after merging master.

The recipe for any scene, from `java/`: `make script
SCRIPT=../out/java/render/<scene>/script.jsonl TAPE=../out/java/tapes/<scene>.jsonl
SEED=1 ARGS="--renderstate <abs path>/<scene>/state"`, with the scene's
`script.jsonl` holding the SceneSetup row, the tick beat row with its `frame`
capture, and `{"cmd":"run","class":"MeshProbe","out":"<abs path>/<scene>",
"radius":<renderDistance>,"allowEmpty":true}`. The scene still needs the
environment RGBA dumps (`sun.rgba`, `moon_phases.rgba`, `clouds.rgba`, and the
entity textures the pass reads) alongside; nothing in the tree produces them,
so they are copied from a scene that has them.

## 2026-09-24 bound native test parallelism (TESTJ)

The `make -C native test` target fanned out one background process per scene
slot with `&` then `wait` - unbounded. Once render-scene goldens were added,
that became ~670 concurrent processes on the 128-core box. The tests are
CPU-bound, so oversubscription bought no speed; worse, that many concurrent
slots (some loading large radius-8 worlds) overran the nv2.slice 24G memory
cgroup with swap off, wedging dozens of processes in uninterruptible D-state
reclaim that even SIGKILL could not clear until the cap was lifted. A suite
that ran in ~25s stalled past 5 minutes.

Fixed: the target now writes a job list and runs it through `xargs -P $(TESTJ)`
(default 48), bounding concurrency. Same 522 PASS, 32s wall, and peak slice
memory stays well under the 24G cap. Raise TESTJ on a box with more headroom;
lower it under a tighter cap. Nothing else about the suite changed.

2026-09-24: Whole-server chunk reload now restores saved world-generation creatures in Java's section order, including their pre-snapshot entity tick and fresh load-constructor draws; play-reload-s1 replays all 398 rows and the native suite passes.

## 2026-09-24 the playable C client, and what a played session found

out/native/play (native/play/play.c, SDL3, make -C native play) runs the
whole-server tick pair test_snapshots.c replays, at 20 Hz from
mobspawn-final-s1 (seed 1, mobs on, generation pinned off), with the keyboard
and mouse as each tick's act, and draws every frame with raster_live_frame: the
renderer's live path, renderstate_compute's numbers over the server world's
chunks. Every session is written as an oracle tape marked inputs_only; the Java
oracle replays such a tape without comparing and records its own rows, and
native/play/check.sh runs that on the GPU host and checks the Java rows with
test_snapshots. Native now builds clean under the Mac's clang, and the arm64
build passes every play-relevant recording (97) and renders scenes
byte-identical to the GPU host's.

Frame time, measured with play --bench TAPE on a real 398-tick session: 265 ms
was 252 ms of re-meshing, because each tick changes ~25 sections and every
change re-meshed 26 neighbours on one thread. Now a change re-meshes neighbours
only across the borders its cells touch, chunks compare straight from live
memory with a whole-plane fast path, the stale sections mesh on every thread,
and a frame records its triangles once then rasterizes row bands in parallel:
frame p50 17.7 ms, tick p50 2.9 ms. Every step was checked bit-exact (the
section cache against a full re-mesh, the spawn frame's hash at 1 to 14
threads, the file path's scene bytes). Not yet: a ~0.75 s hitch the first time
a pre-snapshot chunk reloads (sr_ensure_saved builds the seed world lazily;
moving it would make the client's ticks differ from the checker's).

The first played session diverged at tick 210 (w.ents 134 vs 128): crossing a
chunk border brought back spawn-area chunks unloaded before the snapshot, and
Java restored their saved creatures. Fixed on lane reloadents (GPT-6 Sol,
medium, 13 min); the session is out/java/snapshots/play-reload-s1. Also found:
renderstate wrote 0x0901 for GL_LINEAR fog and test_renderstate only compared
fog start/end under that wrong constant, so those never ran; both use 0x2601
now and all 104 frames are exact with the mode compared.

The option set is pinned in java/mods/netherite/oracle/Main.java writeOptions
(the quality profile). Decided direction: pin a performance profile instead
and support only it; render distance is also the integrated server's view
distance, so choosing it re-records the whole-server snapshots.
